Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.IRFactory.TransformDispatcher.transformAsString(AstNode)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/IRFactory.java
Original range: 403-416
Documentation:
/**
     * Transforms the given node and then sets its type to Token.STRING if it
     * was Token.NAME. If its type was already Token.STRING, then quotes it.
     * Used for properties, as the old AST uses String tokens, while the new one
     * uses Name tokens for unquoted strings. For example, in
     * var o = {'a' : 1, b: 2};
     * the string 'a' is quoted, while the name b is turned into a string, but
     * unquoted.
     */
Method code:
403 |     private Node transformAsString(AstNode n) {
404 |       Node ret;
405 |       if (n instanceof Name) {
406 |         ret = transformNameAsString((Name)n);
407 |       } else if (n instanceof NumberLiteral) {
408 |         ret = transformNumberAsString((NumberLiteral)n);
409 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
410 |       } else {
411 |         ret = transform(n);
412 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
413 |       }
414 |       Preconditions.checkState(ret.getType() == Token.STRING);
415 |       return ret;
416 |     }

===== M0012 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal,Node,Node,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 781-819
Documentation:
/**
     * Updates our respresentation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name's longest prefix before the "prototype" property if the
     * name includes the "prototype" property. Does nothing otherwise.
     *
     * @param t The current node traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     * @return Whether the name was handled
     */
Method code:
781 |     boolean maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent,
782 |         String name) {
783 |       // We use a string-based approach instead of inspecting the parse tree
784 |       // to avoid complexities with object literals, possibly nested, beneath
785 |       // assignments.
786 | 
787 |       int numLevelsToRemove;
788 |       String prefix;
789 |       if (name.endsWith(".prototype")) {
790 |         numLevelsToRemove = 1;
791 |         prefix = name.substring(0, name.length() - 10);
792 |       } else {
793 |         int i = name.indexOf(".prototype.");
794 |         if (i == -1) {
795 |           return false;
796 |         }
797 |         prefix = name.substring(0, i);
798 |         numLevelsToRemove = 2;
799 |         i = name.indexOf('.', i + 11);
800 |         while (i >= 0) {
801 |           numLevelsToRemove++;
802 |           i = name.indexOf('.', i + 1);
803 |         }
804 |       }
805 | 
806 |       if (parent != null && NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
807 |         // Object literal keys have no prefix that's referenced directly per
808 |         // key, so we're done.
809 |         return true;
810 |       }
811 | 
812 |       for (int i = 0; i < numLevelsToRemove; i++) {
813 |         parent = n;
814 |         n = n.getFirstChild();
815 |       }
816 | 
817 |       handleGet(t, n, parent, prefix, Ref.Type.PROTOTYPE_GET);
818 |       return true;
819 |     }

/**
     * If any of the variables are well-defined and alias other variables,
     * mark them as aliasing candidates.
     */
Method code:
169 |     private void collectAliasCandidates(NodeTraversal t,
170 |         ReferenceMap referenceMap) {
171 |       if (mode != Mode.CONSTANTS_ONLY) {
172 |         for (Iterator<Var> it = t.getScope().getVars(); it.hasNext();) {
173 |           Var v = it.next();
174 |           ReferenceCollection referenceInfo = referenceMap.getReferences(v);
175 | 
176 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): Don't handle variables that are never used.
177 |           // The tests are much easier to write if you don't, and there's
178 |           // another pass that handles unused variables much more elegantly.
179 |           if (referenceInfo != null && referenceInfo.references.size() >= 2 &&
180 |               referenceInfo.isWellDefined() &&

183 |             Node value = init.getAssignedValue();

185 |               aliasCandidates.put(value, new AliasCandidate(v, referenceInfo));
186 |             }

===== M0031 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeCheck.visitFunction(NodeTraversal,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeCheck.java
Original range: 1473-1535
Documentation:
/**
   * Visits a {@link Token#FUNCTION} node.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal object that supplies context, such as the
   * scope chain to use in name lookups as well as error reporting.
   * @param n The node being visited.
   */
Method code:
1473 |   private void visitFunction(NodeTraversal t, Node n) {
1474 |     FunctionType functionType = (FunctionType) n.getJSType();
1475 |     String functionPrivateName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
1476 |     if (functionType.isConstructor()) {
1477 |       FunctionType baseConstructor = functionType.
1478 |           getPrototype().getImplicitPrototype().getConstructor();
1479 |       if (baseConstructor != null &&
1480 |           baseConstructor != getNativeType(OBJECT_FUNCTION_TYPE) &&
1481 |           (baseConstructor.isInterface() && functionType.isConstructor())) {
1482 |         compiler.report(
1483 |             t.makeError(n, CONFLICTING_EXTENDED_TYPE, functionPrivateName));
1484 |       } else {
1485 |         // All interfaces are properly implemented by a class
1486 |         for (JSType baseInterface : functionType.getImplementedInterfaces()) {
1487 |           boolean badImplementedType = false;
1488 |           ObjectType baseInterfaceObj = ObjectType.cast(baseInterface);
1489 |           if (baseInterfaceObj != null) {
1490 |             FunctionType interfaceConstructor =
1491 |               baseInterfaceObj.getConstructor();
1492 |             if (interfaceConstructor != null &&
1493 |                 !interfaceConstructor.isInterface()) {
1494 |               badImplementedType = true;
1495 |             }
1496 |           } else {
1497 |             badImplementedType = true;
1498 |           }
1499 |           if (badImplementedType) {
1500 |             report(t, n, BAD_IMPLEMENTED_TYPE, functionPrivateName);
1501 |           }
1502 |         }
1503 |         // check properties
1504 |         validator.expectAllInterfaceProperties(t, n, functionType);
1505 |       }
1506 |     } else if (functionType.isInterface()) {
1507 |       // Interface must extend only interfaces
1508 |       for (ObjectType extInterface : functionType.getExtendedInterfaces()) {
1509 |         if (extInterface.getConstructor() != null
1510 |             && !extInterface.getConstructor().isInterface()) {
1511 |           compiler.report(
1512 |               t.makeError(n, CONFLICTING_EXTENDED_TYPE, functionPrivateName));
1513 |         }
1514 |       }
1515 |       // Interface cannot implement any interfaces
1516 |       if (functionType.hasImplementedInterfaces()) {
1517 |         compiler.report(t.makeError(n,
1518 |             CONFLICTING_IMPLEMENTED_TYPE, functionPrivateName));
1519 |       }
1520 |       // Check whether the extended interfaces have any conflicts
1521 |       if (functionType.getExtendedInterfacesCount() > 1) {
1522 |         // Only check when extending more than one interfaces
1523 |         HashMap<String, ObjectType> properties
1524 |             = new HashMap<String, ObjectType>();
1525 |         HashMap<String, ObjectType> currentProperties
1526 |             = new HashMap<String, ObjectType>();
1527 |         for (ObjectType interfaceType : functionType.getExtendedInterfaces()) {
1528 |           currentProperties.clear();
1529 |           checkInterfaceConflictProperties(t, n, functionPrivateName,
1530 |               properties, currentProperties, interfaceType);
1531 |           properties.putAll(currentProperties);
1532 |         }
1533 |       }
1534 |     }
1535 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VariableReferenceCheck.ReferenceCheckingBehavior.checkVar(NodeTraversal,Var,List<Reference>)

Documentation:
/**
     * If the variable is declared more than once in a basic block, generate a
     * warning. Also check if a variable is used in a given scope before it is
     * declared, which suggest a likely error. Relies on the fact that
     * references is in parse-tree order.
     */
Method code:
106 |     private void checkVar(NodeTraversal t, Var v, List<Reference> references) {
107 |       blocksWithDeclarations.clear();
108 |       boolean isDeclaredInScope = false;
109 |       boolean isUnhoistedNamedFunction = false;
110 |       Reference hoistedFn = null;
111 | 
112 |       // Look for hoisted functions.
113 |       for (Reference reference : references) {
114 |         if (reference.isHoistedFunction()) {
115 |           blocksWithDeclarations.add(reference.getBasicBlock());
116 |           isDeclaredInScope = true;
117 |           hoistedFn = reference;
118 |           break;
119 |         } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(
120 |             reference.getNode().getParent())) {
121 |           isUnhoistedNamedFunction = true;
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 | 
125 |       for (Reference reference : references) {
126 |         if (reference == hoistedFn) {
127 |           continue;
128 |         }
129 | 
130 |         BasicBlock basicBlock = reference.getBasicBlock();
131 |         boolean isDeclaration = reference.isDeclaration();
132 | 
133 |         boolean allowDupe =
134 |             SyntacticScopeCreator.hasDuplicateDeclarationSuppression(
135 |                 reference.getNode(), v);
136 |         if (isDeclaration && !allowDupe) {
137 |           // Look through all the declarations we've found so far, and
138 |           // check if any of them are before this block.
139 |           for (BasicBlock declaredBlock : blocksWithDeclarations) {
140 |             if (declaredBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(basicBlock)) {
141 |               compiler.report(
142 |                   JSError.make(reference.getSourceFile().getName(),
143 |                       reference.getNode(),
144 |                       checkLevel,
145 |                       REDECLARED_VARIABLE, v.name));
146 |               break;
147 |             }
148 |           }
149 |         }
150 | 
151 |         if (isUnhoistedNamedFunction && !isDeclaration && isDeclaredInScope) {
152 |           // Only allow an unhoisted named function to be used within the
153 |           // block it is declared.
154 |           for (BasicBlock declaredBlock : blocksWithDeclarations) {
155 |             if (!declaredBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(basicBlock)) {
156 |               compiler.report(
157 |                   JSError.make(reference.getSourceFile().getName(),
158 |                       reference.getNode(),
159 |                       AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTION_DECL, v.name));
160 |               break;
161 |             }
162 |           }
163 |         }
164 | 
165 |         if (!isDeclaration && !isDeclaredInScope) {
166 |           // Don't check the order of refer in externs files.
167 |           if (!reference.getSourceFile().isExtern()) {
168 |             // Special case to deal with var goog = goog || {}
169 |             Node grandparent = reference.getGrandparent();
170 |             if (grandparent.getType() == Token.NAME
171 |                 && grandparent.getString() == v.name) {
172 |               continue;
173 |             }
174 | 
175 |             // Only generate warnings if the scopes do not match in order
176 |             // to deal with possible forward declarations and recursion
177 |             if (reference.getScope() == v.scope) {
178 |               compiler.report(
179 |                   JSError.make(reference.getSourceFile().getName(),
180 |                                reference.getNode(),
181 |                                checkLevel,
182 |                                UNDECLARED_REFERENCE, v.name));
183 |             }
184 |           }
185 |         }
186 | 
187 |         if (isDeclaration) {
188 |           blocksWithDeclarations.add(basicBlock);
189 |           isDeclaredInScope = true;
190 |         }
191 |       }
192 |     }

Original range: 113-134
Documentation:
/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 2 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. If A and B are in the same fixed point loop,
   * the loop will continue to run both A and B until both are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * Other than that, the PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and
   * frequency of multi-run passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
113 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
114 |     Loop currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
115 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
116 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
117 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
118 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
119 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
120 | 
121 |           currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
122 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
123 |         }
124 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
125 |       } else {
126 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
127 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
128 |       }
129 |     }
130 | 
131 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
132 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
133 |     }
134 |   }

491 |   private List<String> processArgs(String[] args) {
492 |     // Args4j has a different format that the old command-line parser.
493 |     // So we use some voodoo to get the args into the format that args4j
494 |     // expects.
495 |     Pattern argPattern = Pattern.compile("(--[a-zA-Z_]+)=(.*)");
496 |     Pattern quotesPattern = Pattern.compile("^['\"](.*)['\"]$");
497 |     List<String> processedArgs = Lists.newArrayList();
498 | 
499 |     for (String arg : args) {
500 |       Matcher matcher = argPattern.matcher(arg);
501 |       if (matcher.matches()) {
502 |         processedArgs.add(matcher.group(1));
503 | 
504 |         String value = matcher.group(2);
505 |         Matcher quotesMatcher = quotesPattern.matcher(value);
506 |         if (quotesMatcher.matches()) {
507 |           processedArgs.add(quotesMatcher.group(1));
508 |         } else {
509 |           processedArgs.add(value);
510 |         }
511 |       } else {

513 |       }
514 |     }
515 |

   * Attempt to replace the condition of if or hook immediately that is a
   * reference to a name that is assigned immediately before.
   */

494 |   private void tryOptimizeConditionalAfterAssign(Node n) {
495 |     Node next = n.getNext();
496 | 
497 |     // Look for patterns like the following and replace the if-condition with
498 |     // a constant value so it can later be folded:
499 |     //   var a = /a/;
500 |     //   if (a) {foo(a)}
501 |     // or

503 |     //   a ? foo(a) : c;

506 |     //   a || foo(a);
507 |     // or

510 |     //
511 |     // TODO(johnlenz): This would be better handled by control-flow sensitive
512 |     // constant propagation. As the other case that I want to handle is:
513 |     //   i=0; for(;i<0;i++){}

515 |     // This is here simply to remove the cruft left behind goog.userAgent and
516 |     // similar cases.

519 |       Node lhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentName(n);
520 | 
521 |       Node condition = getConditionalStatementCondition(next);
522 |       if (NodeUtil.isName(lhsAssign) && NodeUtil.isName(condition)
523 |           && lhsAssign.getString().equals(condition.getString())) {
524 |         Node rhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentValue(n);
525 |         TernaryValue value = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(rhsAssign);
526 |         if (value != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {

529 |           condition.getParent().replaceChild(condition,
530 |               new Node(replacementConditionNodeType));

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SourceFile.getLine(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SourceFile.java
Original range: 166-201
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the source line for the indicated line number.
   *
   * @param lineNumber the line number, 1 being the first line of the file.
   * @return The line indicated. Does not include the newline at the end
   *     of the file. Returns {@code null} if it does not exist,
   *     or if there was an IO exception.
   */
Method code:
166 |   public String getLine(int lineNumber) {
167 |     String js = "";
168 |     try {
169 |       // NOTE(nicksantos): Right now, this is optimized for few warnings.
170 |       // This is probably the right trade-off, but will be slow if there
171 |       // are lots of warnings in one file.
172 |       js = getCode();
173 |     } catch (IOException e) {
174 |       return null;
175 |     }
176 | 
177 |     int pos = 0;
178 |     int startLine = 1;
179 | 
180 |     // If we've saved a previous offset and it's for a line less than the
181 |     // one we're searching for, then start at that point.
182 |     if (lineNumber >= lastLine) {
183 |       pos = lastOffset;
184 |       startLine = lastLine;
185 |     }
186 | 
187 |     for (int n = startLine; n < lineNumber; n++) {
188 |       int nextpos = js.indexOf('\n', pos);
189 |       if (nextpos == -1) {
190 |         return null;
191 |       }
192 |       pos = nextpos + 1;
193 |     }
194 | 
195 |     // Remember this offset for the next search we do.
196 |     lastOffset = pos;
197 |     lastLine = lineNumber;
198 | 
199 |     return (js.indexOf('\n', pos) == -1) ? null :
200 |         js.substring(pos, js.indexOf('\n', pos));
201 |   }

/**
   * Tokenizes JSDoc comments.

59 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
60 |   final JsDocToken getJsDocToken() {
61 |     int c;
62 |     stringBufferTop = 0;
63 |     for (;;) {
64 |       // eat white spaces
65 |       for (;;) {
66 |         charno = -1;
67 |         c = getChar();
68 |         if (c == EOF_CHAR) {
69 |           return JsDocToken.EOF;

71 |           return JsDocToken.EOL;
72 |         } else if (!isJSSpace(c)) {
73 |           break;
74 |         }
75 |       }
76 |

78 |         // annotation, e.g. @type or @constructor

83 |               addToString(c);
84 |             } else {
85 |               ungetChar(c);

88 |               return JsDocToken.ANNOTATION;

91 | 
92 |         case '*':
93 |           if (matchChar('/')) {
94 |             return JsDocToken.EOC;
95 |           } else {
96 |             return JsDocToken.STAR;
97 |           }

100 |           return JsDocToken.COMMA;
101 | 
102 |         case '>':
103 |           return JsDocToken.GT;
104 | 
105 |         case '(':
106 |           return JsDocToken.LP;
107 | 
108 |         case ')':
109 |           return JsDocToken.RP;
110 | 
111 |         case '{':
112 |           return JsDocToken.LC;
113 | 
114 |         case '}':
115 |           return JsDocToken.RC;
116 | 
117 |         case '[':
118 |           return JsDocToken.LB;
119 | 
120 |         case ']':
121 |           return JsDocToken.RB;
122 | 
123 |         case '?':
124 |           return JsDocToken.QMARK;
125 | 
126 |         case '!':
127 |           return JsDocToken.BANG;
128 | 
129 |         case ':':
130 |           return JsDocToken.COLON;
131 | 
132 |         case '=':
133 |           return JsDocToken.EQUALS;
134 | 
135 |         case '|':
136 |           matchChar('|');
137 |           return JsDocToken.PIPE;
138 | 
139 |         case '.':
140 |           c = getChar();

142 |             return JsDocToken.LT;
143 |           } else {

145 |               c = getChar();

155 |           }

158 |         default: {

160 |           // a non-jsdoc comment char, e.g. Array.<

/**
   * Visits an assignment <code>lvalue = rvalue</code>. If the
   * <code>lvalue</code> is a prototype modification, we change the schema
   * of the object type it is referring to.
   * @param t the traversal
   * @param assign the assign node
   * (<code>assign.getType() == Token.ASSIGN</code> is an implicit invariant)
   */
Method code:
841 |   private void visitAssign(NodeTraversal t, Node assign) {
842 |     JSDocInfo info = assign.getJSDocInfo();
843 |     Node lvalue = assign.getFirstChild();
844 |     Node rvalue = assign.getLastChild();
845 | 
846 |     if (lvalue.getType() == Token.GETPROP) {
847 |       Node object = lvalue.getFirstChild();
848 |       JSType objectJsType = getJSType(object);
849 |       String property = lvalue.getLastChild().getString();
850 | 
851 |       // the first name in this getprop refers to an interface
852 |       // we perform checks in addition to the ones below
853 |       if (object.getType() == Token.GETPROP) {
854 |         JSType jsType = getJSType(object.getFirstChild());
855 |         if (jsType.isInterface() &&
856 |             object.getLastChild().getString().equals("prototype")) {
857 |           visitInterfaceGetprop(t, assign, object, property, lvalue, rvalue);
858 |         }
859 |       }
860 | 
861 |       // /** @type ... */object.name = ...;
862 |       if (info != null && info.hasType()) {
863 |         visitAnnotatedAssignGetprop(t, assign,
864 |             info.getType().evaluate(t.getScope(), typeRegistry), object,
865 |             property, rvalue);
866 |         return;
867 |       }
868 | 
869 |       // /** @enum ... */object.name = ...;
870 |       if (info != null && info.hasEnumParameterType()) {
871 |         checkEnumInitializer(
872 |             t, rvalue, info.getEnumParameterType().evaluate(
873 |                 t.getScope(), typeRegistry));
874 |         return;
875 |       }
876 | 
877 |       // object.prototype = ...;
878 |       if (property.equals("prototype")) {
879 |         if (objectJsType instanceof FunctionType) {
880 |           FunctionType functionType = (FunctionType) objectJsType;
881 |           if (functionType.isConstructor()) {
882 |             JSType rvalueType = rvalue.getJSType();
883 |             validator.expectObject(t, rvalue, rvalueType,
884 |                 OVERRIDING_PROTOTYPE_WITH_NON_OBJECT);
885 |           }
886 |         } else {
887 |           // TODO(user): might want to flag that
888 |         }
889 |         return;
890 |       }
891 | 
892 |       // object.prototype.property = ...;
893 |       if (object.getType() == Token.GETPROP) {
894 |         Node object2 = object.getFirstChild();
895 |         String property2 = NodeUtil.getStringValue(object.getLastChild());
896 | 
897 |         if ("prototype".equals(property2)) {
898 |           JSType jsType = object2.getJSType();
899 |           if (jsType instanceof FunctionType) {
900 |             FunctionType functionType = (FunctionType) jsType;
901 |             if (functionType.isConstructor() || functionType.isInterface()) {
902 |               checkDeclaredPropertyInheritance(
903 |                   t, assign, functionType, property, info, getJSType(rvalue));
904 |             }
905 |           } else {
906 |             // TODO(user): might want to flag that
907 |           }
908 |           return;
909 |         }
910 |       }
911 | 
912 |       // object.property = ...;
913 |       ObjectType type = ObjectType.cast(
914 |           objectJsType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined());
915 |       if (type != null) {
916 |         if (type.hasProperty(property) &&
917 |             !type.isPropertyTypeInferred(property) &&
918 |             !propertyIsImplicitCast(type, property)) {
919 |           validator.expectCanAssignToPropertyOf(
920 |               t, assign, getJSType(rvalue),
921 |               type.getPropertyType(property), object, property);
922 |         }
923 |         return;
924 |       }
925 |     } else if (lvalue.getType() == Token.NAME) {
926 |       // variable with inferred type case
927 |       JSType rvalueType = getJSType(assign.getLastChild());
928 |       Var var = t.getScope().getVar(lvalue.getString());
929 |       if (var != null) {
930 |         if (var.isTypeInferred()) {
931 |           return;
932 |         }
933 |       }
934 |     }
935 | 
936 |     // fall through case
937 |     JSType leftType = getJSType(lvalue);
938 |     Node rightChild = assign.getLastChild();
939 |     JSType rightType = getJSType(rightChild);
940 |     if (validator.expectCanAssignTo(
941 |             t, assign, rightType, leftType, "assignment")) {
942 |       ensureTyped(t, assign, rightType);
943 |     } else {
944 |       ensureTyped(t, assign);
945 |     }
946 |   }

Method code:
203 |   void addOp(String op, boolean binOp) {
204 |     maybeEndStatement();
205 | 
206 |     char first = op.charAt(0);
207 |     char prev = getLastChar();
208 | 
209 |     if ((first == '+' || first == '-') && prev == first) {
210 |       // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of
211 |       // things like "x + ++y" or "x++ + ++y"
212 |       append(" ");
213 |     } else if (Character.isLetter(first) &&
214 |                isWordChar(prev)) {
215 |       // Make sure there is a space after e.g. instanceof , typeof
216 |       append(" ");
217 |     } else if (prev == '-' && first == '>') {
218 |       // Make sure that we don't emit -->
219 |       append(" ");
220 |     }
221 | 
222 |     // Allow formating around the operator.
223 |     appendOp(op, binOp);
224 | 
225 |     // Line breaking after an operator is always safe. Line breaking before an
226 |     // operator on the other hand is not. We only line break after a bin op
227 |     // because it looks strange.
228 |     if (binOp) {
229 |       maybeCutLine();
230 |     }

Documentation:
/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an function expression? An function expression is one
   * that has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of function expressions:
   * <pre>
   * (function () {})
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> expressions:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A node
   * @return Whether n is an function used within an expression.
   */
Method code:
1934 |   static boolean isFunctionExpression(Node n) {
1935 |     return n.getType() == Token.FUNCTION && !isStatement(n);
1936 |   }

237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

796 |                   Node typeNode = null;

798 |                       annotation == Annotation.RETURN) {

800 |                     // it as the unknown type.

803 |                     skipEOLs();

806 |                   }

812 |                     }

818 |                     // recovering parsing

824 |                               lineno, charno);

832 |                           break;
833 |                         }

838 |                               extractMultilineTextualBlock(token);

840 |                           String returnDescription =
841 |                               returnDescriptionInfo.string;

843 |                           if (returnDescription.length() > 0) {
844 |                             jsdocBuilder.recordReturnDescription(
845 |                                 returnDescription);
846 |                           }
847 | 
848 |                           token = returnDescriptionInfo.token;
849 |                         } else {
850 |                           token = eatTokensUntilEOL(token);
851 |                         }
852 |                         continue retry;
853 | 
854 |                       case THIS:
855 |                         if (!jsdocBuilder.recordThisType(type)) {
856 |                           parser.addTypeWarning(
857 |                               "msg.jsdoc.incompat.type", lineno, charno);
858 |                         }
859 |                         break;
860 | 
861 |                       case TYPE:
862 |                         if (!jsdocBuilder.recordType(type)) {
863 |                           parser.addTypeWarning(
864 |                               "msg.jsdoc.incompat.type", lineno, charno);
865 |                         }
866 |                         break;

869 |                         if (!jsdocBuilder.recordTypedef(type)) {
870 |                           parser.addTypeWarning(
871 |                               "msg.jsdoc.incompat.type", lineno, charno);
872 |                         }
873 |                         break;
874 |                     }
875 |                   }
876 | 
877 |                   token = eatTokensUntilEOL();
878 |                   continue retry;
879 |               }
880 |             }
881 |           }
882 |           break;
883 | 
884 |         case EOC:
885 |           if (hasParsedFileOverviewDocInfo()) {
886 |             fileOverviewJSDocInfo = retrieveAndResetParsedJSDocInfo();
887 |           }
888 |           checkExtendedTypes(extendedTypes);
889 |           return true;
890 | 
891 |         case EOF:
892 |           // discard any accumulated information
893 |           jsdocBuilder.build(null);
894 |           parser.addParserWarning("msg.unexpected.eof",
895 |               stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
896 |           checkExtendedTypes(extendedTypes);
897 |           return false;
898 | 
899 |         case EOL:
900 |           if (state == State.SEARCHING_NEWLINE) {
901 |             state = State.SEARCHING_ANNOTATION;
902 |           }
903 |           token = next();
904 |           continue retry;
905 | 
906 |         default:
907 |           if (token == JsDocToken.STAR && state == State.SEARCHING_ANNOTATION) {
908 |             token = next();
909 |             continue retry;
910 |           } else {
911 |             state = State.SEARCHING_NEWLINE;
912 |             token = eatTokensUntilEOL();
913 |             continue retry;
914 |           }
915 |       }
916 | 
917 |       // next token
918 |       token = next();
919 |     }
920 |   }

/**
   * Stop the trace.
   * This may only be done once and must be done from the same thread
   * that started it.
   * @param silence_threshold Traces for time less than silence_threshold
   * ms will be left out of the trace report. A value of -1 indicates
   * that the current ThreadTrace silence_threshold should be used.
   * @return The time that this trace actually ran
   */
Method code:
406 |   long stop(int silence_threshold) {
407 |     Preconditions.checkState(Thread.currentThread() == startThread);
408 | 
409 |     ThreadTrace trace = getThreadTrace();
410 |     // Do nothing if the thread trace was not initialized.
411 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
412 |       return 0;
413 |     }

416 |     if (extraTracingValues != null) {
417 |       // We use extraTracingValues.length rather than
418 |       // extraTracingStatistics.size() because a new statistic may
419 |       // have been added
420 |       for (int i = 0; i < extraTracingValues.length; i++) {
421 |         long value = extraTracingStatistics.get(i).stop(startThread);
422 |         extraTracingValues[i] = value - extraTracingValues[i];
423 |       }

427 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
428 |       return 0;
429 |     }

/** Test if all characters in the string are in the Basic Latin (aka ASCII)
   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode

/**
   * Connects cfgNode to the proper CATCH block if target subtree might throw
   * an exception. If there are FINALLY blocks reached before a CATCH, it will
   * make the corresponding entry in finallyMap.
   */
Method code:
820 |   private void connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node cfgNode, Node target) {
821 |     if (mayThrowException(target) && !exceptionHandler.isEmpty()) {
822 |       Node lastJump = cfgNode;
823 |       for (Node handler : exceptionHandler) {
824 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunction(handler)) {
825 |           return;
826 |         }
827 |         Preconditions.checkState(handler.getType() == Token.TRY);
828 |         Node catchBlock = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(handler);
829 | 
830 |         if (!NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(catchBlock)) { // No catch but a FINALLY.
831 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
832 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, handler.getLastChild());
833 |           } else {
834 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, handler.getLastChild());
835 |           }
836 |         } else { // Has a catch.
837 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
838 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, catchBlock);
839 |             return;
840 |           } else {
841 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, catchBlock);
842 |           }
843 |         }
844 |         lastJump = handler;
845 |       }
846 |     }
847 |   }

Documentation:
/**
     * Creates a new function type, based on the given nodes.
     *
     * This handles two cases that are semantically very different, but
     * are not mutually exclusive:
     * - A function literal that needs a type attached to it.
     * - An assignment expression with function-type info in the jsdoc.
     *
     * All parameters are optional, and we will do the best we can to create
     * a function type.
     *
     * This function will always create a function type, so only call it if
     * you're sure that's what you want.
     *
     * @param rValue The function node.
     * @param name the function's name
     * @param info the {@link JSDocInfo} attached to the function definition
     * @param lvalueNode The node where this function is being
     *     assigned. For example, {@code A.prototype.foo = ...} would be used to
     *     determine that this function is a method of A.prototype. May be
     *     null to indicate that this is not being assigned to a qualified name.
     */
Method code:
801 |     private FunctionType createFunctionTypeFromNodes(
802 |         @Nullable Node rValue,
803 |         @Nullable String name,
804 |         @Nullable JSDocInfo info,
805 |         @Nullable Node lvalueNode) {
806 | 
807 |       FunctionType functionType = null;
808 | 
809 |       // Global ctor aliases should be registered with the type registry.
810 |       if (rValue != null && rValue.isQualifiedName() && scope.isGlobal()) {
811 |         Var var = scope.getVar(rValue.getQualifiedName());
812 |         if (var != null && var.getType() instanceof FunctionType) {
813 |           FunctionType aliasedType  = (FunctionType) var.getType();
814 |           if ((aliasedType.isConstructor() || aliasedType.isInterface()) &&
815 |               !aliasedType.isNativeObjectType()) {
816 |             functionType = aliasedType;
817 | 
818 |             if (name != null && scope.isGlobal()) {
819 |               typeRegistry.declareType(name, functionType.getInstanceType());
820 |             }
821 |           }
822 |         }
823 |       }
824 | 
825 |       if (functionType == null) {
826 |         Node errorRoot = rValue == null ? lvalueNode : rValue;
827 |         boolean isFnLiteral =
828 |             rValue != null && rValue.getType() == Token.FUNCTION;
829 |         Node fnRoot = isFnLiteral ? rValue : null;
830 |         Node parametersNode = isFnLiteral ?
831 |             rValue.getFirstChild().getNext() : null;
832 |         Node fnBlock = isFnLiteral ? parametersNode.getNext() : null;
833 | 
834 |         if (info != null && info.hasType()) {
835 |           JSType type = info.getType().evaluate(scope, typeRegistry);
836 | 
837 |           // Known to be not null since we have the FUNCTION token there.
838 |           type = type.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
839 |           if (type.isFunctionType()) {
840 |             functionType = (FunctionType) type;
841 |             functionType.setJSDocInfo(info);
842 |           }
843 |         }
844 | 
845 |         if (functionType == null) {
846 |           // Find the type of any overridden function.
847 |           FunctionType overriddenPropType = null;
848 |           if (lvalueNode != null &&
849 |               lvalueNode.getType() == Token.GETPROP &&
850 |               lvalueNode.isQualifiedName()) {
851 |             Var var = scope.getVar(
852 |                 lvalueNode.getFirstChild().getQualifiedName());
853 |             if (var != null) {
854 |               ObjectType ownerType = ObjectType.cast(var.getType());
855 |               if (ownerType != null) {
856 |                 String propName = lvalueNode.getLastChild().getString();
857 |                 overriddenPropType =
858 |                     findOverriddenFunction(ownerType, propName);
859 |               }
860 |             }
861 |           }
862 | 
863 |           FunctionTypeBuilder builder =
864 |               new FunctionTypeBuilder(name, compiler, errorRoot, sourceName,
865 |                   scope)
866 |               .setSourceNode(fnRoot)
867 |               .inferFromOverriddenFunction(overriddenPropType, parametersNode)
868 |               .inferTemplateTypeName(info)
869 |               .inferReturnType(info)
870 |               .inferInheritance(info);
871 | 
872 |           // Infer the context type.
873 |           boolean searchedForThisType = false;
874 |           if (lvalueNode != null &&
875 |               lvalueNode.getType() == Token.GETPROP) {
876 |             Node objNode = lvalueNode.getFirstChild();
877 |             if (objNode.getType() == Token.GETPROP &&
878 |                 objNode.getLastChild().getString().equals("prototype")) {
879 |               builder.inferThisType(info, objNode.getFirstChild());
880 |               searchedForThisType = true;
881 |             } else if (objNode.getType() == Token.THIS) {
882 |               builder.inferThisType(info, objNode.getJSType());
883 |               searchedForThisType = true;
884 |             }
885 |           }
886 | 
887 |           if (!searchedForThisType) {
888 |             builder.inferThisType(info, (Node) null);
889 |           }
890 | 
891 |           functionType = builder
892 |               .inferParameterTypes(parametersNode, info)
893 |               .inferReturnStatementsAsLastResort(fnBlock)
894 |               .buildAndRegister();
895 |         }
896 |       }
897 | 
898 |       // all done
899 |       return functionType;
900 |     }

146 |   @Override
147 |   LiveVariableLattice flowThrough(Node node, LiveVariableLattice input) {
148 |     final BitSet gen = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
149 |     final BitSet kill = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
150 | 
151 |     // Make kills conditional if the node can end abruptly by an exception.
152 |     boolean conditional = false;
153 |     List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> edgeList = getCfg().getOutEdges(node);
154 |     for (DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch> edge : edgeList) {
155 |       if (Branch.ON_EX.equals(edge.getValue())) {
156 |         conditional = true;
157 |       }
158 |     }
159 |     computeGenKill(node, gen, kill, conditional);
160 |     LiveVariableLattice result = new LiveVariableLattice(input);
161 |     // L_in = L_out - Kill + Gen
162 |     result.liveSet.andNot(kill);
163 |     result.liveSet.or(gen);
164 |     return result;
165 |   }

261 |     @Override
262 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
263 |       if (isCallToScopeMethod(n)) {
264 |         if (!NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(parent)) {
265 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USED_IMPROPERLY);
266 |         }
267 |         if (n.getChildCount() != 2) {
268 |           // The goog.scope call should have exactly 1 parameter.  The first
269 |           // child is the "goog.scope" and the second should be the parameter.
270 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_HAS_BAD_PARAMETERS);
271 |         } else {
272 |           Node anonymousFnNode = n.getChildAtIndex(1);
273 |           if (!NodeUtil.isFunction(anonymousFnNode) ||
274 |               NodeUtil.getFunctionName(anonymousFnNode) != null ||
275 |               NodeUtil.getFunctionParameters(anonymousFnNode).hasChildren()) {
276 |             report(t, anonymousFnNode, GOOG_SCOPE_HAS_BAD_PARAMETERS);
277 |           } else {
278 |             scopeCalls.add(n);
279 |           }
280 |         }
281 |       }
282 | 
283 | 
284 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() == 2) {
285 |         int type = n.getType();
286 |         if (type == Token.NAME && parent.getType() == Token.VAR) {
287 |           if (n.hasChildren() && n.getFirstChild().isQualifiedName()) {
288 |             String name = n.getString();
289 |             Var aliasVar = t.getScope().getVar(name);
290 |             aliases.put(name, aliasVar);
291 |             aliasDefinitions.add(n);
292 |             String qualifiedName =
293 |                 aliasVar.getInitialValue().getQualifiedName();
294 |             transformation.addAlias(name, qualifiedName);
295 |             return;
296 |           } else {
297 |             // TODO(robbyw): Support using locals for private variables.
298 |             report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_NON_ALIAS_LOCAL, n.getString());
299 |           }
300 |         }
301 | 
302 |         if (type == Token.NAME && NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent) &&
303 |             n == parent.getFirstChild()) {
304 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_ALIAS_REDEFINED, n.getString());
305 |         }
306 | 
307 |         if (type == Token.RETURN) {
308 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_RETURN);
309 |         } else if (type == Token.THIS) {
310 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_REFERENCES_THIS);
311 |         } else if (type == Token.THROW) {
312 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_THROW);
313 |         }
314 |       }
315 | 
316 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() >= 2) {
317 |         if (n.getType() == Token.NAME) {
318 |           String name = n.getString();
319 |           Var aliasVar = aliases.get(name);
320 | 
321 |           // Check if this name points to an alias.
322 |           if (aliasVar != null &&
323 |               t.getScope().getVar(name) == aliasVar) {
324 |             // Note, to support the transitive case, it's important we don't
325 |             // clone aliasedNode here.  For example,
326 |             // var g = goog; var d = g.dom; d.createElement('DIV');
327 |             // The node in aliasedNode (which is "g") will be replaced in the
328 |             // changes pass above with "goog".  If we cloned here, we'd end up
329 |             // with <code>g.dom.createElement('DIV')</code>.
330 |             Node aliasedNode = aliasVar.getInitialValue();
331 |             aliasUsages.add(new AliasedNode(n, aliasedNode));
332 |           }
333 |         }
334 | 
335 |         JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
336 |         if (info != null) {
337 |           for (Node node : info.getTypeNodes()) {
338 |             fixTypeNode(node);
339 |           }
340 |         }
341 | 
342 |         // TODO(robbyw): Error for goog.scope not at root.
343 |       }
344 |     }

===== M0224 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.traverseName(Node,FlowScope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 632-671
Documentation:

Method code:
632 |   private FlowScope traverseName(Node n, FlowScope scope) {
633 |     String varName = n.getString();
634 |     Node value = n.getFirstChild();
635 |     JSType type = n.getJSType();
636 |     if (value != null) {
637 |       scope = traverse(value, scope);
638 |       updateScopeForTypeChange(scope, n, n.getJSType() /* could be null */,
639 |           getJSType(value));
640 |       return scope;
641 |     } else {
642 |       StaticSlot<JSType> var = scope.getSlot(varName);
643 |       if (var != null) {
644 |         // There are two situations where we don't want to use type information
645 |         // from the scope, even if we have it.
646 | 
647 |         // 1) The var is escaped in a weird way, e.g.,
648 |         // function f() { var x = 3; function g() { x = null } (x); }
649 |         boolean isInferred = var.isTypeInferred();
650 |         boolean unflowable =
651 |             isInferred && unflowableVarNames.contains(varName);
652 | 
653 |         // 2) We're reading type information from another scope for an
654 |         // inferred variable.
655 |         // var t = null; function f() { (t); }
656 |         boolean nonLocalInferredSlot =
657 |             isInferred &&
658 |             syntacticScope.getParent() != null &&
659 |             var == syntacticScope.getParent().getSlot(varName);
660 | 
661 |         if (!unflowable && !nonLocalInferredSlot) {
662 |           type = var.getType();
663 |           if (type == null) {
664 |             type = getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
665 |           }
666 |         }
667 |       }
668 |     }
669 |     n.setJSType(type);
670 |     return scope;
671 |   }

/**
   * Compute set of escaped variables. When a variable is escaped in a
   * dataflow analysis, it can be reference outside of the code that we are
   * analyzing. A variable is escaped if any of the following is true:
   *
   * <p><ol>
   * <li>It is defined as the exception name in CATCH clause so it became a
   * variable local not to our definition of scope.</li>
   * <li>Exported variables as they can be needed after the script terminates.
   * </li>
   * <li>Names of named functions because in javascript, <i>function foo(){}</i>
   * does not kill <i>foo</i> in the dataflow.</li>
   */
Method code:
548 |   static void computeEscaped(final Scope jsScope, final Set<Var> escaped,
549 |       AbstractCompiler compiler) {
550 |     // TODO(user): Very good place to store this information somewhere.
551 |     AbstractPostOrderCallback finder = new AbstractPostOrderCallback() {
552 |       @Override
553 |       public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
554 |         if (jsScope == t.getScope() || !NodeUtil.isName(n)
555 |             || NodeUtil.isFunction(parent)) {
556 |           return;
557 |         }
558 |         String name = n.getString();
559 |         Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
560 |         if (var != null && var.scope == jsScope) {
561 |           escaped.add(jsScope.getVar(name));
562 |         }
563 |       }
564 |     };
565 | 
566 |     NodeTraversal t = new NodeTraversal(compiler, finder);
567 |     t.traverseAtScope(jsScope);
568 | 
569 |     // 1: Remove the exception name in CATCH which technically isn't local to
570 |     //    begin with.
571 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = jsScope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
572 |       Var var = i.next();
573 |       if (var.getParentNode().getType() == Token.CATCH ||
574 |           compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.getName())) {
575 |         escaped.add(var);
576 |       }
577 |     }
578 |   }

===== M0266 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.ensurePropertyDefined(Node,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 545-590
Documentation:
/**
   * Defines a property if the property has not been defined yet.
   */
Method code:
545 |   private void ensurePropertyDefined(Node getprop, JSType rightType) {
546 |     String propName = getprop.getLastChild().getString();
547 |     JSType nodeType = getJSType(getprop.getFirstChild());
548 |     ObjectType objectType = ObjectType.cast(
549 |         nodeType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined());
550 |     if (objectType == null) {
551 |       registry.registerPropertyOnType(propName, nodeType);
552 |     } else {
553 |       if (ensurePropertyDeclaredHelper(getprop, objectType)) {
554 |         return;
555 |       }
556 | 
557 |       if (!objectType.isPropertyTypeDeclared(propName)) {
558 |         // We do not want a "stray" assign to define an inferred property
559 |         // for every object of this type in the program. So we use a heuristic
560 |         // approach to determine whether to infer the propery.
561 |         //
562 |         // 1) If the property is already defined, join it with the previously
563 |         //    inferred type.
564 |         // 2) If this isn't an instance object, define it.
565 |         // 3) If the property of an object is being assigned in the constructor,
566 |         //    define it.
567 |         // 4) If this is a stub, define it.
568 |         // 5) Otherwise, do not define the type, but declare it in the registry
569 |         //    so that we can use it for missing property checks.
570 |         if (objectType.hasProperty(propName) ||
571 |             !objectType.isInstanceType()) {
572 |           if ("prototype".equals(propName)) {
573 |             objectType.defineDeclaredProperty(
574 |                 propName, rightType, getprop);
575 |           } else {
576 |             objectType.defineInferredProperty(
577 |                 propName, rightType, getprop);
578 |           }
579 |         } else {
580 |           if (getprop.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.THIS &&
581 |               getJSType(syntacticScope.getRootNode()).isConstructor()) {
582 |             objectType.defineInferredProperty(
583 |                 propName, rightType, getprop);
584 |           } else {
585 |             registry.registerPropertyOnType(propName, objectType);
586 |           }
587 |         }
588 |       }
589 |     }
590 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InferJSDocInfo.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InferJSDocInfo.java
Original range: 92-188
Documentation:

Method code:
92 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
93 |     JSDocInfo docInfo;
94 | 
95 |     switch (n.getType()) {
96 |       // Infer JSDocInfo on types of all type declarations on variables.
97 |       case Token.NAME:
98 |         if (parent == null) {
99 |           return;
100 |         }
101 | 
102 |         // Only allow JSDoc on VARs, function declarations, and assigns.
103 |         if (parent.getType() != Token.VAR &&
104 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent) &&
105 |             !(parent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN &&
106 |               n == parent.getFirstChild())) {
107 |           return;
108 |         }
109 | 
110 |         // There are four places the doc info could live.
111 |         // 1) A FUNCTION node.
112 |         // /** ... */ function f() { ... }
113 |         // 2) An ASSIGN parent.
114 |         // /** ... */ x = function () { ... }
115 |         // 3) A NAME parent.
116 |         // var x, /** ... */ y = function() { ... }
117 |         // 4) A VAR gramps.
118 |         // /** ... */ var x = function() { ... }
119 |         docInfo = n.getJSDocInfo();
120 |         if (docInfo == null &&
121 |             !(parent.getType() == Token.VAR &&
122 |                 !parent.hasOneChild())) {
123 |           docInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
124 |         }
125 | 
126 |         // Try to find the type of the NAME.
127 |         JSType varType = n.getJSType();
128 |         if (varType == null && parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
129 |           varType = parent.getJSType();
130 |         }
131 | 
132 |         // If we have no type to attach JSDocInfo to, then there's nothing
133 |         // we can do.
134 |         if (varType == null || docInfo == null) {
135 |           return;
136 |         }
137 | 
138 |         // Dereference the type. If the result is not an object, or already
139 |         // has docs attached, then do nothing.
140 |         ObjectType objType = dereferenceToObject(varType);
141 |         if (objType == null || objType.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
142 |           return;
143 |         }
144 | 
145 |         attachJSDocInfoToNominalTypeOrShape(objType, docInfo, n.getString());
146 |         break;
147 | 
148 |       case Token.GETPROP:
149 |         // Infer JSDocInfo on properties.
150 |         // There are two ways to write doc comments on a property.
151 |         //
152 |         // 1)
153 |         // /** @deprecated */
154 |         // obj.prop = ...
155 |         //
156 |         // 2)
157 |         // /** @deprecated */
158 |         // obj.prop;
159 |         if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(parent) ||
160 |             (parent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN &&
161 |              parent.getFirstChild() == n)) {
162 |           docInfo = n.getJSDocInfo();
163 |           if (docInfo == null) {
164 |             docInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
165 |           }
166 |           if (docInfo != null) {
167 |             ObjectType lhsType =
168 |                 dereferenceToObject(n.getFirstChild().getJSType());
169 |             if (lhsType != null) {
170 |               // Put the JSDoc in the property slot, if there is one.
171 |               String propName = n.getLastChild().getString();
172 |               if (lhsType.hasOwnProperty(propName)) {
173 |                 lhsType.setPropertyJSDocInfo(propName, docInfo);
174 |               }
175 | 
176 |               // Put the JSDoc in any constructors or function shapes as well.
177 |               ObjectType propType =
178 |                   dereferenceToObject(lhsType.getPropertyType(propName));
179 |               if (propType != null) {
180 |                 attachJSDocInfoToNominalTypeOrShape(
181 |                     propType, docInfo, n.getQualifiedName());
182 |               }
183 |             }
184 |           }
185 |         }
186 |         break;
187 |     }
188 |   }

===== M0274 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.branchedFlowThrough(Node,FlowScope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 188-300
Documentation:

Method code:
188 |   @Override
189 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
190 |   List<FlowScope> branchedFlowThrough(Node source, FlowScope input) {
191 |     // NOTE(nicksantos): Right now, we just treat ON_EX edges like UNCOND
192 |     // edges. If we wanted to be perfect, we'd actually JOIN all the out
193 |     // lattices of this flow with the in lattice, and then make that the out
194 |     // lattice for the ON_EX edge. But it's probably to expensive to be
195 |     // worthwhile.
196 |     FlowScope output = flowThrough(source, input);
197 |     Node condition = null;
198 |     FlowScope conditionFlowScope = null;
199 |     BooleanOutcomePair conditionOutcomes = null;
200 | 
201 |     List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> branchEdges = getCfg().getOutEdges(source);
202 |     List<FlowScope> result = Lists.newArrayListWithCapacity(branchEdges.size());
203 |     for (DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch> branchEdge : branchEdges) {
204 |       Branch branch = branchEdge.getValue();
205 |       FlowScope newScope = output;
206 | 
207 |       switch (branch) {
208 |         case ON_TRUE:
209 |           if (NodeUtil.isForIn(source)) {
210 |             // item is assigned a property name, so its type should be string.
211 |             Node item = source.getFirstChild();
212 |             Node obj = item.getNext();
213 | 
214 |             FlowScope informed = traverse(obj, output.createChildFlowScope());
215 | 
216 |             if (item.getType() == Token.VAR) {
217 |               item = item.getFirstChild();
218 |             }
219 |             if (item.getType() == Token.NAME) {
220 |               JSType iterKeyType = getNativeType(STRING_TYPE);
221 |               ObjectType objType = getJSType(obj).dereference();
222 |               JSType objIndexType = objType == null ?
223 |                   null : objType.getIndexType();
224 |               if (objIndexType != null && !objIndexType.isUnknownType()) {
225 |                 JSType narrowedKeyType =
226 |                     iterKeyType.getGreatestSubtype(objIndexType);
227 |                 if (!narrowedKeyType.isEmptyType()) {
228 |                   iterKeyType = narrowedKeyType;
229 |                 }
230 |               }
231 |               redeclareSimpleVar(informed, item, iterKeyType);
232 |             }
233 |             newScope = informed;
234 |             break;
235 |           }
236 | 
237 |           // FALL THROUGH
238 | 
239 |         case ON_FALSE:
240 |           if (condition == null) {
241 |             condition = NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(source);
242 |             if (condition == null && source.getType() == Token.CASE) {
243 |               condition = source;
244 | 
245 |               // conditionFlowScope is cached from previous iterations
246 |               // of the loop.
247 |               if (conditionFlowScope == null) {
248 |                 conditionFlowScope = traverse(
249 |                     condition.getFirstChild(), output.createChildFlowScope());
250 |               }
251 |             }
252 |           }
253 | 
254 |           if (condition != null) {
255 |             if (condition.getType() == Token.AND ||
256 |                 condition.getType() == Token.OR) {
257 |               // When handling the short-circuiting binary operators,
258 |               // the outcome scope on true can be different than the outcome
259 |               // scope on false.
260 |               //
261 |               // TODO(nicksantos): The "right" way to do this is to
262 |               // carry the known outcome all the way through the
263 |               // recursive traversal, so that we can construct a
264 |               // different flow scope based on the outcome. However,
265 |               // this would require a bunch of code and a bunch of
266 |               // extra computation for an edge case. This seems to be
267 |               // a "good enough" approximation.
268 | 
269 |               // conditionOutcomes is cached from previous iterations
270 |               // of the loop.
271 |               if (conditionOutcomes == null) {
272 |                 conditionOutcomes = condition.getType() == Token.AND ?
273 |                     traverseAnd(condition, output.createChildFlowScope()) :
274 |                     traverseOr(condition, output.createChildFlowScope());
275 |               }
276 |               newScope =
277 |                   reverseInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(
278 |                       condition,
279 |                       conditionOutcomes.getOutcomeFlowScope(
280 |                           condition.getType(), branch == Branch.ON_TRUE),
281 |                       branch == Branch.ON_TRUE);
282 |             } else {
283 |               // conditionFlowScope is cached from previous iterations
284 |               // of the loop.
285 |               if (conditionFlowScope == null) {
286 |                 conditionFlowScope =
287 |                     traverse(condition, output.createChildFlowScope());
288 |               }
289 |               newScope =
290 |                   reverseInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(
291 |                       condition, conditionFlowScope, branch == Branch.ON_TRUE);
292 |             }
293 |           }
294 |           break;
295 |       }

88 |

91 |     }

100 |     switch(subtree.getType()) {
101 |       case Token.GETPROP:
102 |         return tryFoldGetProp(subtree, left, right);
103 | 
104 |       case Token.GETELEM:
105 |         return tryFoldGetElem(subtree, left, right);
106 | 
107 |       case Token.INSTANCEOF:
108 |         return tryFoldInstanceof(subtree, left, right);

112 |         return tryFoldAndOr(subtree, left, right);

115 |       case Token.RSH:
116 |       case Token.URSH:
117 |         return tryFoldShift(subtree, left, right);
118 | 
119 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
120 |         return tryFoldAssign(subtree, left, right);
121 | 
122 |       case Token.ADD:
123 |         return tryFoldAdd(subtree, left, right);
124 | 
125 |       case Token.SUB:
126 |       case Token.DIV:
127 |       case Token.MOD:
128 |         return tryFoldArithmeticOp(subtree, left, right);
129 | 
130 |       case Token.MUL:
131 |       case Token.BITAND:
132 |       case Token.BITOR:
133 |       case Token.BITXOR:
134 |         Node result = tryFoldArithmeticOp(subtree, left, right);
135 |         if (result != subtree) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.optimizeSubtree(Node)

34 |   @Override
35 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
36 |     if (subtree.getType() != Token.SCRIPT
37 |         && subtree.getType() != Token.BLOCK) {
38 |       return subtree;
39 |     }
40 | 
41 |     boolean codeChanged = false;
42 | 
43 |     // Look for variable declarations or simple assignments
44 |     // and start processing there.
45 |     for (Node child = subtree.getFirstChild();
46 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()) {
47 |       if (child.getType() != Token.VAR && !NodeUtil.isExprAssign(child)) {
48 |         continue;
49 |       }
50 |       if (!isPropertyAssignmentToName(child.getNext())) {
51 |         // Quick check to see if there's anything to collapse.
52 |         continue;
53 |       }
54 | 
55 |       Preconditions.checkState(child.hasOneChild());
56 |       Node name = getName(child);
57 |       if (name.getType() != Token.NAME) {
58 |         // The assignment target is not a simple name.
59 |         continue;
60 |       }
61 |       Node value = getValue(child);
62 |       if (value == null || !isInterestingValue(value)) {
63 |         // No initializer or not an Object or Array literal.
64 |         continue;
65 |       }
66 | 
67 |       Node propertyCandidate;
68 |       while ((propertyCandidate = child.getNext()) != null) {
69 |         // This does not infinitely loop because collectProperty always
70 |         // removes propertyCandidate from its parent when it returns true.
71 |         if (!collectProperty(propertyCandidate, name.getString(), value)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |         codeChanged = true;
75 |       }
76 |     }
77 | 
78 |     if (codeChanged) {
79 |       reportCodeChange();
80 |     }
81 |     return subtree;
82 |   }

===== M0297 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeArgumentsArray.tryReplaceArguments(Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeArgumentsArray.java
Original range: 178-290
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to optimize all the arguments array access in this scope by assigning
   * a name to each element.
   *
   * @param scope scope of the function
   * @return true if any modification has been done to the AST
   */
Method code:
178 |   private boolean tryReplaceArguments(Scope scope) {
179 | 
180 |     Node parametersList = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
181 |     Preconditions.checkState(parametersList.getType() == Token.LP);
182 | 
183 |     // Keep track of rather this function modified the AST and needs to be
184 |     // reported back to the compiler later.
185 |     boolean changed = false;
186 | 
187 |     // Number of parameter that can be accessed without using the arguments
188 |     // array.
189 |     int numNamedParameter = parametersList.getChildCount();
190 | 
191 |     // We want to guess what the highest index that has been access from the
192 |     // arguments array. We will guess that it does not use anything index higher
193 |     // than the named parameter list first until we see other wise.
194 |     int highestIndex = numNamedParameter - 1;
195 | 
196 |     // Iterate through all the references to arguments array in the function to
197 |     // determine the real highestIndex.
198 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
199 | 
200 |       Node getElem = ref.getParent();
201 | 
202 |       // Bail on anything but argument[c] access where c is a constant.
203 |       // TODO(user): We might not need to bail out all the time, there might
204 |       // be more cases that we can cover.
205 |       if (getElem.getType() != Token.GETELEM) {
206 |         return false;
207 |       }
208 | 
209 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
210 | 
211 |       // We have something like arguments[x] where x is not a constant. That
212 |       // means at least one of the access is not known.
213 |       if (index.getType() != Token.NUMBER) {
214 |         // TODO(user): Its possible not to give up just yet. The type
215 |         // inference did a 'semi value propagation'. If we know that string
216 |         // is never a subclass of the type of the index. We'd know that
217 |         // it is never 'callee'.
218 |         return false; // Give up.
219 |       }
220 | 
221 |       Node getElemParent = getElem.getParent();
222 |       // When we have argument[0](), replacing it with a() is semantically
223 |       // different if argument[0] is a function call that refers to 'this'
224 |       if (NodeUtil.isCall(getElemParent) &&
225 |           getElemParent.getFirstChild() == getElem) {
226 |         // TODO(user): We can consider using .call() if aliasing that
227 |         // argument allows shorter alias for other arguments.
228 |         return false;
229 |       }
230 | 
231 |       // Replace the highest index if we see an access that has a higher index
232 |       // than all the one we saw before.
233 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
234 |       if (value > highestIndex) {
235 |         highestIndex = value;
236 |       }
237 |     }
238 | 
239 |     // Number of extra arguments we need.
240 |     // For example: function() { arguments[3] } access index 3 so
241 |     // it will need 4 extra named arguments to changed into:
242 |     // function(a,b,c,d) { d }.
243 |     int numExtraArgs = highestIndex - numNamedParameter + 1;
244 | 
245 |     // Temporary holds the new names as string for quick access later.
246 |     String[] argNames = new String[numExtraArgs];
247 | 
248 |     // Insert the formal parameter to the method's signature.
249 |     // Example: function() --> function(r0, r1, r2)
250 |     for (int i = 0; i < numExtraArgs; i++) {
251 |       String name = getNewName();
252 |       argNames[i] = name;
253 |       parametersList.addChildrenToBack(Node.newString(Token.NAME, name));
254 |       changed = true;
255 |     }
256 | 
257 |     // This loop performs the replacement of arguments[x] -> a if x is known.
258 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
259 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
260 | 
261 |       // Skip if it is unknown.
262 |       if (index.getType() != Token.NUMBER) {
263 |         continue;
264 |       }
265 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
266 | 
267 |       // Unnamed parameter.
268 |       if (value >= numNamedParameter) {
269 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
270 |             Node.newString(Token.NAME, argNames[value - numNamedParameter]));
271 |       } else {
272 | 
273 |         // Here, for no apparent reason, the user is accessing a named parameter
274 |         // with arguments[idx]. We can replace it with the actual name for them.
275 |         Node name = parametersList.getFirstChild();
276 | 
277 |         // This is a linear search for the actual name from the signature.
278 |         // It is not necessary to make this fast because chances are the user
279 |         // will not deliberately write code like this.
280 |         for (int i = 0; i < value; i++) {
281 |           name = name.getNext();
282 |         }
283 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
284 |             Node.newString(Token.NAME, name.getString()));
285 |       }
286 |       changed = true;
287 |     }
288 | 
289 |     return changed;
290 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.StatementFusion.canFuseIntoOneStatement(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/StatementFusion.java
Original range: 46-83
Documentation:

Method code:
46 |   private static boolean canFuseIntoOneStatement(Node block) {
47 |     // Fold only statement block. NOT scripts block.
48 |     if (block.getType() != Token.BLOCK) {
49 |       return false;
50 |     }
51 | 
52 |     // Nothing to do here.
53 |     if (!block.hasChildren() || block.hasOneChild()) {
54 |       return false;
55 |     }
56 | 
57 |     Node last = block.getLastChild();
58 | 
59 |     for (Node c = block.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
60 |       if (!NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(c) && c != last) {
61 |         return false;
62 |       }
63 |     }
64 | 
65 |     // TODO(user): Support more control statement for fusion.
66 |     // FOR
67 |     switch(last.getType()) {
68 |       case Token.IF:
69 |       case Token.THROW:
70 |       case Token.SWITCH:
71 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
72 |         return true;
73 |       case Token.RETURN:
74 |         // We don't want to add a new return value.
75 |         return last.hasChildren();
76 |       case Token.FOR:
77 |         return NodeUtil.isForIn(last) &&
78 |             // Avoid cases where we have for(var x = foo() in a) { ....
79 |             !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(last.getFirstChild());
80 |     }
81 | 
82 |     return false;
83 |   }

===== M0320 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessClosurePrimitives.ProvidedName.replace()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessClosurePrimitives.java
Original range: 875-938
Documentation:
/**
     * Replace the provide statement.
     *
     * If we're providing a name with no definition, then create one.
     * If we're providing a name with a duplicate definition, then make sure
     * that definition becomes a declaration.
     */
Method code:
875 |     void replace() {
876 |       if (firstNode == null) {
877 |         // Don't touch the base case ('goog').
878 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
879 |         return;
880 |       }
881 | 
882 |       // Handle the case where there is a duplicate definition for an explicitly
883 |       // provided symbol.
884 |       if (candidateDefinition != null && explicitNode != null) {
885 |         explicitNode.detachFromParent();
886 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
887 | 
888 |         // Does this need a VAR keyword?
889 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
890 |         if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(candidateDefinition) &&
891 |             !candidateDefinition.getFirstChild().isQualifiedName()) {
892 |           candidateDefinition.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_NAMESPACE, true);
893 |           Node assignNode = candidateDefinition.getFirstChild();
894 |           Node nameNode = assignNode.getFirstChild();
895 |           if (nameNode.getType() == Token.NAME) {
896 |             // Need to convert this assign to a var declaration.
897 |             Node valueNode = nameNode.getNext();
898 |             assignNode.removeChild(nameNode);
899 |             assignNode.removeChild(valueNode);
900 |             nameNode.addChildToFront(valueNode);
901 |             Node varNode = new Node(Token.VAR, nameNode);
902 |             varNode.copyInformationFrom(candidateDefinition);
903 |             candidateDefinition.getParent().replaceChild(
904 |                 candidateDefinition, varNode);
905 |             nameNode.setJSDocInfo(assignNode.getJSDocInfo());
906 |             compiler.reportCodeChange();
907 |             replacementNode = varNode;
908 |           }
909 |         }
910 |       } else {
911 |         // Handle the case where there's not a duplicate definition.
912 |         replacementNode = createDeclarationNode();
913 |         if (firstModule == minimumModule) {
914 |           firstNode.getParent().addChildBefore(replacementNode, firstNode);
915 |         } else {
916 |           // In this case, the name was implicitly provided by two independent
917 |           // modules. We need to move this code up to a common module.
918 |           int indexOfDot = namespace.lastIndexOf('.');
919 |           if (indexOfDot == -1) {
920 |             // Any old place is fine.
921 |             compiler.getNodeForCodeInsertion(minimumModule)
922 |                 .addChildToBack(replacementNode);
923 |           } else {
924 |             // Add it after the parent namespace.
925 |             ProvidedName parentName =
926 |                 providedNames.get(namespace.substring(0, indexOfDot));
927 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName);
928 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName.replacementNode);
929 |             parentName.replacementNode.getParent().addChildAfter(
930 |                 replacementNode, parentName.replacementNode);
931 |           }
932 |         }
933 |         if (explicitNode != null) {
934 |           explicitNode.detachFromParent();
935 |         }
936 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
937 |       }
938 |     }

/**
   * Informally, a function is represented by
   * {@code function (params): returnType} where the {@code params} is a comma
   * separated list of types, the first one being a special
   * {@code this:T} if the function expects a known type for {@code this}.
   */
Method code:
773 |   @Override
774 |   public String toString() {

776 |       return "Function";
777 |     }

779 |     StringBuilder b = new StringBuilder(32);
780 |     b.append("function (");
781 |     int paramNum = call.parameters.getChildCount();
782 |     boolean hasKnownTypeOfThis = !typeOfThis.isUnknownType();
783 |     if (hasKnownTypeOfThis) {
784 |       if (isConstructor()) {
785 |         b.append("new:");
786 |       } else {
787 |         b.append("this:");
788 |       }

796 |       if (p.isVarArgs()) {
797 |         appendVarArgsString(b, p.getJSType());
798 |       } else {
799 |         b.append(p.getJSType().toString());
800 |       }
801 |       p = p.getNext();
802 |       while (p != null) {
803 |         b.append(", ");
804 |         if (p.isVarArgs()) {
805 |           appendVarArgsString(b, p.getJSType());

807 |           b.append(p.getJSType().toString());
808 |         }
809 |         p = p.getNext();
810 |       }
811 |     }

203 |   private static boolean isBlockBoundary(Node n, Node parent) {
204 |     if (parent != null) {
205 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
206 |         case Token.DO:
207 |         case Token.FOR:
208 |         case Token.TRY:

   * Two function types are equal if their signatures match. Since they don't
   * have signatures, two interfaces are equal if their names match.
   */

730 |   @Override

755 |         this.call.isEquivalentTo(that.call);

===== M0415 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 201-229
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
201 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
202 |     initialize();
203 |     int step = 0;
204 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
205 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
206 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
207 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
208 |       }
209 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
210 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
211 |       joinInputs(curNode);
212 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
213 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
214 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
215 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
216 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
217 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
218 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
219 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
220 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |       step++;
225 |     }
226 |     if (isForward()) {
227 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
228 |     }
229 |   }
