Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LiveVariablesAnalysis.computeGenKill(Node,BitSet,BitSet,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LiveVariablesAnalysis.java
Original range: 178-263
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the GEN and KILL set.
   *
   * @param n Root node.
   * @param gen Local variables that are live because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param kill Local variables that are killed because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param conditional {@code true} if any assignments encountered are
   *        conditionally executed. These assignments might not kill a variable.
   */
Method code:
178 |   private void computeGenKill(Node n, BitSet gen, BitSet kill,
179 |       boolean conditional) {
180 | 
181 |     switch (n.getType()) {
182 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
183 |       case Token.BLOCK:
184 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
185 |         return;
186 | 
187 |       case Token.WHILE:
188 |       case Token.DO:
189 |       case Token.IF:
190 |         computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
191 |             conditional);
192 |         return;
193 | 
194 |       case Token.FOR:
195 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
196 |           computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
197 |               conditional);
198 |         } else {
199 |           // for(x in y) {...}
200 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
201 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
202 |           if (NodeUtil.isVar(lhs)) {
203 |             // for(var x in y) {...}
204 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild();
205 |           }
206 |           addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
207 |           addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
208 |           computeGenKill(rhs, gen, kill, conditional);
209 |         }
210 |         return;
211 | 
212 |       case Token.VAR:
213 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
214 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
215 |             computeGenKill(c.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
216 |             if (!conditional) {
217 |               addToSetIfLocal(c, kill);
218 |             }
219 |           }
220 |         }
221 |         return;
222 | 
223 |       case Token.AND:
224 |       case Token.OR:
225 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
226 |         // May short circuit.
227 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
228 |         return;
229 | 
230 |       case Token.HOOK:
231 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
232 |         // Assume both sides are conditional.
233 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), gen, kill, true);
234 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
235 |         return;
236 | 
237 |       case Token.NAME:
238 |         if (isArgumentsName(n)) {
239 |           markAllParametersEscaped();
240 |         } else {
241 |           addToSetIfLocal(n, gen);
242 |         }
243 |         return;
244 | 
245 |       default:
246 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isName(n.getFirstChild())) {
247 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
248 |           if (!conditional) {
249 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
250 |           }
251 |           if (!NodeUtil.isAssign(n)) {
252 |             // assignments such as a += 1 reads a.
253 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
254 |           }
255 |           computeGenKill(lhs.getNext(), gen, kill, conditional);
256 |         } else {
257 |           for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
258 |             computeGenKill(c, gen, kill, conditional);
259 |           }
260 |         }
261 |         return;
262 |     }
263 |   }

134 | 
135 |       // Sort nodes by degree.

137 |         @Override

139 |           int result = graph.getWeight(o2.getValue())
140 |               - graph.getWeight(o1.getValue());
141 |           return result == 0 && tieBreaker != null ?
142 |               tieBreaker.compare(o1.getValue(), o2.getValue()) : result;
143 |         }

147 |       // a unique color if none of its neighbor has been assigned that color.

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryMinimizeCondition(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 1004-1186
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to minimize conditions expressions, as there are additional
   * assumptions that can be made when it is known that the final result
   * is a boolean.
   *
   * The following transformations are done recursively:
   *   !(x||y) --> !x&&!y
   *   !(x&&y) --> !x||!y
   *   !!x     --> x
   * Thus:
   *   !(x&&!y) --> !x||!!y --> !x||y
   *
   *   Returns the replacement for n, or the original if no change was made
   */
Method code:
1004 |   private Node tryMinimizeCondition(Node n) {
1005 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
1006 | 
1007 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1008 |       case Token.NOT:
1009 |         Node first = n.getFirstChild();
1010 |         switch (first.getType()) {
1011 |           case Token.NOT: {
1012 |               Node newRoot = first.removeFirstChild();
1013 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1014 |               reportCodeChange();
1015 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1016 |               // NOT children are handled below.
1017 |               return newRoot;
1018 |             }
1019 |           case Token.AND:
1020 |           case Token.OR: {
1021 |               // !(!x && !y) --> x || y
1022 |               // !(!x || !y) --> x && y
1023 |               // !(!x && y) --> x || !y
1024 |               // !(!x || y) --> x && !y
1025 |               // !(x && !y) --> !x || y
1026 |               // !(x || !y) --> !x && y
1027 |               // !(x && y) --> !x || !y
1028 |               // !(x || y) --> !x && !y
1029 |               Node leftParent = first.getFirstChild();
1030 |               Node rightParent = first.getLastChild();
1031 |               Node left, right;
1032 | 
1033 |               // Check special case when such transformation cannot reduce
1034 |               // due to the added ()
1035 |               // It only occurs when both of expressions are not NOT expressions
1036 |               if (leftParent.getType() != Token.NOT
1037 |                   && rightParent.getType() != Token.NOT) {
1038 |                 // If an expression has higher precendence than && or ||,
1039 |                 // but lower precedence than NOT, an additional () is needed
1040 |                 // Thus we do not preceed
1041 |                 int op_precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType());
1042 |                 if ((isLowerPrecedence(leftParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1043 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(leftParent, op_precedence))
1044 |                     || (isLowerPrecedence(rightParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1045 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(rightParent, op_precedence))) {
1046 |                   return n;
1047 |                 }
1048 |               }
1049 | 
1050 |               if (leftParent.getType() == Token.NOT) {
1051 |                 left = leftParent.removeFirstChild();
1052 |               } else {
1053 |                 leftParent.detachFromParent();
1054 |                 left = new Node(Token.NOT, leftParent)
1055 |                   .copyInformationFrom(leftParent);
1056 |               }
1057 |               if (rightParent.getType() == Token.NOT) {
1058 |                 right = rightParent.removeFirstChild();
1059 |               } else {
1060 |                 rightParent.detachFromParent();
1061 |                 right = new Node(Token.NOT, rightParent)
1062 |                   .copyInformationFrom(rightParent);
1063 |               }
1064 | 
1065 |               int newOp = (first.getType() == Token.AND) ? Token.OR : Token.AND;
1066 |               Node newRoot = new Node(newOp, left, right);
1067 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1068 |               reportCodeChange();
1069 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1070 |               // AND and OR children below.
1071 |               return newRoot;
1072 |             }
1073 | 
1074 |            default:
1075 |              TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(first);
1076 |              if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1077 |                boolean result = nVal.not().toBoolean(true);
1078 |                int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1079 |                return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1080 |              }
1081 |         }
1082 |         // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the NOT
1083 |         // children in the general case in the main post-order traversal.
1084 |         return n;
1085 | 
1086 |       case Token.OR:
1087 |       case Token.AND: {
1088 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
1089 |         Node right = n.getLastChild();
1090 | 
1091 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1092 |         // the children, this can't be done in the general case.
1093 |         left = tryMinimizeCondition(left);
1094 |         right = tryMinimizeCondition(right);
1095 | 
1096 |         // Remove useless conditionals
1097 |         // Handle four cases:
1098 |         //   x || false --> x
1099 |         //   x || true  --> true
1100 |         //   x && true --> x
1101 |         //   x && false  --> false
1102 |         TernaryValue rightVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right);
1103 |         if (NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right) != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1104 |           int type = n.getType();
1105 |           Node replacement = null;
1106 |           boolean rval = rightVal.toBoolean(true);
1107 | 
1108 |           // (x || FALSE) => x
1109 |           // (x && TRUE) => x
1110 |           if (type == Token.OR && !rval ||
1111 |               type == Token.AND && rval) {
1112 |             replacement = left;
1113 |           } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
1114 |             replacement = right;
1115 |           }
1116 | 
1117 |           if (replacement != null) {
1118 |             n.detachChildren();
1119 |             parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1120 |             reportCodeChange();
1121 |             return replacement;
1122 |           }
1123 |         }
1124 |         return n;
1125 |       }
1126 | 
1127 |       case Token.HOOK: {
1128 |         Node condition = n.getFirstChild();
1129 |         Node trueNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
1130 |         Node falseNode = n.getLastChild();
1131 | 
1132 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1133 |         // the result children, this can't be done in the general case.
1134 |         // The condition is handled in the general case in #optimizeSubtree
1135 |         trueNode = tryMinimizeCondition(trueNode);
1136 |         falseNode = tryMinimizeCondition(falseNode);
1137 | 
1138 |         // Handle four cases:
1139 |         //   x ? true : false --> x
1140 |         //   x ? false : true --> !x
1141 |         //   x ? true : y     --> x || y
1142 |         //   x ? y : false    --> x && y
1143 |         Node replacement = null;
1144 |         TernaryValue trueNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(trueNode);
1145 |         TernaryValue falseNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(falseNode);
1146 |         if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE
1147 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1148 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1149 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1150 |           replacement = condition;
1151 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE
1152 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1153 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1154 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1155 |           replacement = new Node(Token.NOT, condition);
1156 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1157 |           // Remove useless true case.
1158 |           n.detachChildren();
1159 |           replacement = new Node(Token.OR, condition, falseNode);
1160 |         } else if (falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1161 |           // Remove useless false case
1162 |           n.detachChildren();
1163 |           replacement = new Node(Token.AND, condition, trueNode);
1164 |         }
1165 | 
1166 |         if (replacement != null) {
1167 |           parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1168 |           n = replacement;
1169 |           reportCodeChange();
1170 |         }
1171 | 
1172 |         return n;
1173 |       }
1174 | 
1175 |       default:
1176 |         // while(true) --> while(1)
1177 |         TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(n);
1178 |         if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1179 |           boolean result = nVal.toBoolean(true);
1180 |           int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1181 |           return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1182 |         }
1183 |         // We can't do anything else currently.
1184 |         return n;
1185 |     }
1186 |   }

/**

Method code:

===== M0441 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.identifierEscape(String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 1077-1097
Documentation:

Method code:
1077 |   static String identifierEscape(String s) {
1078 |     // First check if escaping is needed at all -- in most cases it isn't.
1079 |     if (NodeUtil.isLatin(s)) {
1080 |       return s;
1081 |     }
1082 | 
1083 |     // Now going through the string to escape non-latin characters if needed.
1084 |     StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
1085 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
1086 |       char c = s.charAt(i);
1087 |       // Identifiers should always go to Latin1/ ASCII characters because
1088 |       // different browser's rules for valid identifier characters are
1089 |       // crazy.
1090 |       if (c > 0x1F && c < 0x7F) {
1091 |         sb.append(c);
1092 |       } else {
1093 |         appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1094 |       }
1095 |     }
1096 |     return sb.toString();
1097 |   }

===== M0481 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 122-168
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a literal. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function
   * except it return UNKNOWN for known values with side-effects, use
   * getExpressionBooleanValue if you don't care about side-effects.
   */
Method code:
122 |   static TernaryValue getPureBooleanValue(Node n) {
123 |     switch (n.getType()) {
124 |       case Token.STRING:
125 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getString().length() > 0);
126 | 
127 |       case Token.NUMBER:
128 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getDouble() != 0);
129 | 
130 |       case Token.NOT:
131 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild()).not();
132 | 
133 |       case Token.NULL:
134 |       case Token.FALSE:
135 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
136 | 
137 |       case Token.VOID:
138 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n.getFirstChild())) {
139 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
140 |         }
141 |         break;
142 | 
143 |       case Token.NAME:
144 |         String name = n.getString();
145 |         if ("undefined".equals(name)
146 |             || "NaN".equals(name)) {
147 |           // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
148 |           // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
149 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
150 |         } else if ("Infinity".equals(name)) {
151 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
152 |         }
153 |         break;
154 | 
155 |       case Token.TRUE:
156 |       case Token.REGEXP:
157 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
158 | 
159 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
160 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
161 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
162 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
163 |         }
164 |         break;
165 |     }
166 | 
167 |     return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
168 |   }

/**
     * Look for a type declaration on a property assignment
     * (in an ASSIGN or an object literal key).
     *
     * @param info The doc info for this property.
     * @param lValue The l-value node.
     * @param rValue The node that {@code n} is being initialized to,
     *     or {@code null} if this is a stub declaration.

Method code:
1183 |     private JSType getDeclaredType(String sourceName, JSDocInfo info,
1184 |         Node lValue, @Nullable Node rValue) {
1185 |       if (info != null && info.hasType()) {
1186 |         return getDeclaredTypeInAnnotation(sourceName, lValue, info);
1187 |       } else if (rValue != null && rValue.getType() == Token.FUNCTION &&
1188 |           shouldUseFunctionLiteralType(
1189 |               (FunctionType) rValue.getJSType(), info, lValue)) {
1190 |         return rValue.getJSType();

1200 |           return createFunctionTypeFromNodes(

   * Try to fold array-length. e.g [1, 2, 3].length ==> 3, [x, y].length ==> 2
   */
Method code:
1267 |   private Node tryFoldGetProp(Node n, Node left, Node right) {
1268 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.getType() == Token.GETPROP);
1269 | 
1270 |     if (left.getType() == Token.OBJECTLIT) {
1271 |       return tryFoldObjectPropAccess(n, left, right);
1272 |     }
1273 | 
1274 |     if (right.getType() == Token.STRING &&
1275 |         right.getString().equals("length")) {
1276 |       int knownLength = -1;
1277 |       switch (left.getType()) {
1278 |         case Token.ARRAYLIT:
1279 |           if (mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
1280 |             // Nope, can't fold this, without handling the side-effects.
1281 |             return n;
1282 |           }
1283 |           knownLength = left.getChildCount();
1284 |           break;
1285 |         case Token.STRING:
1286 |           knownLength = left.getString().length();
1287 |           break;
1288 |         default:
1289 |           // Not a foldable case, forget it.
1290 |           return n;
1291 |       }
1292 | 
1293 |       Preconditions.checkState(knownLength != -1);
1294 |       Node lengthNode = Node.newNumber(knownLength);
1295 |       n.getParent().replaceChild(n, lengthNode);
1296 |       reportCodeChange();
1297 | 
1298 |       return lengthNode;
1299 |     }
1300 | 
1301 |     return n;
1302 |   }

/**
   * Look ahead for a type annotation by advancing the character stream.
   * Does not modify the token stream.
   * This is kind of a hack, and is only necessary because we use the token
   * stream to parse types, but need the underlying character stream to get

1127 |   Node parseInputs() {

1136 |       jsRoot.detachChildren();
1137 |     }
1138 |

1140 |     jsRoot = new Node(Token.BLOCK);
1141 |     jsRoot.setIsSyntheticBlock(true);

1144 |     externsRoot.setIsSyntheticBlock(true);

1151 |           options.tracer == TracerMode.ALL);
1152 |       addChangeHandler(tracker.getCodeChangeHandler());
1153 |     }
1154 | 
1155 |     Tracer tracer = newTracer("parseInputs");
1156 | 
1157 |     try {
1158 |       // Parse externs sources.
1159 |       for (CompilerInput input : externs) {
1160 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1161 |         if (hasErrors()) {
1162 |           return null;
1163 |         }
1164 |         externsRoot.addChildToBack(n);
1165 |       }
1166 | 
1167 |       // Check if the sources need to be re-ordered.
1168 |       if (options.manageClosureDependencies) {
1169 |         for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1170 |           input.setCompiler(this);
1171 | 
1172 |           // Forward-declare all the provided types, so that they
1173 |           // are not flagged even if they are dropped from the process.
1174 |           for (String provide : input.getProvides()) {
1175 |             getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(provide);
1176 |           }
1177 |         }
1178 | 
1179 |         try {
1180 |           inputs =
1181 |               (moduleGraph == null ? new JSModuleGraph(modules) : moduleGraph)
1182 |               .manageDependencies(
1183 |                   options.manageClosureDependenciesEntryPoints, inputs);
1184 |         } catch (CircularDependencyException e) {
1185 |           report(JSError.make(
1186 |               JSModule.CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY_ERROR, e.getMessage()));
1187 |           return null;
1188 |         } catch (MissingProvideException e) {
1189 |           report(JSError.make(
1190 |               MISSING_ENTRY_ERROR, e.getMessage()));
1191 |           return null;
1192 |         }
1193 |       }
1194 | 
1195 |       // Check if inputs need to be rebuilt from modules.
1196 |       boolean staleInputs = false;
1197 |       for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1198 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1199 | 
1200 |         // Inputs can have a null AST during initial parse.
1201 |         if (n == null) {
1202 |           continue;
1203 |         }
1204 | 
1205 |         if (n.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
1206 |           JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();

1224 |

1240 |             return null;
1241 |           }

/**
   * Gets the value of a node as a String, or null if it cannot be converted.
   * When it returns a non-null String, this method effectively emulates the
   * <code>String()</code> JavaScript cast function.
   */
Method code:
175 |   static String getStringValue(Node n) {
176 |     // TODO(user): regex literals as well.
177 |     switch (n.getType()) {
178 |       case Token.STRING:
179 |         return n.getString();
180 | 
181 |       case Token.NAME:
182 |         String name = n.getString();
183 |         if ("undefined".equals(name)
184 |             || "Infinity".equals(name)
185 |             || "NaN".equals(name)) {
186 |           return name;
187 |         }
188 |         break;
189 | 
190 |       case Token.NUMBER:
191 |         return getStringValue(n.getDouble());
192 | 
193 |       case Token.FALSE:
194 |       case Token.TRUE:
195 |       case Token.NULL:
196 |         return Node.tokenToName(n.getType());
197 | 
198 |       case Token.VOID:
199 |         return "undefined";
200 | 
201 |       case Token.NOT:
202 |         TernaryValue child = getPureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
203 |         if (child != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
204 |           return child.toBoolean(true) ? "false" : "true"; // reversed.
205 |         }
206 |         break;
207 | 
208 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
209 |         return arrayToString(n);
210 | 
211 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
212 |         return "[object Object]";
213 |     }
214 |     return null;
215 |   }

===== M0585 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldAssign(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java
Original range: 440-510
Documentation:

Method code:
440 |   private Node tryFoldAssign(Node n, Node left, Node right) {
441 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.getType() == Token.ASSIGN);
442 | 
443 |     // Tries to convert x = x + y -> x += y;
444 |     if (!right.hasChildren() ||
445 |         right.getFirstChild().getNext() != right.getLastChild()) {
446 |       // RHS must have two children.
447 |       return n;
448 |     }
449 | 
450 |     if (mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
451 |       return n;
452 |     }
453 | 
454 |     Node newRight;
455 |     if (areNodesEqualForInlining(left, right.getFirstChild())) {
456 |       newRight = right.getLastChild();
457 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isCommutative(right.getType()) &&
458 |           areNodesEqualForInlining(left, right.getLastChild())) {
459 |       newRight = right.getFirstChild();
460 |     } else {
461 |       return n;
462 |     }
463 | 
464 |     int newType = -1;
465 |     switch (right.getType()) {
466 |       case Token.ADD:
467 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_ADD;
468 |         break;
469 |       case Token.BITAND:
470 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_BITAND;
471 |         break;
472 |       case Token.BITOR:
473 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_BITOR;
474 |         break;
475 |       case Token.BITXOR:
476 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_BITXOR;
477 |         break;
478 |       case Token.DIV:
479 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_DIV;
480 |         break;
481 |       case Token.LSH:
482 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_LSH;
483 |         break;
484 |       case Token.MOD:
485 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_MOD;
486 |         break;
487 |       case Token.MUL:
488 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_MUL;
489 |         break;
490 |       case Token.RSH:
491 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_RSH;
492 |         break;
493 |       case Token.SUB:
494 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_SUB;
495 |         break;
496 |       case Token.URSH:
497 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_URSH;
498 |         break;
499 |       default:
500 |         return n;
501 |     }
502 | 
503 |     Node newNode = new Node(newType,
504 |         left.detachFromParent(), newRight.detachFromParent());
505 |     n.getParent().replaceChild(n, newNode);
506 | 
507 |     reportCodeChange();
508 |

510 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeCheck.visitVar(NodeTraversal,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeCheck.java
Original range: 1368-1401
Documentation:
/**
   * Visits a VAR node.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal object that supplies context, such as the
   * scope chain to use in name lookups as well as error reporting.
   * @param n The node being visited.
   */
Method code:
1368 |   private void visitVar(NodeTraversal t, Node n) {
1369 |     // TODO(nicksantos): Fix this so that the doc info always shows up
1370 |     // on the NAME node. We probably want to wait for the parser
1371 |     // merge to fix this.
1372 |     JSDocInfo varInfo = n.hasOneChild() ? n.getJSDocInfo() : null;
1373 |     for (Node name : n.children()) {
1374 |       Node value = name.getFirstChild();
1375 |       // A null var would indicate a bug in the scope creation logic.
1376 |       Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name.getString());
1377 | 
1378 |       if (value != null) {
1379 |         JSType valueType = getJSType(value);
1380 |         JSType nameType = var.getType();
1381 |         nameType = (nameType == null) ? getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE) : nameType;
1382 | 
1383 |         JSDocInfo info = name.getJSDocInfo();
1384 |         if (info == null) {
1385 |           info = varInfo;
1386 |         }
1387 |         if (info != null && info.hasEnumParameterType()) {
1388 |           // var.getType() can never be null, this would indicate a bug in the
1389 |           // scope creation logic.
1390 |           checkEnumInitializer(
1391 |               t, value,
1392 |               info.getEnumParameterType().evaluate(t.getScope(), typeRegistry));
1393 |         } else if (var.isTypeInferred()) {
1394 |           ensureTyped(t, name, valueType);
1395 |         } else {
1396 |           validator.expectCanAssignTo(
1397 |               t, value, valueType, nameType, "initializing variable");
1398 |         }
1399 |       }
1400 |     }
1401 |   }

Original range: 337-391

337 |   protected int getChar() {
338 |     if (ungetCursor != 0) {
339 |       cursor++;
340 |       --ungetCursor;
341 |       if (charno == -1) {
342 |         charno = getOffset();
343 |       }
344 |       return ungetBuffer[ungetCursor];
345 |     }
346 | 
347 |     for(;;) {
348 |       int c;
349 |       if (sourceCursor == sourceEnd) {
350 |         hitEOF = true;
351 |         if (charno == -1) {
352 |           charno = getOffset();
353 |         }
354 |         return EOF_CHAR;
355 |       }
356 |       cursor++;
357 |       c = sourceString.charAt(sourceCursor++);
358 | 
359 | 
360 |       if (lineEndChar >= 0) {
361 |         if (lineEndChar == '\r' && c == '\n') {
362 |           lineEndChar = '\n';
363 |           continue;
364 |         }
365 |         lineEndChar = -1;
366 |         lineStart = sourceCursor - 1;
367 |         lineno++;
368 |       }
369 | 
370 |       if (c <= 127) {
371 |         if (c == '\n' || c == '\r') {
372 |           lineEndChar = c;
373 |           c = '\n';
374 |         }
375 |       } else {
376 |         if (isJSFormatChar(c)) {
377 |           continue;
378 |         }
379 |         if (ScriptRuntime.isJSLineTerminator(c)) {
380 |           lineEndChar = c;
381 |           c = '\n';
382 |         }
383 |       }
384 | 
385 |       if (charno == -1) {
386 |         charno = getOffset();
387 |       }
388 | 
389 |       return c;
390 |     }
391 |   }

44 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
45 |     Node child;
46 |     switch (n.getType()) {
47 |       case Token.IF:
48 |         child = n.getFirstChild().getNext();  // skip the condition child
49 |         break;
50 |

61 |     // that's usually intentional, especially with loops.
62 |     for (; child != null; child = child.getNext()) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.FixedPointGraphTraversal.computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E>,Set<N>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/FixedPointGraphTraversal.java
Original range: 93-128

/**
   * Compute a fixed point for the given graph, entering from the given nodes.
   * @param graph The graph to traverse.
   * @param entrySet The nodes to begin traversing from.
   */
Method code:
93 |   public void computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E> graph, Set<N> entrySet) {
94 |     int cycleCount = 0;
95 |     long nodeCount = graph.getNodes().size();
96 | 
97 |     // Choose a bail-out heuristically in case the computation
98 |     // doesn't converge.
99 |     long maxIterations = Math.max(nodeCount * nodeCount * nodeCount, 100);
100 | 
101 |     // Use a LinkedHashSet, so that the traversal is deterministic.
102 |     LinkedHashSet<DiGraphNode<N, E>> workSet =
103 |         Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
104 |     for (N n : entrySet) {
105 |       workSet.add(graph.getDirectedGraphNode(n));
106 |     }
107 |     for (; !workSet.isEmpty() && cycleCount < maxIterations; cycleCount++) {
108 |       // For every out edge in the workSet, traverse that edge. If that
109 |       // edge updates the state of the graph, then add the destination
110 |       // node to the resultSet, so that we can update all of its out edges
111 |       // on the next iteration.
112 |       DiGraphNode<N, E> source = workSet.iterator().next();
113 |       N sourceValue = source.getValue();
114 | 
115 |       workSet.remove(source);
116 | 
117 |       List<DiGraphEdge<N, E>> outEdges = source.getOutEdges();
118 |       for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> edge : outEdges) {
119 |         N destNode = edge.getDestination().getValue();
120 |         if (callback.traverseEdge(sourceValue, edge.getValue(), destNode)) {
121 |           workSet.add(edge.getDestination());
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     Preconditions.checkState(cycleCount != maxIterations,
127 |         NON_HALTING_ERROR_MSG);
128 |   }

259 |   public boolean equals(Object other) {

267 |       // two possible function scopes: the real one and the BOTTOM scope.
268 |       // If they have different function scopes, we *should* iterate thru all
269 |       // the variables in each scope and compare. However, 99.9% of the time,
270 |       // they're not equal. And the other .1% of the time, we can pretend
271 |       // they're equal--this just means that data flow analysis will have
272 |       // to propagate the entry lattice a little bit further than it
273 |       // really needs to. Everything will still come out ok.
274 |       if (this.getFunctionScope() != that.getFunctionScope()) {
275 |         return false;
276 |       }

279 |         // If the two flow scopes have the same cache, then we can check
280 |         // equality a lot faster: by just looking at the "dirty" elements
281 |         // in the cache, and comparing them in both scopes.
282 |         for (String name : cache.dirtySymbols) {
283 |           if (diffSlots(getSlot(name), that.getSlot(name))) {
284 |             return false;
285 |           }
286 |         }
287 |

289 |       }

292 |       Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> otherFlowSlots = that.allFlowSlots();
293 |

295 |         if (diffSlots(slot, otherFlowSlots.get(slot.getName()))) {
296 |           return false;
297 |         }

/**
     * Determines whether a set operation is a constructor or enumeration
     * declaration. The set operation may either be an assignment to a name,
     * a variable declaration, or an object literal key mapping.
     *
     * @param n The node that represents the name being set
     * @param parent Parent node of {@code n} (an ASSIGN, VAR, or OBJLIT node)
     * @return Whether the set operation is either a constructor or enum
     *     declaration
     */
Method code:
577 |     private boolean isConstructorOrEnumDeclaration(Node n, Node parent) {
578 |       JSDocInfo info;
579 |       int valueNodeType;
580 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
581 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
582 |           info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
583 |           valueNodeType = n.getNext().getType();
584 |           break;

167 |   private JSType getClassOfMethod(Node n, Node parent) {

1444 |           Preconditions.checkState(!sourceName.isEmpty());
1445 | 
1446 |           delimiter = delimiter.replaceAll("%name%", sourceName)
1447 |             .replaceAll("%num%", String.valueOf(inputSeqNum));
1448 | 
1449 |           cb.append(delimiter)
1450 |             .append("\n");
1451 |         }
1452 |         if (root.getJSDocInfo() != null &&
1453 |             root.getJSDocInfo().getLicense() != null) {
1454 |           cb.append("/*\n")
1455 |             .append(root.getJSDocInfo().getLicense())
1456 |             .append("*/\n");
1457 |         }
1458 | 
1459 |         // If there is a valid source map, then indicate to it that the current
1460 |         // root node's mappings are offset by the given string builder buffer.
1461 |         if (options.sourceMapOutputPath != null) {
1462 |           sourceMap.setStartingPosition(
1463 |               cb.getLineIndex(), cb.getColumnIndex());
1464 |         }
1465 | 
1466 |         // if LanguageMode is ECMASCRIPT5_STRICT, only print 'use strict'
1467 |         // for the first input file
1468 |         String code = toSource(root, sourceMap, inputSeqNum == 0);
1469 |         if (!code.isEmpty()) {
1470 |           cb.append(code);
1471 | 
1472 |           // In order to avoid parse ambiguity when files are concatenated
1473 |           // together, all files should end in a semi-colon. Do a quick
1474 |           // heuristic check if there's an obvious semi-colon already there.
1475 |           int length = code.length();
1476 |           char lastChar = code.charAt(length - 1);
1477 |           char secondLastChar = length >= 2 ?
1478 |               code.charAt(length - 2) : '\0';
1479 |           boolean hasSemiColon = lastChar == ';' ||
1480 |               (lastChar == '\n' && secondLastChar == ';');
1481 |           if (!hasSemiColon) {
1482 |             cb.append(";");
1483 |           }
1484 |         }
1485 |         return null;
1486 |       }
1487 |     });
1488 |   }

640 | 
641 |       case Token.DELPROP:
642 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
643 |         add("delete ");
644 |         add(first);
645 |         break;
646 | 
647 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT: {
648 |         boolean needsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
649 |         if (needsParens) {
650 |           add("(");
651 |         }
652 |         add("{");
653 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
654 |           if (c != first) {
655 |             cc.listSeparator();
656 |           }
657 | 
658 |           if (c.getType() == Token.GET || c.getType() == Token.SET) {
659 |             add(c);
660 |           } else {
661 |             Preconditions.checkState(c.getType() == Token.STRING);
662 |             String key = c.getString();
663 |             // Object literal property names don't have to be quoted if they
664 |             // are not JavaScript keywords
665 |             if (!c.isQuotedString() &&
666 |                 !TokenStream.isKeyword(key) &&
667 |                 TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(key) &&
668 |                 // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that
669 |                 // were unicode escaped.
670 |                 NodeUtil.isLatin(key)) {
671 |               add(key);
672 |             } else {
673 |               // Determine if the string is a simple number.
674 |               double d = getSimpleNumber(key);
675 |               if (!Double.isNaN(d)) {
676 |                 cc.addNumber(d);
677 |               } else {
678 |                 addExpr(c, 1);
679 |               }
680 |             }
681 |             add(":");
682 |             addExpr(c.getFirstChild(), 1);
683 |           }
684 |         }
685 |         add("}");
686 |         if (needsParens) {
687 |           add(")");
688 |         }
689 |         break;
690 |       }
691 | 
692 |       case Token.SWITCH:
693 |         add("switch(");
694 |         add(first);
695 |         add(")");
696 |         cc.beginBlock();
697 |         addAllSiblings(first.getNext());
698 |         cc.endBlock(context == Context.STATEMENT);
699 |         break;
700 | 
701 |       case Token.CASE:
702 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
703 |         add("case ");
704 |         add(first);
705 |         addCaseBody(last);
706 |         break;
707 | 
708 |       case Token.DEFAULT:
709 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
710 |         add("default");
711 |         addCaseBody(first);
712 |         break;
713 | 
714 |       case Token.LABEL:
715 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
716 |         if (first.getType() != Token.LABEL_NAME) {
717 |           throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
718 |         }
719 |         add(first);
720 |         add(":");
721 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
722 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), true);
723 |         break;
724 | 
725 |       // This node is auto generated in anonymous functions and should just get
726 |       // ignored for our purposes.
727 |       case Token.SETNAME:
728 |         break;
729 | 
730 |       default:
731 |         throw new Error("Unknown type " + type + "\n" + n.toStringTree());
732 |     }
733 | 
734 |     cc.endSourceMapping(n);
735 |   }

/**
   * Updates the scope according to the result of a type change, like
   * an assignment or a type cast.

Method code:
494 |   private void updateScopeForTypeChange(
495 |       FlowScope scope, Node left, JSType leftType, JSType resultType) {
496 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(resultType);

502 |           assignedOuterLocalVars.put(var.getScope(), var);

===== M0790 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.UnreachableCodeElimination.tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/UnreachableCodeElimination.java
Original range: 130-179
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to remove n if an unconditional branch node (break, continue or
   * return) if the target of n is the same as the the follow of n. That is, if
   * we remove n, the control flow remains the same. Also if n targets to
   * another unconditional branch, this function will recursively try to remove
   * the target branch as well. The reason why we want to cascade this removal
   * is because we only run this pass once. If we have code such as
   *
   * break -> break -> break
   *
   * where all 3 break's are useless. The order of removal matters. When we
   * first look at the first break, we see that it branches to the 2nd break.
   * However, if we remove the last break, the 2nd break becomes useless and
   * finally the first break becomes useless as well.
   *
   * @return The target of this jump. If the target is also useless jump,
   *     the target of that useless jump recursively.
   */
Method code:
130 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
131 |   private Node tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node n) {
132 |     /*
133 |      * For each of the unconditional branching control flow node, check to see
134 |      * if the ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode of that node is same as
135 |      * the branching target. If it is, the branch node is safe to be removed.
136 |      *
137 |      * This is not as clever as MinimizeExitPoints because it doesn't do any
138 |      * if-else conversion but it handles more complicated switch statements
139 |      * much nicer.
140 |      */
141 | 
142 |     // If n is null the target is the end of the function, nothing to do.
143 |     if (n == null) {
144 |        return n;
145 |     }
146 | 
147 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = curCfg.getDirectedGraphNode(n);
148 | 
149 |     if (gNode == null) {
150 |       return n;
151 |     }
152 | 
153 |     switch (n.getType()) {
154 |       case Token.RETURN:
155 |         if (n.hasChildren()) {
156 |           break;
157 |         }
158 |       case Token.BREAK:
159 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
160 | 
161 |         // We are looking for a control flow changing statement that always
162 |         // branches to the same node. If removing it the control flow still
163 |         // branches to that same node. It is safe to remove it.
164 |         List<DiGraphEdge<Node,Branch>> outEdges = gNode.getOutEdges();
165 |         if (outEdges.size() == 1 &&
166 |             // If there is a next node, there is no chance this jump is useless.
167 |             (n.getNext() == null || n.getNext().getType() == Token.FUNCTION)) {
168 | 
169 |           Preconditions.checkState(outEdges.get(0).getValue() == Branch.UNCOND);
170 |           Node fallThrough = computeFollowing(n);
171 |           Node nextCfgNode = outEdges.get(0).getDestination().getValue();
172 |           if (nextCfgNode == fallThrough) {
173 |             removeDeadExprStatementSafely(n);
174 |             return fallThrough;
175 |           }
176 |         }
177 |     }
178 |     return n;
179 |   }

785 |       // Remove calls to inheritance-defining functions where the unreferenced
786 |       // class is the subclass.
787 |       for (Node exprCallNode : inheritsCalls.get(var)) {
788 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(exprCallNode.getParent(), exprCallNode);
789 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
790 |       }
791 | 
792 |       // Regardless of what happens to the original declaration,
793 |       // we need to remove all assigns, because they may contain references
794 |       // to other unreferenced variables.
795 |       removeAllAssigns(var);
796 | 
797 |       compiler.addToDebugLog("Unreferenced var: " + var.name);
798 |       Node nameNode = var.nameNode;
799 |       Node toRemove = nameNode.getParent();
800 |       Node parent = toRemove.getParent();
801 | 
802 |       Preconditions.checkState(
803 |           toRemove.getType() == Token.VAR ||
804 |           toRemove.getType() == Token.FUNCTION ||
805 |           toRemove.getType() == Token.LP &&
806 |           parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION,
807 |           "We should only declare vars and functions and function args");
808 | 
809 |       if (toRemove.getType() == Token.LP &&
810 |           parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
811 |         // Don't remove function arguments here. That's a special case
812 |         // that's taken care of in removeUnreferencedFunctionArgs.
813 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(toRemove)) {
814 |         if (!preserveFunctionExpressionNames) {
815 |           toRemove.getFirstChild().setString("");
816 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
817 |         }
818 |         // Don't remove bleeding functions.
819 |       } else if (parent != null &&
820 |           parent.getType() == Token.FOR &&
821 |           parent.getChildCount() < 4) {
822 |         // foreach iterations have 3 children. Leave them alone.
823 |       } else if (toRemove.getType() == Token.VAR &&
824 |           nameNode.hasChildren() &&
825 |           NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(nameNode.getFirstChild())) {
826 |         // If this is a single var declaration, we can at least remove the
827 |         // declaration itself and just leave the value, e.g.,
828 |         // var a = foo(); => foo();
829 |         if (toRemove.getChildCount() == 1) {
830 |           parent.replaceChild(toRemove,
831 |               new Node(Token.EXPR_RESULT, nameNode.removeFirstChild()));
832 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
833 |         }
834 |       } else if (toRemove.getType() == Token.VAR &&
835 |           toRemove.getChildCount() > 1) {
836 |         // For var declarations with multiple names (i.e. var a, b, c),
837 |         // only remove the unreferenced name
838 |         toRemove.removeChild(nameNode);
839 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
840 |       } else if (parent != null) {
841 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(parent, toRemove);
842 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
843 |       }
844 |     }
845 |   }

/**
   * Determines whether we know enough about the given value to be able
   * to collapse it into subsequent expressions.
   *
   * For example, we can collapse booleans and variable names:
   * <code>
   * x = 3; y = x; // y = x = 3;
   * a = true; b = true; // b = a = true;
   * <code>
   * But we won't try to collapse complex expressions.
   *
   * @param value The value node.
   * @param isLValue Whether it's on the left-hand side of an expr.
   */
Method code:
76 |   private boolean isCollapsibleValue(Node value, boolean isLValue) {
77 |     switch (value.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.GETPROP:
79 |         // Do not collapse GETPROPs on arbitrary objects, because
80 |         // they may be implemented  setter functions, and oftentimes
81 |         // setter functions fail on native objects. This is ok for "THIS"
82 |         // objects, because we assume that they are non-native.
83 |         return !isLValue || value.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.THIS;
84 | 
85 |       case Token.NAME:
86 |         return true;
87 | 
88 |       default:
89 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value);
90 |     }
91 |   }

/**
   * Enforces type casts, and ensures the node is typed.
   *
   * A cast in the way that we use it in JSDoc annotations never
   * alters the generated code and therefore never can induce any runtime
   * operation. What this means is that a 'cast' is really just a compile
   * time constraint on the underlying value. In the future, we may add
   * support for run-time casts for compiled tests.
   *
   * To ensure some shred of sanity, we enforce the notion that the
   * type you are casting to may only meaningfully be a narrower type
   * than the underlying declared type. We also invalidate optimizations
   * on bad type casts.
   *
   * @param t The traversal object needed to report errors.
   * @param n The node getting a type assigned to it.
   * @param type The type to be assigned.
   */
Method code:
1860 |   private void ensureTyped(NodeTraversal t, Node n, JSType type) {
1861 |     // Make sure FUNCTION nodes always get function type.
1862 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getType() != Token.FUNCTION ||
1863 |             type instanceof FunctionType ||
1864 |             type.isUnknownType());
1865 |     JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
1866 |     if (info != null) {
1867 |       if (info.hasType()) {
1868 |         JSType infoType = info.getType().evaluate(t.getScope(), typeRegistry);
1869 |         validator.expectCanCast(t, n, infoType, type);
1870 |         type = infoType;
1871 |       }
1872 | 
1873 |       if (info.isImplicitCast() && !inExterns) {
1874 |         String propName = n.getType() == Token.GETPROP ?
1875 |             n.getLastChild().getString() : "(missing)";
1876 |         compiler.report(
1877 |             t.makeError(n, ILLEGAL_IMPLICIT_CAST, propName));
1878 |       }
1879 |     }
1880 | 
1881 |     if (n.getJSType() == null) {
1882 |       n.setJSType(type);
1883 |     }
1884 |   }

/**
   * Tries apply our various peephole minimizations on the passed in node.
   */
Method code:
74 |   @Override
75 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
76 |   public Node optimizeSubtree(Node node) {
77 |     switch(node.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.RETURN: {
79 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
80 |         if (result != node) {
81 |           return result;
82 |         }
83 |         result = tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
84 |         if (result != node) {
85 |           return result;
86 |         }
87 |         return tryReduceReturn(node);
88 |       }
89 | 
90 |       case Token.THROW: {
91 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
92 |         if (result != node) {
93 |           return result;
94 |         }
95 |         return tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
96 |       }
97 | 
98 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Maybe remove redundant BREAK and CONTINUE. Overlaps
99 |       // with MinimizeExitPoints.
100 | 
101 |       case Token.NOT:
102 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
103 |         return tryMinimizeNot(node);
104 | 
105 |       case Token.IF:
106 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
107 |         return tryMinimizeIf(node);
108 | 
109 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
110 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
111 |         return node;
112 | 
113 |       case Token.HOOK:
114 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
115 |         return node;
116 | 
117 |       case Token.WHILE:
118 |       case Token.DO:
119 |         tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
120 |         return node;
121 | 
122 |       case Token.FOR:
123 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(node)) {
124 |           tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
125 |         }
126 |         return node;
127 | 
128 | 
129 |       case Token.TRUE:
130 |       case Token.FALSE:
131 |         return reduceTrueFalse(node);
132 | 
133 |       case Token.NEW:
134 |         node = tryFoldStandardConstructors(node);
135 |         if (node.getType() != Token.CALL) {
136 |           return node;
137 |         }
138 |         // Fall through on purpose because tryFoldStandardConstructors() may
139 |         // convert a NEW node into a CALL node
140 |       case Token.CALL:
141 |         Node result =  tryFoldLiteralConstructor(node);
142 |         if (result == node) {
143 |           result = tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(node);
144 |         }
145 |         return result;
146 | 
147 |       case Token.COMMA:
148 |         return tryFoldComma(node);
149 | 
150 |       case Token.NAME:
151 |         return tryReplaceUndefined(node);
152 | 
153 |       case Token.BLOCK:
154 |         return tryReplaceIf(node);
155 | 
156 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
157 |         return tryMinimizeArrayLiteral(node);
158 | 
159 |       default:
160 |         return node; //Nothing changed
161 |     }

330 |         compiler.report(
331 |             t.makeError(n, NON_GLOBAL_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, ""));
332 |       }
333 | 
334 |       if (lvalueToRemoveLater == n) {
335 |         lvalueToRemoveLater = null;
336 |         if (n.getType() == Token.ASSIGN) {
337 |           Node last = n.getLastChild();
338 |           n.removeChild(last);
339 |           parent.replaceChild(n, last);
340 |         } else {
341 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getType() == Token.NAME);
342 |           n.removeChild(n.getFirstChild());
343 |         }
344 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
345 |       }
346 | 
347 |       if (n.getType() == Token.CALL) {
348 |         if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
349 |           // If there's a function call in the global scope,
350 |           // we just say it's unsafe and freeze all the defines.
351 |           //
352 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): We could be a lot smarter here. For example,
353 |           // ReplaceOverriddenVars keeps a call graph of all functions and
354 |           // which functions/variables that they reference, and tries
355 |           // to statically determine which functions are "safe" and which
356 |           // are not. But this would be overkill, expecially because
357 |           // the intended use of defines is with config_files, where
358 |           // all the defines are at the top of the bundle.
359 |           for (DefineInfo info : assignableDefines.values()) {
360 |             setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
361 |           }
362 | 
363 |           assignableDefines.clear();
364 |         }
365 |       }
366 | 
367 |       updateAssignAllowedStack(n, false);
368 |     }

470 |   private void traverseFunction(Node n, Node parent) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

134 |   @Override
135 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
136 |     if (colorings.isEmpty() || !NodeUtil.isName(n) ||
137 |         NodeUtil.isFunction(parent)) {
138 |       // Don't rename named functions.
139 |       return;
140 |     }
141 |     Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
142 |     GraphNode<Var, ?> vNode = colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(var);
143 |     if (vNode == null) {
144 |       // This is not a local.
145 |       return;
146 |     }
147 |     Var coalescedVar = colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(var);
148 | 
149 |     if (!usePseudoNames) {
150 |       if (vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar)) {
151 |         // The coalesced name is itself, nothing to do.
152 |         return;
153 |       }
154 | 
155 |       // Rename.
156 |       n.setString(coalescedVar.name);
157 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
158 | 
159 |       if (NodeUtil.isVar(parent)) {
160 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
161 |       }
162 |     } else {
163 |       // This code block is slow but since usePseudoName is for debugging,
164 |       // we should not sacrifice performance for non-debugging compilation to
165 |       // make this fast.
166 |       String pseudoName = null;
167 |       Set<String> allMergedNames = Sets.newTreeSet();
168 |       for (Iterator<Var> i = t.getScope().getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
169 |         Var iVar = i.next();
170 | 
171 |         // Look for all the variables that can be merged (in the graph by now)
172 |         // and it is merged with the current coalscedVar.
173 |         if (colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(iVar) != null &&
174 |             coalescedVar.equals(colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(iVar))) {
175 |           allMergedNames.add(iVar.name);
176 |         }
177 |       }
178 | 
179 |       // Keep its original name.
180 |       if (allMergedNames.size() == 1) {
181 |         return;
182 |       }
183 | 
184 |       pseudoName = Joiner.on("_").join(allMergedNames);
185 | 
186 |       while (t.getScope().isDeclared(pseudoName, true)) {
187 |         pseudoName += "$";
188 |       }
189 | 
190 |       n.setString(pseudoName);
191 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
192 | 
193 |       if (!vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar) && NodeUtil.isVar(parent)) {
194 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
195 |       }
196 |     }

131 |           traversal.getAliasDefinitions().size() > 0 ||

===== M0872 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.traverseNode(Node,Node,Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 190-294
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses everything in the current scope and marks variables that
   * are referenced.
   *
   * During traversal, we identify subtrees that will only be
   * referenced if their enclosing variables are referenced. Instead of
   * traversing those subtrees, we create a continuation for them,
   * and traverse them lazily.
   */
Method code:
190 |   private void traverseNode(Node n, Node parent, Scope scope) {
191 |     int type = n.getType();
192 |     Var var = null;
193 |     switch (type) {
194 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
195 |         // If this function is a removable var, then create a continuation
196 |         // for it instead of traversing immediately.
197 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
198 |           var = scope.getVar(n.getFirstChild().getString());
199 |         }
200 | 
201 |         if (var != null && isRemovableVar(var)) {
202 |           continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
203 |         } else {
204 |           traverseFunction(n, scope);
205 |         }
206 |         return;
207 | 
208 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
209 |         Assign maybeAssign = Assign.maybeCreateAssign(n);
210 |         if (maybeAssign != null) {
211 |           // Put this in the assign map. It might count as a reference,
212 |           // but we won't know that until we have an index of all assigns.
213 |           var = scope.getVar(maybeAssign.nameNode.getString());
214 |           if (var != null) {
215 |             assignsByVar.put(var, maybeAssign);
216 |             assignsByNode.put(maybeAssign.nameNode, maybeAssign);
217 | 
218 |             if (isRemovableVar(var) &&
219 |                 !maybeAssign.mayHaveSecondarySideEffects) {
220 |               // If the var is unreferenced and performing this assign has
221 |               // no secondary side effects, then we can create a continuation
222 |               // for it instead of traversing immediately.
223 |               continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
224 |               return;
225 |             }
226 |           }
227 |         }
228 |         break;
229 | 
230 |       case Token.CALL:
231 |         // Look for calls to inheritance-defining calls (such as goog.inherits).
232 |         SubclassRelationship subclassRelationship =
233 |             codingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(n);
234 |         if (subclassRelationship != null) {
235 |           Var subclassVar = scope.getVar(subclassRelationship.subclassName);
236 |           // Don't try to track the inheritance calls for non-globals. It would
237 |           // be more correct to only not track when the subclass does not
238 |           // reference a constructor, but checking that it is a global is
239 |           // easier and mostly the same.
240 |           if (subclassVar != null && subclassVar.isGlobal()
241 |               && !referenced.contains(subclassVar)) {
242 |             // Save a reference to the EXPR node.
243 |             inheritsCalls.put(subclassVar, parent);
244 |             continuations.put(subclassVar, new Continuation(n, scope));
245 |             return;
246 |           }
247 |         }
248 |         break;
249 | 
250 |       case Token.NAME:
251 |         var = scope.getVar(n.getString());
252 |         if (parent.getType() == Token.VAR) {
253 |           Node value = n.getFirstChild();
254 |           if (value != null && var != null && isRemovableVar(var) &&
255 |               !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(value)) {
256 |             // If the var is unreferenced and creating its value has no side
257 |             // effects, then we can create a continuation for it instead
258 |             // of traversing immediately.
259 |             continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
260 |             return;
261 |           }
262 |         } else {
263 | 
264 |           // If arguments is escaped, we just assume the worst and continue
265 |           // on all the parameters.
266 |           if ("arguments".equals(n.getString()) && scope.isLocal()) {
267 |             Node lp = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
268 |             for (Node a = lp.getFirstChild(); a != null; a = a.getNext()) {
269 |               markReferencedVar(scope.getVar(a.getString()));
270 |             }
271 |           }
272 | 
273 |           // All name references that aren't declarations or assigns
274 |           // are references to other vars.
275 |           if (var != null) {
276 |             // If that var hasn't already been marked referenced, then
277 |             // start tracking it.  If this is an assign, do nothing
278 |             // for now.
279 |             if (isRemovableVar(var)) {
280 |               if (!assignsByNode.containsKey(n)) {
281 |                 markReferencedVar(var);
282 |               }
283 |             } else {
284 |               markReferencedVar(var);
285 |             }
286 |           }
287 |         }
288 |         break;
289 |     }
290 | 
291 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
292 |       traverseNode(c, n, scope);
293 |     }
294 |   }

/**
   * Given a constructor type and a property name, check that the property has
   * the JSDoc annotation @override iff the property is declared on a

1027 |       NodeTraversal t, Node n, FunctionType ctorType, String propertyName,
1028 |       JSDocInfo info, JSType propertyType) {
1029 |     // If the supertype doesn't resolve correctly, we've warned about this
1030 |     // already.
1031 |     if (hasUnknownOrEmptySupertype(ctorType)) {
1032 |       return;
1033 |     }
1034 | 
1035 |     FunctionType superClass = ctorType.getSuperClassConstructor();
1036 |     boolean superClassHasProperty = superClass != null &&
1037 |         superClass.getPrototype().hasProperty(propertyName);
1038 |     // For interface
1039 |     boolean superInterfacesHasProperty = false;
1040 |     if (ctorType.isInterface()) {
1041 |       for (ObjectType interfaceType : ctorType.getExtendedInterfaces()) {
1042 |         superInterfacesHasProperty =
1043 |           superInterfacesHasProperty || interfaceType.hasProperty(propertyName);
1044 |       }
1045 |     }
1046 |     boolean declaredOverride = info != null && info.isOverride();
1047 | 
1048 |     boolean foundInterfaceProperty = false;
1049 |     if (ctorType.isConstructor()) {
1050 |       for (JSType implementedInterface :
1051 |           ctorType.getAllImplementedInterfaces()) {
1052 |         if (implementedInterface.isUnknownType() ||
1053 |             implementedInterface.isEmptyType()) {
1054 |           continue;
1055 |         }
1056 |         FunctionType interfaceType =
1057 |             implementedInterface.toObjectType().getConstructor();
1058 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(interfaceType);
1059 |         boolean interfaceHasProperty =
1060 |             interfaceType.getPrototype().hasProperty(propertyName);
1061 |         foundInterfaceProperty = foundInterfaceProperty || interfaceHasProperty;
1062 |         if (reportMissingOverride.isOn() && !declaredOverride &&
1063 |             interfaceHasProperty) {
1064 |           // @override not present, but the property does override an interface
1065 |           // property
1066 |           compiler.report(t.makeError(n, reportMissingOverride,
1067 |               HIDDEN_INTERFACE_PROPERTY, propertyName,
1068 |               interfaceType.getTopMostDefiningType(propertyName).toString()));
1069 |         }
1070 |       }
1071 |     }
1072 | 
1073 |     if (!declaredOverride && !superClassHasProperty
1074 |         && !superInterfacesHasProperty) {
1075 |       // nothing to do here, it's just a plain new property
1076 |       return;
1077 |     }
1078 | 
1079 |     JSType topInstanceType = superClassHasProperty ?
1080 |         superClass.getTopMostDefiningType(propertyName) : null;
1081 |     if (reportMissingOverride.isOn() && ctorType.isConstructor() &&
1082 |         !declaredOverride && superClassHasProperty) {
1083 |       // @override not present, but the property does override a superclass
1084 |       // property
1085 |       compiler.report(t.makeError(n, reportMissingOverride,
1086 |           HIDDEN_SUPERCLASS_PROPERTY, propertyName,
1087 |           topInstanceType.toString()));
1088 |     }
1089 |     if (!declaredOverride) {
1090 |       // there's no @override to check
1091 |       return;
1092 |     }
1093 |     // @override is present and we have to check that it is ok
1094 |     if (superClassHasProperty) {
1095 |       // there is a superclass implementation
1096 |       JSType superClassPropType =

1101 |                 propertyName, topInstanceType.toString(),
1102 |                 superClassPropType.toString(), propertyType.toString()));
1103 |       }
1104 |     } else if (superInterfacesHasProperty) {
1105 |       // there is an super interface property
1106 |       for (ObjectType interfaceType : ctorType.getExtendedInterfaces()) {
1107 |         if (interfaceType.hasProperty(propertyName)) {

1115 |                     propertyName, topInstanceType.toString(),
1116 |                     superPropertyType.toString(),
1117 |                     propertyType.toString()));
1118 |           }
1119 |         }
1120 |       }
1121 |     } else if (!foundInterfaceProperty) {
1122 |       // there is no superclass nor interface implementation
1123 |       compiler.report(
1124 |           t.makeError(n, UNKNOWN_OVERRIDE,
1125 |               propertyName, ctorType.getInstanceType().toString()));
1126 |     }
1127 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.moveNamedFunctions(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 577-609
Documentation:
/**
     * Move all the functions that are valid at the execution of the first
     * statement of the function to the beginning of the function definition.
     */
Method code:
577 |     private void moveNamedFunctions(Node functionBody) {
578 |       Preconditions.checkState(
579 |           functionBody.getParent().getType() == Token.FUNCTION);
580 |       Node previous = null;
581 |       Node current = functionBody.getFirstChild();
582 |       // Skip any declarations at the beginning of the function body, they
583 |       // are already in the right place.
584 |       while (current != null && NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(current)) {
585 |         previous = current;
586 |         current = current.getNext();
587 |       }
588 | 
589 |       // Find any remaining declarations and move them.
590 |       Node insertAfter = previous;
591 |       while (current != null) {
592 |         // Save off the next node as the current node maybe removed.
593 |         Node next = current.getNext();
594 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(current)) {
595 |           // Remove the declaration from the body.
596 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(previous);
597 |           functionBody.removeChildAfter(previous);
598 | 
599 |           // Readd the function at the top of the function body (after any
600 |           // previous declarations).
601 |           insertAfter = addToFront(functionBody, current, insertAfter);
602 |           reportCodeChange("Move function declaration not at top of function");
603 |         } else {
604 |           // Update the previous only if the current node hasn't been moved.
605 |           previous = current;
606 |         }
607 |         current = next;
608 |       }
609 |     }

/**
     * For all variables in this scope, see if they are only used once.
     * If it looks safe to do so, inline them.
     */
Method code:
196 |     private void doInlinesForScope(NodeTraversal t, ReferenceMap referenceMap) {
197 | 
198 |       boolean maybeModifiedArguments =
199 |           maybeEscapedOrModifiedArguments(t.getScope(), referenceMap);
200 |       for (Iterator<Var> it = t.getScope().getVars(); it.hasNext();) {
201 |         Var v = it.next();

204 | 
205 |         // referenceInfo will be null if we're in constants-only mode
206 |         // and the variable is not a constant.
207 |         if (referenceInfo == null || isVarInlineForbidden(v)) {
208 |           // Never try to inline exported variables or variables that

217 |           // If we're in constants-only mode, don't run more aggressive
218 |           // inlining heuristics. See InlineConstantsTest.
219 |           continue;
220 |         } else {

222 |         }

===== M0959 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessClosurePrimitives.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessClosurePrimitives.java
Original range: 169-260
Documentation:

Method code:
169 |   @Override
170 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
171 |     switch (n.getType()) {
172 |       case Token.CALL:
173 |         boolean isExpr = parent.getType() == Token.EXPR_RESULT;
174 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
175 |         if (left.getType() == Token.GETPROP) {
176 |           Node name = left.getFirstChild();
177 |           if (name.getType() == Token.NAME &&
178 |               GOOG.equals(name.getString())) {
179 |             // For the sake of simplicity, we report code changes
180 |             // when we see a provides/requires, and don't worry about
181 |             // reporting the change when we actually do the replacement.
182 |             String methodName = name.getNext().getString();
183 |             if ("base".equals(methodName)) {
184 |               processBaseClassCall(t, n);
185 |             } else if (!isExpr) {
186 |               // All other methods must be called in an EXPR.
187 |               break;
188 |             } else if ("require".equals(methodName)) {
189 |               processRequireCall(t, n, parent);
190 |             } else if ("provide".equals(methodName)) {
191 |               processProvideCall(t, n, parent);
192 |             } else if ("exportSymbol".equals(methodName)) {
193 |               Node arg = left.getNext();
194 |               if (arg.getType() == Token.STRING) {
195 |                 int dot = arg.getString().indexOf('.');
196 |                 if (dot == -1) {
197 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString());
198 |                 } else {
199 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString().substring(0, dot));
200 |                 }
201 |               }
202 |             } else if ("addDependency".equals(methodName)) {
203 |               CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
204 |               List<String> typeDecls =
205 |                   convention.identifyTypeDeclarationCall(n);
206 |               if (typeDecls != null) {
207 |                 for (String typeDecl : typeDecls) {
208 |                   compiler.getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(typeDecl);
209 |                 }
210 |               }
211 | 
212 |               // We can't modify parent, so just create a node that will
213 |               // get compiled out.
214 |               parent.replaceChild(n, Node.newNumber(0));
215 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
216 |             } else if ("setCssNameMapping".equals(methodName)) {
217 |               processSetCssNameMapping(t, n, parent);
218 |             }
219 |           }
220 |         }
221 |         break;
222 | 
223 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
224 |       case Token.NAME:
225 |         // If this is an assignment to a provided name, remove the provided
226 |         // object.
227 |         handleCandidateProvideDefinition(t, n, parent);
228 |         break;
229 | 
230 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
231 |         handleTypedefDefinition(t, n, parent);
232 |         break;
233 | 
234 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
235 |         // If this is a declaration of a provided named function, this is an
236 |         // error. Hosited functions will explode if the're provided.
237 |         if (t.inGlobalScope() &&
238 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
239 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
240 |           ProvidedName pn = providedNames.get(name);
241 |           if (pn != null) {
242 |             compiler.report(t.makeError(n, FUNCTION_NAMESPACE_ERROR, name));
243 |           }
244 |         }
245 |         break;
246 | 
247 |       case Token.NEW:
248 |         trySimplifyNewDate(t, n, parent);
249 |         break;
250 | 
251 |       case Token.GETPROP:
252 |         if (n.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.NAME &&
253 |             parent.getType() != Token.CALL &&
254 |             parent.getType() != Token.ASSIGN &&
255 |             "goog.base".equals(n.getQualifiedName())) {
256 |           reportBadBaseClassUse(t, n, "May only be called directly.");
257 |         }
258 |         break;
259 |     }
260 |   }

===== M0984 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.assignNames(Set<Assignment>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 441-511
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines which new names to substitute for the original names.
   */
Method code:
441 |   private void assignNames(Set<Assignment> varsToRename) {
442 |     NameGenerator globalNameGenerator =
443 |         new NameGenerator(reservedNames, prefix, reservedCharacters);
444 | 
445 |     // Local variables never need a prefix.
446 |     NameGenerator localNameGenerator =
447 |         prefix.isEmpty() ? globalNameGenerator : new NameGenerator(
448 |             reservedNames, "", reservedCharacters);
449 | 
450 |     // Generated names and the assignments for non-local vars.
451 |     List<Assignment> pendingAssignments = new ArrayList<Assignment>();
452 |     List<String> generatedNamesForAssignments = new ArrayList<String>();
453 | 
454 |     for (Assignment a : varsToRename) {
455 |       if (a.newName != null) {
456 |         continue;
457 |       }
458 | 
459 |       if (externNames.contains(a.oldName)) {
460 |         continue;
461 |       }
462 | 
463 |       String newName;
464 |       if (a.oldName.startsWith(LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX)) {
465 |         // For local variable, we make the assignment right away.
466 |         newName = localNameGenerator.generateNextName();
467 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, newName);
468 |       } else {
469 |         // For non-local variable, delay finalizing the name assignment
470 |         // until we know how many new names we'll have of length 2, 3, etc.
471 |         newName = globalNameGenerator.generateNextName();
472 |         pendingAssignments.add(a);
473 |         generatedNamesForAssignments.add(newName);
474 |       }
475 |       reservedNames.add(newName);
476 |     }
477 | 
478 |     // Now that we have a list of generated names, and a list of variable
479 |     // Assignment objects, we assign the generated names to the vars as
480 |     // follows:
481 |     // 1) The most frequent vars get the shorter names.
482 |     // 2) If N number of vars are going to be assigned names of the same
483 |     //    length, we assign the N names based on the order at which the vars
484 |     //    first appear in the source. This makes the output somewhat less
485 |     //    random, because symbols declared close together are assigned names
486 |     //    that are quite similar. With this heuristic, the output is more
487 |     //    compressible.
488 |     //    For instance, the output may look like:
489 |     //    var da = "..", ea = "..";
490 |     //    function fa() { .. } function ga() { .. }
491 | 
492 |     int numPendingAssignments = generatedNamesForAssignments.size();
493 |     for (int i = 0; i < numPendingAssignments;) {
494 |       SortedSet<Assignment> varsByOrderOfOccurrence =
495 |           new TreeSet<Assignment>(ORDER_OF_OCCURRENCE_COMPARATOR);
496 | 
497 |       // Add k number of Assignment to the set, where k is the number of
498 |       // generated names of the same length.
499 |       int len = generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i).length();
500 |       for (int j = i; j < numPendingAssignments
501 |           && generatedNamesForAssignments.get(j).length() == len; j++) {
502 |         varsByOrderOfOccurrence.add(pendingAssignments.get(j));
503 |       }
504 | 
505 |       // Now, make the assignments
506 |       for (Assignment a : varsByOrderOfOccurrence) {
507 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i));
508 |         ++i;
509 |       }
510 |     }
511 |   }

/**
     * If this is an assign to a variable or its property, return it.
     * Otherwise, return null.
     */
Method code:
910 |     static Assign maybeCreateAssign(Node assignNode) {
911 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(assignNode));
912 | 
913 |       // Skip one level of GETPROPs or GETELEMs.
914 |       //
915 |       // Don't skip more than one level, because then we get into
916 |       // situations where assigns to properties of properties will always
917 |       // trigger side-effects, and the variable they're on cannot be removed.
918 |       boolean isPropAssign = false;
919 |       Node current = assignNode.getFirstChild();
920 |       if (NodeUtil.isGet(current)) {
921 |         current = current.getFirstChild();
922 |         isPropAssign = true;
923 | 
924 |         if (current.getType() == Token.GETPROP &&
925 |             current.getLastChild().getString().equals("prototype")) {
926 |           // Prototype properties sets should be considered like normal
927 |           // property sets.
928 |           current = current.getFirstChild();
929 |         }
930 |       }
931 | 
932 |       if (current.getType() == Token.NAME) {
933 |         return new Assign(assignNode, current, isPropAssign);
934 |       }
935 |       return null;
936 |     }
