===== M1014 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MustBeReachingVariableDef.computeMustDef(Node,Node,MustDef,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MustBeReachingVariableDef.java
Original range: 222-315
Documentation:
/**
   * @param n The node in question.
   * @param cfgNode The node to add
   * @param conditional true if the definition is not always executed.
   */
Method code:
222 |   private void computeMustDef(
223 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, MustDef output, boolean conditional) {
224 |     switch (n.getType()) {
225 | 
226 |       case Token.BLOCK:
227 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
228 |         return;
229 | 
230 |       case Token.WHILE:
231 |       case Token.DO:
232 |       case Token.IF:
233 |         computeMustDef(
234 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
235 |         return;
236 | 
237 |       case Token.FOR:
238 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
239 |           computeMustDef(
240 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
241 |         } else {
242 |           // for(x in y) {...}
243 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
244 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
245 |           if (NodeUtil.isVar(lhs)) {
246 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
247 |           }
248 |           if (NodeUtil.isName(lhs)) {
249 |             addToDefIfLocal(lhs.getString(), cfgNode, rhs, output);
250 |           }
251 |         }
252 |         return;
253 | 
254 |       case Token.AND:
255 |       case Token.OR:
256 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
257 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
258 |         return;
259 | 
260 |       case Token.HOOK:
261 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
262 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
263 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
264 |         return;
265 | 
266 |       case Token.VAR:
267 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
268 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
269 |             computeMustDef(c.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
270 |             addToDefIfLocal(c.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
271 |                 c.getFirstChild(), output);
272 |           }
273 |         }
274 |         return;
275 | 
276 |       default:
277 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n)) {
278 |           if (NodeUtil.isName(n.getFirstChild())) {
279 |             Node name = n.getFirstChild();
280 |             computeMustDef(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
281 |             addToDefIfLocal(name.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
282 |               n.getLastChild(), output);
283 |             return;
284 |           } else if (NodeUtil.isGet(n.getFirstChild())) {
285 |             // Treat all assignments to arguments as redefining the
286 |             // parameters itself.
287 |             Node obj = n.getFirstChild().getFirstChild();
288 |             if (NodeUtil.isName(obj) && "arguments".equals(obj.getString())) {
289 |               // TODO(user): More accuracy can be introduced
290 |               // ie: We know exactly what arguments[x] is if x is a constant
291 |               // number.
292 |               escapeParameters(output);
293 |             }
294 |           }
295 |         }
296 | 
297 |         if (NodeUtil.isName(n) && "arguments".equals(n.getString())) {
298 |           escapeParameters(output);
299 |         }
300 | 
301 |         // DEC and INC actually defines the variable.
302 |         if (n.getType() == Token.DEC || n.getType() == Token.INC) {
303 |           Node target = n.getFirstChild();
304 |           if (NodeUtil.isName(target)) {
305 |             addToDefIfLocal(target.getString(),
306 |                 conditional ? null : cfgNode, null, output);
307 |             return;
308 |           }
309 |         }
310 | 
311 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
312 |           computeMustDef(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
313 |         }
314 |     }
315 |   }

===== M1024 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 682-779
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
682 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
683 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
684 |     /*
685 |      * This is the case where:
686 |      *
687 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
688 |      * the script.
689 |      *
690 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
691 |      * the caller of the function.
692 |      *
693 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
694 |      * back to the caller of the function.
695 |      *
696 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
697 |      * asked to traverse.
698 |      *
699 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
700 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
701 |      */
702 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
703 |     if (parent == null || parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION ||
704 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
705 |       return null;
706 |     }
707 | 
708 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
709 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
710 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
711 |       case Token.IF:
712 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
713 |       case Token.CASE:
714 |       case Token.DEFAULT:
715 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
716 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
717 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
718 |           if (parent.getNext().getType() == Token.CASE) {
719 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
720 |           } else if (parent.getNext().getType() == Token.DEFAULT) {
721 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
722 |           } else {
723 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
724 |           }
725 |         } else {
726 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
727 |         }
728 |         break;
729 |       case Token.FOR:
730 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
731 |           return parent;
732 |         } else {
733 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
734 |         }
735 |       case Token.WHILE:
736 |       case Token.DO:
737 |         return parent;
738 |       case Token.TRY:
739 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
740 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
741 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
742 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
743 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
744 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
745 |           }
746 |         // CATCH block.
747 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
748 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
749 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
750 |           } else {
751 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
752 |           }
753 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
754 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
755 |           if (cfa != null) {
756 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
757 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.UNCOND, finallyNode);
758 |             }
759 |           }
760 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
761 |         }
762 |     }
763 | 
764 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
765 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
766 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
767 | 
768 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
769 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
770 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
771 |     }
772 | 
773 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
774 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
775 |     } else {
776 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transfered up the AST.
777 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
778 |     }
779 |   }

/**
     * Split a var node such as:
     *   var a, b;
     * into individual statements:
     *   var a;
     *   var b;
     * @param n The whose children we should inspect.
     */
Method code:
553 |     private void splitVarDeclarations(Node n) {
554 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
555 |         next = c.getNext();
556 |         if (c.getType() == Token.VAR) {
557 |           if (assertOnChange && !c.hasChildren()) {
558 |             throw new IllegalStateException("Empty VAR node.");
559 |           }

565 |                 Token.VAR, name, n.getLineno(), n.getCharno());
566 |             n.addChildBefore(newVar, c);
567 |             reportCodeChange("VAR with multiple children");
568 |           }
569 |         }
570 |       }
571 |     }

     * @param name The {@link Token#NAME} node.
     * @param var The parent of the {@code name} node, which must be a
     *     {@link Token#VAR} node.

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.joinInputs(DiGraphNode<N, Branch>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 286-324
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the new flow state at a given node's entry by merging the
   * output (input) lattice of the node's predecessor (successor).
   *
   * @param node Node to compute new join.
   */
Method code:
286 |   protected void joinInputs(DiGraphNode<N, Branch> node) {
287 |     FlowState<L> state = node.getAnnotation();
288 |     if (isForward()) {
289 |       if (cfg.getEntry() == node) {
290 |         state.setIn(createEntryLattice());
291 |       } else {
292 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> inNodes = cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(node);
293 |         if (inNodes.size() == 1) {
294 |           FlowState<L> inNodeState = inNodes.get(0).getAnnotation();
295 |           state.setIn(inNodeState.getOut());
296 |         } else if (inNodes.size() > 1) {
297 |           List<L> values = new ArrayList<L>(inNodes.size());
298 |           for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> currentNode : inNodes) {
299 |             FlowState<L> currentNodeState = currentNode.getAnnotation();
300 |             values.add(currentNodeState.getOut());
301 |           }
302 |           state.setIn(joinOp.apply(values));
303 |         }
304 |       }
305 |     } else {
306 |       List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> inNodes = cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(node);
307 |       if (inNodes.size() == 1) {
308 |         DiGraphNode<N, Branch> inNode = inNodes.get(0);
309 |         if (inNode == cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
310 |           state.setOut(createEntryLattice());
311 |         } else {
312 |           FlowState<L> inNodeState = inNode.getAnnotation();
313 |           state.setOut(inNodeState.getIn());
314 |         }
315 |       } else if (inNodes.size() > 1) {
316 |         List<L> values = new ArrayList<L>(inNodes.size());
317 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> currentNode : inNodes) {
318 |           FlowState<L> currentNodeState = currentNode.getAnnotation();
319 |           values.add(currentNodeState.getIn());
320 |         }
321 |         state.setOut(joinOp.apply(values));
322 |       }
323 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FunctionTypeBuilder.getOrCreateConstructor()

Original range: 693-729

/**
   * Returns a constructor function either by returning it from the
   * registry if it exists or creating and registering a new type. If
   * there is already a type, then warn if the existing type is
   * different than the one we are creating, though still return the
   * existing function if possible.  The primary purpose of this is
   * that registering a constructor will fail for all built-in types
   * that are initialized in {@link JSTypeRegistry}.  We a) want to
   * make sure that the type information specified in the externs file
   * matches what is in the registry and b) annotate the externs with
   * the {@link JSType} from the registry so that there are not two
   * separate JSType objects for one type.
   */
Method code:
693 |   private FunctionType getOrCreateConstructor() {
694 |     FunctionType fnType = typeRegistry.createConstructorType(
695 |         fnName, sourceNode, parametersNode, returnType);
696 |     JSType existingType = typeRegistry.getType(fnName);
697 | 
698 |     if (existingType != null) {
699 |       boolean isInstanceObject = existingType instanceof InstanceObjectType;
700 |       if (isInstanceObject || fnName.equals("Function")) {
701 |         FunctionType existingFn =
702 |             isInstanceObject ?
703 |             ((InstanceObjectType) existingType).getConstructor() :
704 |             typeRegistry.getNativeFunctionType(FUNCTION_FUNCTION_TYPE);
705 | 
706 |         if (existingFn.getSource() == null) {
707 |           existingFn.setSource(sourceNode);
708 |         }
709 | 
710 |         if (!existingFn.hasEqualCallType(fnType)) {
711 |           reportWarning(TYPE_REDEFINITION, fnName,
712 |               fnType.toString(), existingFn.toString());
713 |         }
714 | 
715 |         return existingFn;
716 |       } else {
717 |         // We fall through and return the created type, even though it will fail
718 |         // to register. We have no choice as we have to return a function. We
719 |         // issue an error elsewhere though, so the user should fix it.
720 |       }
721 |     }
722 | 
723 |     maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
724 | 
725 |     if (getScopeDeclaredIn().isGlobal() && !fnName.isEmpty()) {
726 |       typeRegistry.declareType(fnName, fnType.getInstanceType());
727 |     }
728 |     return fnType;
729 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SyntacticScopeCreator.java
Original range: 117-170
Documentation:
/**
   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node
   */
Method code:
117 |   private void scanVars(Node n, Node parent) {
118 |     switch (n.getType()) {
119 |       case Token.VAR:
120 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
121 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
122 |              child != null;) {
123 |           Node next = child.getNext();
124 |           declareVar(child);
125 |           child = next;
126 |         }
127 |         return;
128 | 
129 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
130 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
131 |           return;
132 |         }
133 | 
134 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
135 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
136 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
137 |           return;
138 |         }
139 |         declareVar(n.getFirstChild());
140 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
141 | 
142 |       case Token.CATCH:
143 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
144 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.NAME);
145 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
146 |         // is the code block
147 | 
148 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
149 |         final Node block = var.getNext();
150 | 
151 |         declareVar(var);
152 |         scanVars(block, n);
153 |         return;  // only one child to scan
154 | 
155 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
156 |         sourceName = n.getSourceFileName();
157 |         break;
158 |     }
159 | 
160 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
161 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
162 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
163 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
164 |            child != null;) {
165 |         Node next = child.getNext();
166 |         scanVars(child, n);
167 |         child = next;
168 |       }
169 |     }
170 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VarCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Original range: 126-213

126 |   @Override
127 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
128 |     if (n.getType() != Token.NAME) {
129 |       return;
130 |     }
131 | 
132 |     String varName = n.getString();
133 | 
134 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
135 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
136 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunction(parent));
137 | 
138 |       // A function declaration with an empty name passes Rhino,
139 |       // but is supposed to be a syntax error according to the spec.
140 |       if (!NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
141 |         t.report(n, INVALID_FUNCTION_DECL);
142 |       }
143 |       return;
144 |     }
145 | 
146 |     // Check if this is a declaration for a var that has been declared
147 |     // elsewhere. If so, mark it as a duplicate.
148 |     if ((parent.getType() == Token.VAR ||
149 |          NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent)) &&
150 |         varsToDeclareInExterns.contains(varName)) {
151 |       createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
152 | 
153 |       n.addSuppression("duplicate");
154 |     }
155 | 
156 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
157 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
158 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
159 |     if (var == null) {
160 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
161 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
162 |         // current scope.
163 |       } else {
164 |         // The extern checks are stricter, don't report a second error.
165 |         if (!strictExternCheck || !t.getInput().isExtern()) {
166 |           t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
167 |         }
168 | 
169 |         if (sanityCheck) {
170 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
171 |         } else {
172 |           createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
173 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, n,
174 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
175 |         }
176 |       }
177 |       return;
178 |     }
179 | 
180 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
181 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
182 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
183 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
184 |       return;
185 |     }
186 | 
187 |     // Check module dependencies.
188 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
189 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
190 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
191 |     if (varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
192 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
193 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
194 |       } else {
195 |         if (!sanityCheck && scope.isGlobal()) {
196 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
197 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
198 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
199 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
200 |           } else {
201 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
202 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
203 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
204 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
205 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
206 |           }
207 |         } else {

210 |         }
211 |       }
212 |     }
213 |   }

   * A function is a subtype of another if their call methods are related via
   * subtyping and {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that} with regard to
   * the prototype chain.
   */

832 |   @Override
833 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {

845 |         return false;
846 |       }
847 |       // If functionA is a subtype of functionB, then their "this" types
848 |       // should be contravariant. However, this causes problems because
849 |       // of the way we enforce overrides. Because function(this:SubFoo)
850 |       // is not a subtype of function(this:Foo), our override check treats
851 |       // this as an error. It also screws up out standard method
852 |       // for aliasing constructors. Let's punt on all this for now.
853 |       // TODO(nicksantos): fix this.
854 |       FunctionType other = (FunctionType) that;
855 |       boolean treatThisTypesAsCovariant =
856 |         // If either one of these is a ctor, skip 'this' checking.
857 |         this.isConstructor() || other.isConstructor() ||
858 | 
859 |         // An interface 'this'-type is non-restrictive.
860 |         // In practical terms, if C implements I, and I has a method m,
861 |         // then any m doesn't necessarily have to C#m's 'this'
862 |         // type doesn't need to match I.
863 |         (other.typeOfThis.getConstructor() != null &&
864 |              other.typeOfThis.getConstructor().isInterface()) ||
865 | 
866 |         // If one of the 'this' types is covariant of the other,
867 |         // then we'll treat them as covariant (see comment above).
868 |         other.typeOfThis.isSubtype(this.typeOfThis) ||
869 |         this.typeOfThis.isSubtype(other.typeOfThis);
870 |       return treatThisTypesAsCovariant && this.call.isSubtype(other.call);
871 |     }
872 | 
873 |     return getNativeType(JSTypeNative.FUNCTION_PROTOTYPE).isSubtype(that);
874 |   }

   * each one.
   * @return A map of {@link DefineInfo} structures, keyed by name.
   */
Method code:
171 |   private Map<String, DefineInfo> collectDefines(Node root,
172 |       GlobalNamespace namespace) {
173 |     // Find all the global names with a @define annotation
174 |     List<Name> allDefines = Lists.newArrayList();
175 |     for (Name name : namespace.getNameIndex().values()) {
176 |       Ref decl = name.getDeclaration();
177 |       if (name.docInfo != null && name.docInfo.isDefine()) {
178 |         // Process defines should not depend on check types being enabled,
179 |         // so we look for the JSDoc instead of the inferred type.
180 |         if (isValidDefineType(name.docInfo.getType())) {

182 |         } else {

186 |           compiler.report(error);
187 |         }

200 |             info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
201 |           }
202 |

204 |             allDefines.add(name);
205 |             break;
206 |           }
207 |         }

209 |     }

128 |     // It is important that removeDuplicateDeclarations runs after
129 |     // MakeDeclaredNamesUnique in order for catch block exception names to be
130 |     // handled properly. Specifically, catch block exception names are

===== M1129 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ExploitAssigns.collapseAssignEqualTo(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ExploitAssigns.java
Original range: 108-199
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse the given assign expression into the expression directly
   * following it, if possible.
   *
   * @param expr The expression that may be moved.
   * @param exprParent The parent of {@code expr}.
   * @param value The value of this expression, expressed as a node. Each
   *     expression may have multiple values, so this function may be called
   *     multiple times for the same expression. For example,
   *     <code>
   *     a = true;
   *     </code>
   *     is equal to the name "a" and the boolean "true".
   * @return Whether the expression was collapsed succesfully.
   */
Method code:
108 |   private boolean collapseAssignEqualTo(Node expr, Node exprParent,
109 |       Node value) {
110 |     Node assign = expr.getFirstChild();
111 |     Node parent = exprParent;
112 |     Node next = expr.getNext();
113 |     while (next != null) {
114 |       switch (next.getType()) {
115 |         case Token.AND:
116 |         case Token.OR:
117 |         case Token.HOOK:
118 |         case Token.IF:
119 |         case Token.RETURN:
120 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
121 |           // Dive down the left side
122 |           parent = next;
123 |           next = next.getFirstChild();
124 |           break;
125 | 
126 |         case Token.VAR:
127 |           if (next.getFirstChild().hasChildren()) {
128 |             parent = next.getFirstChild();
129 |             next = parent.getFirstChild();
130 |             break;
131 |           }
132 |           return false;
133 | 
134 |         case Token.GETPROP:
135 |         case Token.NAME:
136 |           if (next.isQualifiedName()) {
137 |             String nextName = next.getQualifiedName();
138 |             if (value.isQualifiedName() &&
139 |                 nextName.equals(value.getQualifiedName())) {
140 |               // If the previous expression evaluates to value of a
141 |               // qualified name, and that qualified name is used again
142 |               // shortly, then we can exploit the assign here.
143 | 
144 |               // Verify the assignment doesn't change its own value.
145 |               if (!isSafeReplacement(next, assign)) {
146 |                 return false;
147 |               }
148 | 
149 |               exprParent.removeChild(expr);
150 |               expr.removeChild(assign);
151 |               parent.replaceChild(next, assign);
152 |               return true;
153 |             }
154 |           }
155 |           return false;
156 | 
157 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
158 |           // Assigns are really tricky. In lots of cases, we want to inline
159 |           // into the right side of the assign. But the left side of the
160 |           // assign is evaluated first, and it may have convoluted logic:
161 |           //   a = null;
162 |           //   (a = b).c = null;
163 |           // We don't want to exploit the first assign. Similarly:
164 |           //   a.b = null;
165 |           //   a.b.c = null;
166 |           // We don't want to exploit the first assign either.
167 |           //
168 |           // To protect against this, we simply only inline when the left side
169 |           // is guaranteed to evaluate to the same L-value no matter what.
170 |           Node leftSide = next.getFirstChild();
171 |           if (leftSide.getType() == Token.NAME ||
172 |               leftSide.getType() == Token.GETPROP &&
173 |               leftSide.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.THIS) {
174 |             // Dive down the right side of the assign.
175 |             parent = next;
176 |             next = leftSide.getNext();
177 |             break;
178 |           } else {
179 |             return false;
180 |           }
181 | 
182 |         default:
183 |           if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(next)
184 |               && next.isEquivalentTo(value)) {
185 |             // If the r-value of the expr assign is an immutable value,
186 |             // and the value is used again shortly, then we can exploit
187 |             // the assign here.
188 |             exprParent.removeChild(expr);
189 |             expr.removeChild(assign);
190 |             parent.replaceChild(next, assign);
191 |             return true;
192 |           }
193 |           // Return without inlining a thing
194 |           return false;
195 |       }
196 |     }
197 | 
198 |     return false;
199 |   }

   * Since this pass reports errors only when a global {@code this} keyword

   * The least supertype is the join (&#8744;) or supremum of both types in the
   * type lattice.<p>
   * Examples:
   * <ul>
   * <li>{@code number &#8744; *} = {@code *}</li>
   * <li>{@code number &#8744; Object} = {@code (number, Object)}</li>
   * <li>{@code Number &#8744; Object} = {@code Object}</li>
   * </ul>
   * @return {@code this &#8744; that}
   */
Method code:
581 |   public JSType getLeastSupertype(JSType that) {
582 |     if (that.isUnionType()) {
583 |       // Union types have their own implementation of getLeastSupertype.
584 |       return that.getLeastSupertype(this);
585 |     }
586 |     return getLeastSupertype(this, that);
587 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.filterNoResolvedType(JSType)

Documentation:
/**
   * When computing infimums, we may get a situation like
   * inf(Type1, Type2)
   * where both types are unresolved, so they're technically
   * subtypes of one another.
   *
   * If this happens, filter them down to NoResolvedType.
   */
Method code:
668 |   static JSType filterNoResolvedType(JSType type) {
669 |     if (type.isNoResolvedType()) {
670 |       // inf(UnresolvedType1, UnresolvedType2) needs to resolve
671 |       // to the base unresolved type, so that the relation is symmetric.
672 |       return type.getNativeType(JSTypeNative.NO_RESOLVED_TYPE);
673 |     } else if (type instanceof UnionType) {
674 |       UnionType unionType = (UnionType) type;
675 |       boolean needsFiltering = false;
676 |       for (JSType alt : unionType.getAlternates()) {
677 |         if (alt.isNoResolvedType()) {
678 |           needsFiltering = true;
679 |           break;
680 |         }
681 |       }
682 | 
683 |       if (needsFiltering) {
684 |         UnionTypeBuilder builder = new UnionTypeBuilder(type.registry);
685 |         for (JSType alt : unionType.getAlternates()) {
686 |           if (!alt.isNoResolvedType()) {
687 |             builder.addAlternate(alt);
688 |           }
689 |         }
690 |         return builder.build();
691 |       }
692 |     }
693 |     return type;
694 |   }

Original range: 417-510

/**
   * Determines whether the given property is visible in the current context.
   * @param t The current traversal.
   * @param getprop The getprop node.
   */
Method code:
417 |   private void checkPropertyVisibility(NodeTraversal t,
418 |       Node getprop, Node parent) {
419 |     ObjectType objectType =
420 |         ObjectType.cast(dereference(getprop.getFirstChild().getJSType()));
421 |     String propertyName = getprop.getLastChild().getString();
422 | 
423 |     if (objectType != null) {
424 |       // Is this a normal property access, or are we trying to override
425 |       // an existing property?
426 |       boolean isOverride = parent.getJSDocInfo() != null &&
427 |           parent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN &&
428 |           parent.getFirstChild() == getprop;
429 | 
430 |       // Find the lowest property defined on a class with visibility
431 |       // information.
432 |       if (isOverride) {
433 |         objectType = objectType.getImplicitPrototype();
434 |       }
435 |       JSDocInfo docInfo = null;
436 |       for (; objectType != null;
437 |            objectType = objectType.getImplicitPrototype()) {
438 |         docInfo = objectType.getOwnPropertyJSDocInfo(propertyName);
439 |         if (docInfo != null &&
440 |             docInfo.getVisibility() != Visibility.INHERITED) {
441 |           break;
442 |         }
443 |       }
444 | 
445 |       if (objectType == null) {
446 |         // We couldn't find a visibility modifier; assume it's public.
447 |         return;
448 |       }
449 | 
450 |       boolean sameInput =
451 |           t.getInput().getName().equals(docInfo.getSourceName());
452 |       Visibility visibility = docInfo.getVisibility();
453 |       JSType ownerType = normalizeClassType(objectType);
454 |       if (isOverride) {
455 |         // Check an ASSIGN statement that's trying to override a property
456 |         // on a superclass.
457 |         JSDocInfo overridingInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
458 |         Visibility overridingVisibility = overridingInfo == null ?
459 |             Visibility.INHERITED : overridingInfo.getVisibility();
460 | 
461 |         // Check that (a) the property *can* be overridden, and
462 |         // (b) that the visibility of the override is the same as the
463 |         // visibility of the original property.
464 |         if (visibility == Visibility.PRIVATE && !sameInput) {
465 |           compiler.report(
466 |               t.makeError(getprop, PRIVATE_OVERRIDE,
467 |                   objectType.toString()));
468 |         } else if (overridingVisibility != Visibility.INHERITED &&
469 |             overridingVisibility != visibility) {
470 |           compiler.report(
471 |               t.makeError(getprop, VISIBILITY_MISMATCH,
472 |                   visibility.name(), objectType.toString(),
473 |                   overridingVisibility.name()));
474 |         }
475 |       } else {
476 |         if (sameInput) {
477 |           // private access is always allowed in the same file.
478 |           return;
479 |         } else if (visibility == Visibility.PRIVATE &&
480 |             (currentClass == null || ownerType.differsFrom(currentClass))) {
481 |           if (docInfo.isConstructor() &&
482 |               isValidPrivateConstructorAccess(parent)) {
483 |             return;
484 |           }
485 | 
486 |           // private access is not allowed outside the file from a different
487 |           // enclosing class.
488 |           compiler.report(
489 |               t.makeError(getprop,
490 |                   BAD_PRIVATE_PROPERTY_ACCESS,
491 |                   propertyName,
492 |                   validator.getReadableJSTypeName(
493 |                       getprop.getFirstChild(), true)));
494 |         } else if (visibility == Visibility.PROTECTED) {
495 |           // There are 3 types of legal accesses of a protected property:
496 |           // 1) Accesses in the same file
497 |           // 2) Overriding the property in a subclass
498 |           // 3) Accessing the property from inside a subclass
499 |           // The first two have already been checked for.
500 |           if (currentClass == null || !currentClass.isSubtype(ownerType)) {
501 |             compiler.report(
502 |                 t.makeError(getprop,  BAD_PROTECTED_PROPERTY_ACCESS,
503 |                     propertyName,
504 |                     validator.getReadableJSTypeName(
505 |                         getprop.getFirstChild(), true)));
506 |           }
507 |         }
508 |       }
509 |     }
510 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CheckSideEffects.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CheckSideEffects.java
Original range: 47-123
Documentation:

Method code:
47 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
48 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.
49 |     // I've been unable to think of any cases where this indicates a bug,
50 |     // and apparently some people like keeping these semicolons around,
51 |     // so we'll allow it.
52 |     if (n.getType() == Token.EMPTY ||
53 |         n.getType() == Token.COMMA) {
54 |       return;
55 |     }
56 | 
57 |     if (parent == null)
58 |       return;
59 | 
60 |     int pt = parent.getType();
61 |     if (pt == Token.COMMA) {
62 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
63 |       if (gramps.getType() == Token.CALL &&
64 |           parent == gramps.getFirstChild()) {
65 |         // Semantically, a direct call to eval is different from an indirect
66 |         // call to an eval. See Ecma-262 S15.1.2.1. So it's ok for the first
67 |         // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
68 |         // an eval.
69 |         if (n == parent.getFirstChild() &&
70 |             parent.getChildCount() == 2 &&
71 |             n.getNext().getType() == Token.NAME &&
72 |             "eval".equals(n.getNext().getString())) {
73 |           return;
74 |         }
75 |       }
76 | 
77 |       if (n == parent.getLastChild()) {
78 |         for (Node an : parent.getAncestors()) {
79 |           int ancestorType = an.getType();
80 |           if (ancestorType == Token.COMMA)
81 |             continue;
82 |           if (ancestorType != Token.EXPR_RESULT &&
83 |               ancestorType != Token.BLOCK)
84 |             return;
85 |           else
86 |             break;
87 |         }
88 |       }
89 |     } else if (pt != Token.EXPR_RESULT && pt != Token.BLOCK) {
90 |       if (pt == Token.FOR && parent.getChildCount() == 4 &&
91 |           (n == parent.getFirstChild() ||
92 |            n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext())) {
93 |         // Fall through and look for warnings for the 1st and 3rd child
94 |         // of a for.
95 |       } else {
96 |         return;  // it might be ok to not have a side-effect
97 |       }
98 |     }
99 | 
100 |     boolean isSimpleOp = NodeUtil.isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType());
101 |     if (isSimpleOp ||
102 |         !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(n, t.getCompiler())) {
103 |       if (n.isQualifiedName() && n.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
104 |         // This no-op statement was there so that JSDoc information could
105 |         // be attached to the name. This check should not complain about it.
106 |         return;
107 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(n)) {
108 |         // we already reported the problem when we visited the child.
109 |         return;
110 |       }
111 | 
112 |       String msg = "This code lacks side-effects. Is there a bug?";
113 |       if (n.getType() == Token.STRING) {
114 |         msg = "Is there a missing '+' on the previous line?";
115 |       } else if (isSimpleOp) {
116 |         msg = "The result of the '" + Node.tokenToName(n.getType()) +
117 |             "' operator is not being used.";
118 |       }
119 | 
120 |       t.getCompiler().report(
121 |           t.makeError(n, level, USELESS_CODE_ERROR, msg));
122 |     }
123 |   }

===== M1224 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.BasicErrorManager.LeveledJSErrorComparator.compare(ErrorWithLevel,ErrorWithLevel)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/BasicErrorManager.java
Original range: 120-170
Documentation:

Method code:
120 |     public int compare(ErrorWithLevel p1, ErrorWithLevel p2) {
121 |       // null is the smallest value
122 |       if (p2 == null) {
123 |         if (p1 == null) {
124 |           return 0;
125 |         } else {
126 |           return P1_GT_P2;
127 |         }
128 |       }
129 | 
130 |       // check level
131 |       if (p1.level != p2.level) {
132 |         return p2.level.compareTo(p1.level);
133 |       }
134 | 
135 |       // sourceName comparison
136 |       String source1 = p1.error.sourceName;
137 |       String source2 = p2.error.sourceName;
138 |       if (source1 != null && source2 != null) {
139 |         int sourceCompare = source1.compareTo(source2);
140 |         if (sourceCompare != 0) {
141 |           return sourceCompare;
142 |         }
143 |       } else if (source1 == null && source2 != null) {
144 |         return P1_LT_P2;
145 |       } else if (source1 != null && source2 == null) {
146 |         return P1_GT_P2;
147 |       }
148 |       // lineno comparison
149 |       int lineno1 = p1.error.lineNumber;
150 |       int lineno2 = p2.error.lineNumber;
151 |       if (lineno1 != lineno2) {
152 |         return lineno1 - lineno2;
153 |       } else if (lineno1 < 0 && 0 <= lineno2) {
154 |         return P1_LT_P2;
155 |       } else if (0 <= lineno1 && lineno2 < 0) {
156 |         return P1_GT_P2;
157 |       }
158 |       // charno comparison
159 |       int charno1 = p1.error.getCharno();
160 |       int charno2 = p2.error.getCharno();
161 |       if (charno1 != charno2) {
162 |         return charno1 - charno2;
163 |       } else if (charno1 < 0 && 0 <= charno2) {
164 |         return P1_LT_P2;
165 |       } else if (0 <= charno1 && charno2 < 0) {
166 |         return P1_GT_P2;
167 |       }
168 |       // description
169 |       return p1.error.description.compareTo(p2.error.description);
170 |     }

154 | 
155 |       case Token.BLOCK:
156 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
157 |         return;
158 | 
159 |       case Token.NAME:
160 |         addToUseIfLocal(n.getString(), cfgNode, output);
161 |         return;
162 | 
163 |       case Token.WHILE:
164 |       case Token.DO:
165 |       case Token.IF:
166 |         computeMayUse(
167 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
168 |         return;
169 | 
170 |       case Token.FOR:
171 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
172 |           computeMayUse(
173 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
174 |         } else {
175 |           // for(x in y) {...}
176 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
177 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
178 |           if (NodeUtil.isVar(lhs)) {
179 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
180 |           }
181 |           if (NodeUtil.isName(lhs) && !conditional) {
182 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(lhs.getString(), output);
183 |           }
184 |           computeMayUse(rhs, cfgNode, output, conditional);
185 |         }
186 |         return;
187 | 
188 |       case Token.AND:
189 |       case Token.OR:
190 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
191 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
192 |         return;
193 | 
194 |       case Token.HOOK:
195 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
196 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
197 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
198 |         return;
199 | 
200 |       case Token.VAR:
201 |         Node varName = n.getFirstChild();
202 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasChildren(), "AST should be normalized");
203 | 
204 |         if (varName.hasChildren()) {
205 |           computeMayUse(varName.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
206 |           if (!conditional) {
207 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(varName.getString(), output);
208 |           }
209 |         }
210 |         return;
211 | 
212 |       default:
213 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isName(n.getFirstChild())) {
214 |           Node name = n.getFirstChild();
215 |           if (!conditional) {
216 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(name.getString(), output);
217 |           }
218 | 
219 |           // In case of a += "Hello". There is a read of a.
220 |           if (!NodeUtil.isAssign(n)) {
221 |             addToUseIfLocal(name.getString(), cfgNode, output);
222 |           }
223 | 
224 |           computeMayUse(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
225 |         } else {
226 |           /*
227 |            * We want to traverse in reverse order because we want the LAST
228 |            * definition in the sub-tree....
229 |            * But we have no better way to traverse in reverse other :'(
230 |            */
231 |           for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getChildBefore(c)) {
232 |             computeMayUse(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
233 |           }
234 |         }
235 |     }
236 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.extractForInitializer(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 496-543
Documentation:
/**
     * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
     * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
     * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
     * shouldTraverse).
     *
     * @param n The node to inspect.
     * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
     * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
     *     will be inserted.
     */
Method code:
496 |     private void extractForInitializer(
497 |         Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
498 | 
499 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
500 |         next = c.getNext();
501 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
502 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
503 |         switch (c.getType()) {
504 |           case Token.LABEL:
505 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
506 |             break;
507 |           case Token.FOR:
508 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
509 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
510 |               if (first.getType() == Token.VAR) {
511 |                 // Transform:
512 |                 //    for (var a = 1 in b) {}
513 |                 // to:
514 |                 //    var a = 1; for (a in b) {};
515 |                 Node newStatement = first;
516 |                 // Clone just the node, to remove any initialization.
517 |                 Node name = newStatement.getFirstChild().cloneNode();
518 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
519 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
520 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
521 |               }
522 |             } else if (c.getFirstChild().getType() != Token.EMPTY) {
523 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
524 |               Node empty = new Node(Token.EMPTY);
525 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
526 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
527 | 
528 |               Node newStatement;
529 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
530 |               // but are handled differently.
531 |               if (init.getType() == Token.VAR) {
532 |                 newStatement = init;
533 |               } else {
534 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
535 |               }
536 | 
537 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
538 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
539 |             }
540 |             break;
541 |         }
542 |       }
543 |     }

===== M1246 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MinimizeExitPoints.tryMinimizeExits(Node,int,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MinimizeExitPoints.java
Original range: 113-204
Documentation:
/**
   * Attempts to minimize the number of explicit exit points in a control
   * structure to take advantage of the implied exit at the end of the
   * structure.  This is accomplished by removing redundant statements, and
   * moving statements following a qualifying IF node into that node.
   * For example:
   *
   * function () {
   *   if (x) return;
   *   else blah();
   *   foo();
   * }
   *
   * becomes:
   *
   * function () {
   *  if (x) ;
   *  else {
   *    blah();
   *    foo();
   *  }
   *
   * @param n The execution node of a parent to inspect.
   * @param exitType The type of exit to look for.
   * @param labelName If parent is a label the name of the label to look for,
   *   null otherwise.
   * @nullable labelName non-null only for breaks within labels.
   */
Method code:
113 |   void tryMinimizeExits(Node n, int exitType, String labelName) {
114 | 
115 |     // Just an 'exit'.
116 |     if (matchingExitNode(n, exitType, labelName)) {
117 |       NodeUtil.removeChild(n.getParent(), n);
118 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
119 |       return;
120 |     }
121 | 
122 |     // Just an 'if'.
123 |     if (n.getType() == Token.IF) {
124 |       Node ifBlock = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
125 |       tryMinimizeExits(ifBlock, exitType, labelName);
126 |       Node elseBlock = ifBlock.getNext();
127 |       if (elseBlock != null) {
128 |         tryMinimizeExits(elseBlock, exitType, labelName);
129 |       }
130 |       return;
131 |     }
132 | 
133 |     // Just a 'try/catch/finally'.
134 |     if (n.getType() == Token.TRY) {
135 |       Node tryBlock = n.getFirstChild();
136 |       tryMinimizeExits(tryBlock, exitType, labelName);
137 |       Node allCatchNodes = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(n);
138 |       if (NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(allCatchNodes)) {
139 |         Preconditions.checkState(allCatchNodes.hasOneChild());
140 |         Node catchNode = allCatchNodes.getFirstChild();
141 |         Node catchCodeBlock = catchNode.getLastChild();
142 |         tryMinimizeExits(catchCodeBlock, exitType, labelName);
143 |       }
144 |       if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(n)) {
145 |         Node finallyBlock = n.getLastChild();
146 |         tryMinimizeExits(finallyBlock, exitType, labelName);
147 |       }
148 |     }
149 | 
150 |     // Just a 'label'.
151 |     if (n.getType() == Token.LABEL) {
152 |       Node labelBlock = n.getLastChild();
153 |       tryMinimizeExits(labelBlock, exitType, labelName);
154 |     }
155 | 
156 |     // TODO(johnlenz): The last case of SWITCH statement?
157 | 
158 |     // The rest assumes a block with at least one child, bail on anything else.
159 |     if (n.getType() != Token.BLOCK || n.getLastChild() == null) {
160 |       return;
161 |     }
162 | 
163 |     // Multiple if-exits can be converted in a single pass.
164 |     // Convert "if (blah) break;  if (blah2) break; other_stmt;" to
165 |     // become "if (blah); else { if (blah2); else { other_stmt; } }"
166 |     // which will get converted to "if (!blah && !blah2) { other_stmt; }".
167 |     for (Node c : n.children()) {
168 | 
169 |       // An 'if' block to process below.
170 |       if (c.getType() == Token.IF) {
171 |         Node ifTree = c;
172 |         Node trueBlock, falseBlock;
173 | 
174 |         // First, the true condition block.
175 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
176 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
177 |         tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(trueBlock, falseBlock,
178 |             ifTree, exitType, labelName);
179 | 
180 |         // Now the else block.
181 |         // The if blocks may have changed, get them again.
182 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
183 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
184 |         if (falseBlock != null) {
185 |           tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(falseBlock, trueBlock,
186 |               ifTree, exitType, labelName);
187 |         }
188 |       }
189 | 
190 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
191 |         break;
192 |       }
193 |     }
194 | 
195 |     // Now try to minimize the exits of the last child, if it is removed
196 |     // look at what has become the last child.
197 |     for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getLastChild()) {
198 |       tryMinimizeExits(c, exitType, labelName);
199 |       // If the node is still the last child, we are done.
200 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
201 |         break;

===== M1266 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getValueType(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 508-530
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the type of a value or simple expression.
     *
     * @param n An rvalue in an assignment or variable declaration (not null)
     * @return A {@link Name.Type}
     */
Method code:
508 |     Name.Type getValueType(Node n) {
509 |       switch (n.getType()) {
510 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
511 |           return Name.Type.OBJECTLIT;
512 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
513 |           return Name.Type.FUNCTION;
514 |         case Token.OR:
515 |           // Recurse on the second value. If the first value were an object
516 |           // literal or function, then the OR would be meaningless and the
517 |           // second value would be dead code. Assume that if the second value
518 |           // is an object literal or function, then the first value will also
519 |           // evaluate to one when it doesn't evaluate to false.
520 |           return getValueType(n.getLastChild());
521 |         case Token.HOOK:
522 |           // The same line of reasoning used for the OR case applies here.
523 |           Node second = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
524 |           Name.Type t = getValueType(second);
525 |           if (t != Name.Type.OTHER) return t;
526 |           Node third = second.getNext();
527 |           return getValueType(third);
528 |       }
529 |       return Name.Type.OTHER;
530 |     }

     * Declare the symbol for a qualified name in the global scope.
     *

     * @param n A top-level GETPROP node (it should not be contained inside
     *     another GETPROP).

     * @param rhsValue The node that {@code n} is being initialized to,
     *     or {@code null} if this is a stub declaration.
     */
Method code:
1350 |     void maybeDeclareQualifiedName(NodeTraversal t, JSDocInfo info,
1351 |         Node n, Node parent, Node rhsValue) {
1352 |       Node ownerNode = n.getFirstChild();
1353 |       String ownerName = ownerNode.getQualifiedName();
1354 |       String qName = n.getQualifiedName();
1355 |       String propName = n.getLastChild().getString();
1356 |       Preconditions.checkArgument(qName != null && ownerName != null);
1357 | 
1358 |       // Function prototypes are special.
1359 |       // It's a common JS idiom to do:
1360 |       // F.prototype = { ... };
1361 |       // So if F does not have an explicitly declared super type,
1362 |       // allow F.prototype to be redefined arbitrarily.
1363 |       if ("prototype".equals(propName)) {
1364 |         Var qVar = scope.getVar(qName);
1365 |         if (qVar != null) {
1366 |           if (!qVar.isTypeInferred()) {
1367 |             // Just ignore assigns to declared prototypes.
1368 |             return;
1369 |           }
1370 |           if (qVar.getScope() == scope) {
1371 |             scope.undeclare(qVar);
1372 |           }
1373 |         }
1374 |       }
1375 | 
1376 |       // Precedence of type information on GETPROPs:
1377 |       // 1) @type annnotation / @enum annotation
1378 |       // 2) ASSIGN to FUNCTION literal
1379 |       // 3) @param/@return annotation (with no function literal)
1380 |       // 4) ASSIGN to something marked @const
1381 |       // 5) ASSIGN to anything else
1382 |       //
1383 |       // 1, 3, and 4 are declarations, 5 is inferred, and 2 is a declaration iff
1384 |       // the function has jsdoc or has not been declared before.
1385 |       //
1386 |       // FUNCTION literals are special because TypedScopeCreator is very smart
1387 |       // about getting as much type information as possible for them.
1388 | 
1389 |       // Determining type for #1 + #2 + #3 + #4
1390 |       JSType valueType = getDeclaredType(t.getSourceName(), info, n, rhsValue);
1391 |       if (valueType == null && rhsValue != null) {
1392 |         // Determining type for #5
1393 |         valueType = rhsValue.getJSType();
1394 |       }
1395 | 
1396 |       if (valueType == null) {
1397 |         if (parent.getType() == Token.EXPR_RESULT) {
1398 |           stubDeclarations.add(new StubDeclaration(
1399 |               n,
1400 |               t.getInput() != null && t.getInput().isExtern(),
1401 |               ownerName));
1402 |         }
1403 | 
1404 |         return;
1405 |       }
1406 | 
1407 |       boolean inferred = true;
1408 |       if (info != null) {
1409 |         // Determining declaration for #1 + #3 + #4
1410 |         inferred = !(info.hasType()
1411 |             || info.hasEnumParameterType()
1412 |             || (info.isConstant() && valueType != null
1413 |                 && !valueType.isUnknownType())
1414 |             || FunctionTypeBuilder.isFunctionTypeDeclaration(info));
1415 |       }
1416 | 
1417 |       if (inferred) {
1418 |         // Determining declaration for #2
1419 |         inferred = !(rhsValue != null &&
1420 |             rhsValue.getType() == Token.FUNCTION &&
1421 |             (info != null || !scope.isDeclared(qName, false)));
1422 |       }
1423 | 
1424 |       if (!inferred) {
1425 |         ObjectType ownerType = getObjectSlot(ownerName);
1426 |         if (ownerType != null) {
1427 |           // Only declare this as an official property if it has not been
1428 |           // declared yet.
1429 |           boolean isExtern = t.getInput() != null && t.getInput().isExtern();
1430 |           if ((!ownerType.hasOwnProperty(propName) ||
1431 |                ownerType.isPropertyTypeInferred(propName)) &&
1432 |               ((isExtern && !ownerType.isNativeObjectType()) ||
1433 |                !ownerType.isInstanceType())) {
1434 |             // If the property is undeclared or inferred, declare it now.
1435 |             ownerType.defineDeclaredProperty(propName, valueType, n);
1436 |           }
1437 |         }
1438 | 
1439 |         // If the property is already declared, the error will be
1440 |         // caught when we try to declare it in the current scope.
1441 |         defineSlot(n, parent, valueType, inferred);
1442 |       } else if (rhsValue != null &&
1443 |           rhsValue.getType() == Token.TRUE) {
1444 |         // We declare these for delegate proxy method properties.
1445 |         ObjectType ownerType = getObjectSlot(ownerName);
1446 |         if (ownerType instanceof FunctionType) {
1447 |           JSType ownerTypeOfThis = ((FunctionType) ownerType).getTypeOfThis();
1448 |           String delegateName = codingConvention.getDelegateSuperclassName();
1449 |           JSType delegateType = delegateName == null ?
1450 |               null : typeRegistry.getType(delegateName);
1451 |           if (delegateType != null &&
1452 |               ownerTypeOfThis.isSubtype(delegateType)) {
1453 |             defineSlot(n, parent, getNativeType(BOOLEAN_TYPE),
1454 |                 true);
1455 |           }
1456 |         }
1457 |       }
1458 |     }

===== M1292 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 150-195
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
150 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
151 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
152 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
153 |       case Token.BLOCK:
154 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
155 |       case Token.TRY:
156 |       case Token.FINALLY:
157 |         return true;
158 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
159 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
160 |         // is bleed into the local scope and parameters has been assigned
161 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
162 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
163 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
164 |         // control is going into the function's body represent by the second
165 |         // child.
166 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
167 |       case Token.WHILE:
168 |       case Token.DO:
169 |       case Token.IF:
170 |         // Theses control structure is represented by its node that holds the
171 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
172 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
173 | 
174 |       case Token.FOR:
175 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structure in that
176 |         // it has a initialization and a increment statement. Those
177 |         // two statements have its corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
178 |         // The FOR node represents the condition check for each iteration.
179 |         // That way the following:
180 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
181 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
182 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
183 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
184 |         } else {
185 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
186 |         }
187 |       case Token.SWITCH:
188 |       case Token.CASE:
189 |       case Token.CATCH:
190 |       case Token.WITH:
191 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
192 |       default:
193 |         return false;
194 |     }
195 |   }

===== M1295 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Denormalize.maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Denormalize.java
Original range: 65-127
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(n) && !NodeUtil.isVar(n)) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling == null) {
80 |       return;
81 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)) {
82 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
83 |       Node forVar = forNode.getFirstChild();
84 |       if (NodeUtil.isName(forVar)
85 |           && NodeUtil.isVar(n) && n.hasOneChild()) {
86 |         Node name = n.getFirstChild();
87 |         if (!name.hasChildren()
88 |             && forVar.getString().equals(name.getString())) {
89 |           // Ok, the names match, and the var declaration does not have an
90 |           // initializer. Move it into the loop.
91 |           parent.removeChild(n);
92 |           forNode.replaceChild(forVar, n);
93 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |         }
95 |       }
96 |     } else if (nextSibling.getType() == Token.FOR
97 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.EMPTY) {
98 | 
99 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
100 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some Javascript parsers (such
101 |       // as the Playstation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
102 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
103 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
104 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
105 |         return;
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
109 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
110 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
111 |       parent.removeChild(n);
112 | 
113 |       Node newInitializer;
114 |       if (NodeUtil.isVar(n)) {
115 |         newInitializer = n;
116 |       } else {
117 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
118 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
119 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
120 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
124 | 
125 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
126 |     }
127 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.isSubtype(JSType,JSType)

/**
   * A generic implementation meant to be used as a helper for common subtyping
   * cases.
   */
Method code:
902 |   static boolean isSubtype(JSType thisType, JSType thatType) {
903 |     // unknown
904 |     if (thatType.isUnknownType()) {
905 |       return true;
906 |     }
907 |     // equality
908 |     if (thisType.isEquivalentTo(thatType)) {
909 |       return true;
910 |     }
911 |     // all type
912 |     if (thatType.isAllType()) {
913 |       return true;
914 |     }
915 |     // unions
916 |     if (thatType instanceof UnionType) {
917 |       UnionType union = (UnionType)thatType;
918 |       for (JSType element : union.alternates) {
919 |         if (thisType.isSubtype(element)) {
920 |           return true;
921 |         }
922 |       }
923 |     }
924 |     // named types
925 |     if (thatType instanceof NamedType) {
926 |       return thisType.isSubtype(((NamedType)thatType).getReferencedType());
927 |     }
928 |     return false;
929 |   }

175 |     @Override
176 |     public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
177 |       Scope s = t.getScope();
178 |       if (!s.isLocal()) {
179 |         return;
180 |       }
181 | 
182 |       // Since we don't shadow global, there is nothing to be done in the
183 |       // first immediate local scope as well.
184 |       if (s.getParent().isGlobal()) {
185 |         return;
186 |       }
187 | 
188 |       for (Iterator<Var> vars = s.getVars(); vars.hasNext();) {
189 |         Var var = vars.next();
190 | 
191 |         // Don't shadow variables that is bleed-out to fix an IE bug.
192 |         if (var.isBleedingFunction()) {
193 |           continue;
194 |         }
195 | 
196 |         // Don't shadow an exported local.
197 |         if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.name, s.isLocal())) {
198 |           continue;
199 |         }
200 | 
201 |         // Try to look for the best shadow for the current candidate.
202 |         Assignment bestShadow = findBestShadow(s, var);
203 |         if (bestShadow == null) {
204 |           continue;
205 |         }
206 | 
207 |         // The name assignment being shadowed.
208 |         Assignment localAssignment = assignments.get(var.getName());
209 | 
210 |         // Only shadow if this increases the number of occurrences of the
211 |         // shadowed variable.
212 |         if (bestShadow.count < localAssignment.count) {
213 |           continue; // Hope the next local variable would have a smaller count.
214 |         }
215 | 
216 |         doShadow(localAssignment, bestShadow, var);
217 | 
218 |         if (oldPseudoNameMap != null) {
219 |           String targetPseudoName =
220 |             oldPseudoNameMap.get(s.getVar(bestShadow.oldName).nameNode);
221 |           for (Node use : varToNameUsage.get(var)) {
222 |             deltaPseudoNameMap.put(use, targetPseudoName);
223 |           }
224 |         }
225 |       }
226 |     }

214 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {

217 |       }

220 |

222 |       if (name.length() == 0) {

232 |           (!var.scope.getParent().isGlobal() ||

245 |         return;

249 |       if (!okToRenameVar(name, local)) {
250 |         if (local) {
251 |           // Blindly de-uniquify for the Prototype library for issue 103.
252 |           String newName = MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.ContextualRenameInverter

258 |         return;
259 |       }
260 |

262 |         // Keep track of extern globals.
263 |         if (!local) {

265 |         }
266 |         return;

271 |       }

276 |         incCount(tempName);

/**
   * Infer the parameter and return types of a function from
   * the parameter and return types of the function it is overriding.
   *
   * @param oldType The function being overridden. Does nothing if this is null.
   * @param paramsParent The LP node of the function that we're assigning to.
   *     If null, that just means we're not initializing this to a function
   *     literal.
   */
Method code:
239 |   FunctionTypeBuilder inferFromOverriddenFunction(
240 |       @Nullable FunctionType oldType, @Nullable Node paramsParent) {
241 |     if (oldType == null) {
242 |       return this;
243 |     }
244 | 
245 |     returnType = oldType.getReturnType();
246 |     returnTypeInferred = oldType.isReturnTypeInferred();
247 |     if (paramsParent == null) {
248 |       // Not a function literal.
249 |       parametersNode = oldType.getParametersNode();
250 |       if (parametersNode == null) {
251 |         parametersNode = new FunctionParamBuilder(typeRegistry).build();
252 |       }
253 |     } else {
254 |       // We're overriding with a function literal. Apply type information
255 |       // to each parameter of the literal.
256 |       FunctionParamBuilder paramBuilder =
257 |           new FunctionParamBuilder(typeRegistry);
258 |       Iterator<Node> oldParams = oldType.getParameters().iterator();
259 |       boolean warnedAboutArgList = false;
260 |       boolean oldParamsListHitOptArgs = false;
261 |       for (Node currentParam = paramsParent.getFirstChild();
262 |            currentParam != null; currentParam = currentParam.getNext()) {
263 |         if (oldParams.hasNext()) {
264 |           Node oldParam = oldParams.next();
265 |           Node newParam = paramBuilder.newParameterFromNode(oldParam);
266 | 
267 |           oldParamsListHitOptArgs = oldParamsListHitOptArgs ||
268 |               oldParam.isVarArgs() ||
269 |               oldParam.isOptionalArg();
270 | 
271 |           // The subclass method might right its var_args as individual
272 |           // arguments.
273 |           if (currentParam.getNext() != null && newParam.isVarArgs()) {
274 |             newParam.setVarArgs(false);
275 |             newParam.setOptionalArg(true);
276 |           }
277 |         } else {
278 |           warnedAboutArgList |= addParameter(
279 |               paramBuilder,
280 |               typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE),
281 |               warnedAboutArgList,
282 |               codingConvention.isOptionalParameter(currentParam) ||
283 |                   oldParamsListHitOptArgs,
284 |               codingConvention.isVarArgsParameter(currentParam));
285 |         }
286 |       }
287 |       parametersNode = paramBuilder.build();
288 |     }
289 |     return this;

===== M1382 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue(Node,Predicate<Node>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 2919-2983
Documentation:
/**
   * @param locals A predicate to apply to unknown local values.
   * @return Whether the node is known to be a value that is not a reference
   *     outside the expression scope.
   */
Method code:
2919 |   static boolean evaluatesToLocalValue(Node value, Predicate<Node> locals) {
2920 |     switch (value.getType()) {
2921 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
2922 |         // A result that is aliased by a non-local name, is the effectively the
2923 |         // same as returning a non-local name, but this doesn't matter if the
2924 |         // value is immutable.
2925 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value.getLastChild())
2926 |             || (locals.apply(value)
2927 |                 && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals));
2928 |       case Token.COMMA:
2929 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2930 |       case Token.AND:
2931 |       case Token.OR:
2932 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals)
2933 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2934 |       case Token.HOOK:
2935 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild().getNext(), locals)
2936 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2937 |       case Token.INC:
2938 |       case Token.DEC:
2939 |         if (value.getBooleanProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP)) {
2940 |           return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals);
2941 |         } else {
2942 |           return true;
2943 |         }
2944 |       case Token.THIS:
2945 |         return locals.apply(value);
2946 |       case Token.NAME:
2947 |         return isImmutableValue(value) || locals.apply(value);
2948 |       case Token.GETELEM:
2949 |       case Token.GETPROP:
2950 |         // There is no information about the locality of object properties.
2951 |         return locals.apply(value);
2952 |       case Token.CALL:
2953 |         return callHasLocalResult(value)
2954 |             || isToStringMethodCall(value)
2955 |             || locals.apply(value);
2956 |       case Token.NEW:
2957 |         return newHasLocalResult(value)
2958 |                || locals.apply(value);
2959 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
2960 |       case Token.REGEXP:
2961 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
2962 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
2963 |         // Literals objects with non-literal children are allowed.
2964 |         return true;
2965 |       case Token.DELPROP:
2966 |       case Token.IN:
2967 |         // TODO(johnlenz): should IN operator be included in #isSimpleOperator?
2968 |         return true;
2969 |       default:
2970 |         // Other op force a local value:
2971 |         //  x = '' + g (x is now an local string)
2972 |         //  x -= g (x is now an local number)
2973 |         if (isAssignmentOp(value)
2974 |             || isSimpleOperator(value)
2975 |             || isImmutableValue(value)) {
2976 |           return true;
2977 |         }
2978 | 
2979 |         throw new IllegalStateException(
2980 |             "Unexpected expression node" + value +
2981 |             "\n parent:" + value.getParent());
2982 |     }
2983 |   }

===== M1407 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 148-190
Documentation:

Method code:
148 |   @Override
149 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
150 |     this.root = root;
151 |     astPositionCounter = 0;
152 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();
153 |     nodePriorities = Maps.newHashMap();
154 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities,
155 |                                   edgeAnnotations);
156 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 | 
159 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
160 |     // search on the CFG.
161 |     priorityCounter = 0;
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
163 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);
164 | 
165 |     if (shouldTraverseFunctions) {
166 |       // If we're traversing inner functions, we need to rank the
167 |       // priority of them too.
168 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
169 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();
170 |         if (value != null && value.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
171 |           Preconditions.checkState(
172 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
173 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);
174 |         }
175 |       }
176 |     }
177 | 
178 |     // At this point, all reachable nodes have been given a priority, but
179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
180 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }
186 |     }
187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
190 |   }

===== M1421 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1632-1671
Documentation:
/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1632 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1633 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1634 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1635 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1636 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1637 |       // {?} - right curly
1638 |       // {?=} - equals
1639 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1640 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1641 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1642 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1643 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1644 |       token = next();
1645 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1646 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1647 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1648 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1649 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE) {
1650 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1651 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1652 |       }
1653 | 
1654 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1655 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1656 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1657 |     } else {
1658 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1659 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1660 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1661 |           next();
1662 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1663 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1664 |           next();
1665 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1666 |         }
1667 |       }
1668 | 
1669 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1670 |     }
1671 |   }

128 |     private boolean isVarInlineForbidden(Var var) {

/**
   * Merges the line number and character number in one integer. The Character
   * number takes the first 12 bits and the line number takes the rest. If
   * the character number is greater than <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code> it is

362 |     private void optimizePasses() {
363 |       // It's important that this ordering is deterministic, so that
364 |       // multiple compiles with the same input produce exactly the same
365 |       // results.

373 |             optimalPasses.add(pass);
374 |             break;
375 |           }
376 |         }
377 |       }
378 | 
379 |       myPasses.removeAll(optimalPasses);
380 |       myPasses.addAll(optimalPasses);
