Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/AbstractCommandLineRunner.java
Original range: 1075-1134
Documentation:
/**
   * Create a map of constant names to constant values from a textual
   * description of the map.
   *
   * @param definitions A list of overriding definitions for defines in
   *     the form <name>[=<val>], where <val> is a number, boolean, or
   *     single-quoted string without single quotes.
   */
Method code:
1075 |   @VisibleForTesting
1076 |   static void createDefineOrTweakReplacements(List<String> definitions,
1077 |       CompilerOptions options, boolean tweaks) {
1078 |     // Parse the definitions
1079 |     for (String override : definitions) {
1080 |       String[] assignment = override.split("=", 2);
1081 |       String defName = assignment[0];
1082 | 
1083 |       if (defName.length() > 0) {
1084 |         String defValue = assignment.length == 1 ? "true" : assignment[1];
1085 | 
1086 |         boolean isTrue = defValue.equals("true");
1087 |         boolean isFalse = defValue.equals("false");
1088 |         if (isTrue || isFalse) {
1089 |           if (tweaks) {
1090 |             options.setTweakToBooleanLiteral(defName, isTrue);
1091 |           } else {
1092 |             options.setDefineToBooleanLiteral(defName, isTrue);
1093 |           }
1094 |           continue;
1095 |         } else if (defValue.length() > 1
1096 |             && ((defValue.charAt(0) == '\'' &&
1097 |                 defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\'')
1098 |                 || (defValue.charAt(0) == '\"' &&
1099 |                     defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\"'))) {
1100 |           // If the value starts and ends with a single quote,
1101 |           // we assume that it's a string.
1102 |           String maybeStringVal =
1103 |               defValue.substring(1, defValue.length() - 1);
1104 |           if (maybeStringVal.indexOf(defValue.charAt(0)) == -1) {
1105 |             if (tweaks) {
1106 |               options.setTweakToStringLiteral(defName, maybeStringVal);
1107 |             } else {
1108 |               options.setDefineToStringLiteral(defName, maybeStringVal);
1109 |             }
1110 |             continue;
1111 |           }
1112 |         } else {
1113 |           try {
1114 |             double value = Double.parseDouble(defValue);
1115 |             if (tweaks) {
1116 |               options.setTweakToDoubleLiteral(defName, value);
1117 |             } else {
1118 |               options.setDefineToDoubleLiteral(defName, value);
1119 |             }
1120 |             continue;
1121 |           } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
1122 |             // do nothing, it will be caught at the end
1123 |           }
1124 |         }
1125 |       }
1126 | 
1127 |       if (tweaks) {
1128 |         throw new RuntimeException(
1129 |             "--tweak flag syntax invalid: " + override);
1130 |       }
1131 |       throw new RuntimeException(
1132 |           "--define flag syntax invalid: " + override);
1133 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.UnionTypeBuilder.addAlternate(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/UnionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 95-156
Documentation:
/**
   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
95 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
96 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
97 |     // just bail out early here.
98 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
99 |       return this;
100 |     }
101 | 
102 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
103 | 
104 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
105 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
106 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
107 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
108 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
109 |     }
110 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
111 |       if (alternate instanceof UnionType) {
112 |         UnionType union = (UnionType) alternate;
113 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
114 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
115 |         }
116 |       } else {
117 |         if (alternates.size() > MAX_UNION_SIZE) {
118 |           return this;
119 |         }
120 | 
121 |         // Look through the alternates we've got so far,
122 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
123 |         // one another.
124 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
125 |         while (it.hasNext()) {
126 |           JSType current = it.next();
127 | 
128 |           // Unknown and NoResolved types may just be names that haven't
129 |           // been resolved yet. So keep these in the union, and just use
130 |           // equality checking for simple de-duping.
131 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
132 |               current.isUnknownType() ||
133 |               alternate.isNoResolvedType() ||
134 |               current.isNoResolvedType()) {
135 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
136 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
137 |               return this;
138 |             }
139 |           } else {
140 |             if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
141 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
142 |               return this;
143 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
144 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
145 |               it.remove();
146 |             }
147 |           }
148 |         }
149 |         alternates.add(alternate);
150 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
151 |       }
152 |     } else {
153 |       result = null;
154 |     }
155 |     return this;
156 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseParamTypeExpressionAnnotation(JsDocToken)

/**
   * ParamTypeExpressionAnnotation :=
   *     '{' OptionalParameterType '}' |
   *     '{' TopLevelTypeExpression '}' |
   *     '{' '...' TopLevelTypeExpression '}'
   *
   * OptionalParameterType :=
   *     TopLevelTypeExpression '='
   */
Method code:
1518 |   private Node parseParamTypeExpressionAnnotation(JsDocToken token) {
1519 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(token == JsDocToken.LC);
1520 | 
1521 |     skipEOLs();
1522 | 
1523 |     boolean restArg = false;
1524 |     token = next();
1525 |     if (token == JsDocToken.ELLIPSIS) {
1526 |       token = next();
1527 |       if (token == JsDocToken.RC) {
1528 |         // EMPTY represents the UNKNOWN type in the Type AST.
1529 |         return wrapNode(Token.ELLIPSIS, new Node(Token.EMPTY));
1530 |       }
1531 |       restArg = true;
1532 |     }
1533 | 
1534 |     Node typeNode = parseTopLevelTypeExpression(token);
1535 |     if (typeNode != null) {
1536 |       skipEOLs();
1537 |       if (restArg) {
1538 |         typeNode = wrapNode(Token.ELLIPSIS, typeNode);
1539 |       } else if (match(JsDocToken.EQUALS)) {
1540 |         next();
1541 |         skipEOLs();
1542 |         typeNode = wrapNode(Token.EQUALS, typeNode);
1543 |       }
1544 | 
1545 |       if (!match(JsDocToken.RC)) {
1546 |         reportTypeSyntaxWarning("msg.jsdoc.missing.rc");
1547 |       } else {
1548 |         next();
1549 |       }
1550 |     }
1551 | 
1552 |     return typeNode;
1553 |   }

/**
   * Removes unreferenced arguments from a function declaration and when
   * possible the function's callSites.
   *
   * @param fnScope The scope inside the function
   */
Method code:
358 |   private void removeUnreferencedFunctionArgs(Scope fnScope) {
359 |     // TODO(johnlenz): Update type registry for function signature changes.
360 | 
361 |     Node function = fnScope.getRootNode();
362 | 
363 |     Preconditions.checkState(function.getType() == Token.FUNCTION);
364 |     if (NodeUtil.isGetOrSetKey(function.getParent())) {
365 |       // The parameters object literal setters can not be removed.
366 |       return;
367 |     }
368 |

370 |     boolean modifyCallers = modifyCallSites
371 |         && callSiteOptimizer.canModifyCallers(function);
372 |     if (!modifyCallers) {
373 |       // Strip unreferenced args off the end of the function declaration.
374 |       Node lastArg;
375 |       while ((lastArg = argList.getLastChild()) != null) {
376 |         Var var = fnScope.getVar(lastArg.getString());
377 |         if (!referenced.contains(var)) {
378 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(var == null);
379 |           argList.removeChild(lastArg);
380 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
381 |         } else {
382 |           break;
383 |         }
384 |       }
385 |     } else {
386 |       callSiteOptimizer.optimize(fnScope, referenced);
387 |     }
388 |   }

   * Use "return x?1:2;" in place of "if(x)return 1;return 2;"

===== M1521 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 169-279
Documentation:
/**
   * General cascading unused operation node removal.
   * @param n The root of the expression to simplify.
   * @param removeUnused If true, the node is removed from the AST if
   *     it is not useful, otherwise it replaced with an EMPTY node.
   * @return The replacement node, or null if the node was is not useful.
   */
Method code:
169 |   private Node trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node n, boolean removeUnused) {
170 |     Node result = n;
171 | 
172 |     // Simplify the results of conditional expressions
173 |     switch (n.getType()) {
174 |       case Token.HOOK:
175 |         Node trueNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild().getNext());
176 |         Node falseNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
177 |         // If one or more of the conditional children were removed,
178 |         // transform the HOOK to an equivalent operation:
179 |         //    x() ? foo() : 1 --> x() && foo()
180 |         //    x() ? 1 : foo() --> x() || foo()
181 |         //    x() ? 1 : 1 --> x()
182 |         //    x ? 1 : 1 --> null
183 |         if (trueNode == null && falseNode != null) {
184 |           n.setType(Token.OR);
185 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
186 |         } else if (trueNode != null && falseNode == null) {
187 |           n.setType(Token.AND);
188 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
189 |         } else if (trueNode == null && falseNode == null) {
190 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
191 |         } else {
192 |           // The structure didn't change.
193 |           result = n;
194 |         }
195 |         break;
196 |       case Token.AND:
197 |       case Token.OR:
198 |         // Try to remove the second operand from a AND or OR operations:
199 |         //    x() || f --> x()
200 |         //    x() && f --> x()
201 |         Node conditionalResultNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(
202 |             n.getLastChild());
203 |         if (conditionalResultNode == null) {
204 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
205 |           // The conditionally executed code was removed, so
206 |           // replace the AND/OR with its LHS or remove it if it isn't useful.
207 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
208 |         }
209 |         break;
210 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
211 |         // A function expression isn't useful if it isn't used, remove it and
212 |         // don't bother to look at its children.
213 |         result = null;
214 |         break;
215 |       case Token.COMMA:
216 |         // We rewrite other operations as COMMA expressions (which will later
217 |         // get split into individual EXPR_RESULT statement, if possible), so
218 |         // we special case COMMA (we don't want to rewrite COMMAs as new COMMAs
219 |         // nodes.
220 |         Node left = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
221 |         Node right = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
222 |         if (left == null && right == null) {
223 |           result = null;
224 |         } else if (left == null) {
225 |           result = right;
226 |         } else if (right == null){
227 |           result = left;
228 |         } else {
229 |           // The structure didn't change.
230 |           result = n;
231 |         }
232 |         break;
233 |       default:
234 |         if (!NodeUtil.nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
235 |           // This is the meat of this function. The node itself doesn't generate
236 |           // any side-effects but preserve any side-effects in the children.
237 |           Node resultList = null;
238 |           for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
239 |             next = c.getNext();
240 |             c = trySimplifyUnusedResult(c);
241 |             if (c != null) {
242 |               c.detachFromParent();
243 |               if (resultList == null)  {
244 |                 // The first side-effect can be used stand-alone.
245 |                 resultList = c;
246 |               } else {
247 |                 // Leave the side-effects in-place, simplifying it to a COMMA
248 |                 // expression.
249 |                 resultList = new Node(Token.COMMA, resultList, c)
250 |                     .copyInformationFrom(c);
251 |               }
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 |           result = resultList;
255 |         }
256 |     }
257 | 
258 |     // Fix up the AST, replace or remove the an unused node (if requested).
259 |     if (n != result) {
260 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
261 |       if (result == null) {
262 |         if (removeUnused) {
263 |           parent.removeChild(n);
264 |         } else {
265 |           result = new Node(Token.EMPTY).copyInformationFrom(n);
266 |           parent.replaceChild(n, result);
267 |         }
268 |       } else {
269 |         // A new COMMA expression may not have an existing parent.
270 |         if (result.getParent() != null) {
271 |           result.detachFromParent();
272 |         }
273 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, result);
274 |       }
275 |       reportCodeChange();
276 |     }
277 | 
278 |     return result;
279 |   }

199 |   private UndiGraph<Var, Void> computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(

215 |         // around with it.
216 |         if (!NodeUtil.isFunction(v.getParentNode())) {
217 |           interferenceGraph.createNode(v);
218 |         }
219 |       }
220 |     }
221 | 
222 |     // Go through each variable and try to connect them.
223 |     for (Iterator<Var> i1 = scope.getVars(); i1.hasNext();) {
224 |       Var v1 = i1.next();
225 | 
226 |       NEXT_VAR_PAIR:
227 |       for (Iterator<Var> i2 = scope.getVars(); i2.hasNext();) {
228 |         Var v2 = i2.next();
229 | 
230 |         // Skip duplicate pairs.
231 |         if (v1.index >= v2.index) {
232 |           continue;
233 |         }
234 | 
235 |         if (!interferenceGraph.hasNode(v1) ||
236 |             !interferenceGraph.hasNode(v2)) {
237 |           // Skip nodes that were not added. They are globals and escaped
238 |           // locals. Also avoid merging a variable with itself.
239 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
240 |         }
241 | 
242 |         if (v1.getParentNode().getType() == Token.LP &&
243 |             v2.getParentNode().getType() == Token.LP) {
244 |           interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
245 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
246 |         }
247 | 
248 |         // Go through every CFG node in the program and look at
249 |         // this variable pair. If they are both live at the same
250 |         // time, add an edge between them and continue to the next pair.
251 |         NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE:
252 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
253 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
254 |             continue NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE;
255 |           }
256 | 
257 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
258 |           // Check the live states and add edge when possible.
259 |           if ((state.getIn().isLive(v1) && state.getIn().isLive(v2)) ||
260 |               (state.getOut().isLive(v1) && state.getOut().isLive(v2))) {
261 |             interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
262 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
263 |           }
264 |         }
265 | 
266 |         // v1 and v2 might not have an edge between them! woohoo. there's
267 |         // one last sanity check that we have to do: we have to check
268 |         // if there's a collision *within* the cfg node.
269 |         NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE:
270 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
271 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
272 |             continue NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE;
273 |           }
274 | 
275 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
276 |           boolean v1OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v1);
277 |           boolean v2OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v2);
278 |           CombinedLiveRangeChecker checker = new CombinedLiveRangeChecker(
279 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v1, v2OutLive ? null : v2),
280 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v2, v1OutLive ? null : v1));
281 |           NodeTraversal.traverse(
282 |               compiler,
283 |               cfgNode.getValue(),
284 |               checker);
285 |           if (checker.connectIfCrossed(interferenceGraph)) {
286 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
287 |           }
288 |         }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return interferenceGraph;
292 |   }

/**
   * Expect that the given variable has not been declared with a type.
   *
   * @param sourceName The name of the source file we're in.
   * @param n The node where warnings should point to.
   * @param parent The parent of {@code n}.
   * @param var The variable that we're checking.

   * @param newType The type being applied to the variable. Mostly just here
   *     for the benefit of the warning.

Method code:
509 |   void expectUndeclaredVariable(String sourceName, Node n, Node parent, Var var,
510 |       String variableName, JSType newType) {
511 |     boolean allowDupe = false;
512 |     if (n.getType() == Token.GETPROP ||
513 |         NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
514 |       JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
515 |       if (info == null) {
516 |         info = parent.getJSDocInfo();

520 |     }

526 |     // compilation process.

528 |         varType != typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE) &&
529 |         newType != null &&
530 |         newType != typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE)) {
531 |       // If there are two typed declarations of the same variable, that
532 |       // is an error and the second declaration is ignored, except in the
533 |       // case of native types. A null input type means that the declaration
534 |       // was made in TypedScopeCreator#createInitialScope and is a
535 |       // native type.

538 |         if (parent.getType() == Token.VAR) {

544 |           parent.setJSType(varType);
545 |         }
546 |       } else {
547 |         // Always warn about duplicates if the overridden type does not
548 |         // match the original type.
549 |         //
550 |         // If the types match, suppress the warning iff there was a @suppress
551 |         // tag, or if the original declaration was a stub.

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 732-875
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
732 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
733 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects, AbstractCompiler compiler) {
734 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
735 |     // that we know to be safe
736 |     switch (n.getType()) {
737 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
738 |       case Token.AND:
739 |       case Token.BLOCK:
740 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
741 |       case Token.HOOK:
742 |       case Token.IF:
743 |       case Token.IN:
744 |       case Token.LP:
745 |       case Token.NUMBER:
746 |       case Token.OR:
747 |       case Token.THIS:
748 |       case Token.TRUE:
749 |       case Token.FALSE:
750 |       case Token.NULL:
751 |       case Token.STRING:
752 |       case Token.SWITCH:
753 |       case Token.TRY:
754 |       case Token.EMPTY:
755 |         break;
756 | 
757 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
758 |       case Token.THROW:
759 |         return true;
760 | 
761 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
762 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
763 |           return true;
764 |         }
765 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
766 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
767 |                   c.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
768 |             return true;
769 |           }
770 |         }
771 |         return false;
772 | 
773 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
774 |       case Token.REGEXP:
775 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
776 |           return true;
777 |         }
778 |         break;
779 | 
780 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
781 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
782 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
783 |           return true;
784 |         }
785 |         break;
786 | 
787 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
788 |         // Function expressions don't have side-effects, but function
789 |         // declarations change the namespace. Either way, we don't need to
790 |         // check the children, since they aren't executed at declaration time.
791 |         return checkForNewObjects || !isFunctionExpression(n);
792 | 
793 |       case Token.NEW:
794 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
795 |           return true;
796 |         }
797 | 
798 |         if (!constructorCallHasSideEffects(n)) {
799 |           // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
800 |           // side-effects
801 |           break;
802 |         }
803 |         return true;
804 | 
805 |       case Token.CALL:
806 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
807 |         // side effect property set.
808 |         if (!functionCallHasSideEffects(n, compiler)) {
809 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
810 |           // side-effects
811 |           break;
812 |         }
813 |         return true;
814 | 
815 |       default:
816 |         if (isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType())) {
817 |           break;
818 |         }
819 | 
820 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
821 |           Node assignTarget = n.getFirstChild();
822 |           if (isName(assignTarget)) {
823 |             return true;
824 |           }
825 | 
826 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
827 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
828 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
829 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
830 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
831 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler) ||
832 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
833 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
834 |             return true;
835 |           }
836 | 
837 |           if (isGet(assignTarget)) {
838 |             // If the object being assigned to is a local object, don't
839 |             // consider this a side-effect as it can't be referenced
840 |             // elsewhere.  Don't do this recursively as the property might
841 |             // be an alias of another object, unlike a literal below.
842 |             Node current = assignTarget.getFirstChild();
843 |             if (evaluatesToLocalValue(current)) {
844 |               return false;
845 |             }
846 | 
847 |             // A literal value as defined by "isLiteralValue" is guaranteed
848 |             // not to be an alias, or any components which are aliases of
849 |             // other objects.
850 |             // If the root object is a literal don't consider this a
851 |             // side-effect.
852 |             while (isGet(current)) {
853 |               current = current.getFirstChild();
854 |             }
855 | 
856 |             return !isLiteralValue(current, true);
857 |           } else {
858 |             // TODO(johnlenz): remove this code and make this an exception. This
859 |             // is here only for legacy reasons, the AST is not valid but
860 |             // preserve existing behavior.
861 |             return !isLiteralValue(assignTarget, true);
862 |           }
863 |         }
864 | 
865 |         return true;
866 |     }
867 | 
868 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
869 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
870 |         return true;
871 |       }
872 |     }
873 | 
874 |     return false;
875 |   }

/**
   * Infers the type of {@code this}.
   * @param info The JSDocInfo for this function.
   * @param owner The node for the object whose prototype "owns" this function.
   *     For example, {@code A} in the expression {@code A.prototype.foo}. May
   *     be null to indicate that this is not a prototype property.

423 |   FunctionTypeBuilder inferThisType(JSDocInfo info,
424 |       @Nullable Node owner) {
425 |     ObjectType maybeThisType = null;
426 |     if (info != null && info.hasThisType()) {

/**
   * Visits a NAME node.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal object that supplies context, such as the
   * scope chain to use in name lookups as well as error reporting.
   * @param n The node being visited.
   * @param parent The parent of the node n.
   * @return whether the node is typeable or not
   */
Method code:
1219 |   boolean visitName(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
1220 |     // At this stage, we need to determine whether this is a leaf
1221 |     // node in an expression (which therefore needs to have a type
1222 |     // assigned for it) versus some other decorative node that we
1223 |     // can safely ignore.  Function names, arguments (children of LP nodes) and
1224 |     // variable declarations are ignored.
1225 |     // TODO(user): remove this short-circuiting in favor of a
1226 |     // pre order traversal of the FUNCTION, CATCH, LP and VAR nodes.

1229 |         parentNodeType == Token.CATCH ||
1230 |         parentNodeType == Token.LP ||
1231 |         parentNodeType == Token.VAR) {
1232 |       return false;
1233 |     }
1234 |

1236 |     if (type == null) {
1237 |       type = getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);

1239 |       if (var != null) {
1240 |         JSType varType = var.getType();
1241 |         if (varType != null) {

1243 |         }
1244 |       }
1245 |     }
1246 |     ensureTyped(t, n, type);
1247 |     return true;
1248 |   }

   * Determines if n matches the type and name for the following types of
   * "exits":
   *    - return without values
   *    - continues and breaks with or without names.
   * @param n The node to inspect.
   * @param type The Token type to look for.

   * @return Whether the node matches the specified block-exit type.

Method code:

   */

565 |   static void writeOutput(Appendable out, Compiler compiler, String code,

114 |   public void exitScope(NodeTraversal traversal) {

117 |     // This is the case when we are exiting the global scope where we had never
118 |     // collected argument access list. Since we do not perform this optimization
119 |     // for the global scope, we will skip this exit point.

132 |     // current scope anymore. We'll pop the access list from the outer scope
133 |     // and set it as currentArgumentsAcess if the outer scope is not the global
134 |     // scope.

===== M1661 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 530-568
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if this is a literal value. We define a literal value
   * as any node that evaluates to the same thing regardless of when or
   * where it is evaluated. So /xyz/ and [3, 5] are literals, but
   * the name a is not.
   *
   * Function literals do not meet this definition, because they
   * lexically capture variables. For example, if you have
   * <code>
   * function() { return a; }
   * </code>
   * If it is evaluated in a different scope, then it
   * captures a different variable. Even if the function did not read
   * any captured vairables directly, it would still fail this definition,
   * because it affects the lifecycle of variables in the enclosing scope.
   *
   * However, a function literal with respect to a particular scope is
   * a literal.
   *
   * @param includeFunctions If true, all function expressions will be
   *     treated as literals.
   */
Method code:
530 |   static boolean isLiteralValue(Node n, boolean includeFunctions) {
531 |     switch (n.getType()) {
532 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
533 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
534 |              child = child.getNext()) {
535 |           if (child.getType() != Token.EMPTY
536 |               && !isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
537 |             return false;
538 |           }
539 |         }
540 |         return true;
541 | 
542 |       case Token.REGEXP:
543 |         // Return true only if all children are const.
544 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
545 |              child = child.getNext()) {
546 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
547 |             return false;
548 |           }
549 |         }
550 |         return true;
551 | 
552 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
553 |         // Return true only if all values are const.
554 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
555 |              child = child.getNext()) {
556 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child.getFirstChild(), includeFunctions)) {
557 |             return false;
558 |           }
559 |         }
560 |         return true;
561 | 
562 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
563 |         return includeFunctions && !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n);
564 | 
565 |       default:
566 |         return isImmutableValue(n);
567 |     }
568 |   }

===== M1684 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.runCallable(Callable<T>,boolean,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 579-630
Documentation:

Method code:
579 |   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
580 |   static <T> T runCallable(
581 |       final Callable<T> callable, boolean useLargeStackThread, boolean trace) {
582 | 
583 |     // Under JRE 1.6, the jscompiler overflows the stack when running on some
584 |     // large or complex js code. Here we start a new thread with a larger
585 |     // stack in order to let the compiler do its thing, without having to
586 |     // increase the stack size for *every* thread (which is what -Xss does).
587 |     // Might want to add thread pool support for clients that compile a lot.
588 | 
589 |     final boolean dumpTraceReport = trace;
590 |     final Object[] result = new Object[1];
591 |     final Throwable[] exception = new Throwable[1];
592 |     Runnable runnable = new Runnable() {
593 |       public void run() {
594 |         try {
595 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
596 |             Tracer.initCurrentThreadTrace();
597 |           }
598 |           result[0] = callable.call();
599 |         } catch (Throwable e) {
600 |           exception[0] = e;
601 |         } finally {
602 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
603 |             Tracer.logAndClearCurrentThreadTrace();
604 |           }
605 |         }
606 |       }
607 |     };
608 | 
609 |     if (useLargeStackThread) {
610 |       Thread th = new Thread(null, runnable, "jscompiler", COMPILER_STACK_SIZE);
611 |       th.start();
612 |       while (true) {
613 |         try {
614 |           th.join();
615 |           break;
616 |         } catch (InterruptedException ignore) {
617 |           // ignore
618 |         }
619 |       }
620 |     } else {
621 |       runnable.run();
622 |     }
623 | 
624 |     // Pass on any exception caught by the runnable object.
625 |     if (exception[0] != null) {
626 |       throw new RuntimeException(exception[0]);
627 |     }
628 | 
629 |     return (T) result[0];
630 |   }

===== M1695 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.interpretAssigns()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 703-748
Documentation:
/**
   * Look at all the property assigns to all variables.
   * These may or may not count as references. For example,
   *
   * <code>
   * var x = {};
   * x.foo = 3; // not a reference.
   * var y = foo();
   * y.foo = 3; // is a reference.
   * </code>
   *
   * Interpreting assigments could mark a variable as referenced that
   * wasn't referenced before, in order to keep it alive. Because we find
   * references by lazily traversing subtrees, marking a variable as
   * referenced could trigger new traversals of new subtrees, which could
   * find new references.
   *
   * Therefore, this interpretation needs to be run to a fixed point.
   */
Method code:
703 |   private void interpretAssigns() {
704 |     boolean changes = false;
705 |     do {
706 |       changes = false;
707 | 
708 |       // We can't use traditional iterators and iterables for this list,
709 |       // because our lazily-evaluated continuations will modify it while
710 |       // we traverse it.
711 |       for (int current = 0; current < maybeUnreferenced.size(); current++) {
712 |         Var var = maybeUnreferenced.get(current);
713 |         if (referenced.contains(var)) {
714 |           maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
715 |           current--;
716 |         } else {
717 |           boolean assignedToUnknownValue = false;
718 |           boolean hasPropertyAssign = false;
719 | 
720 |           if (var.getParentNode().getType() == Token.VAR &&
721 |               !NodeUtil.isForIn(var.getParentNode().getParent())) {
722 |             Node value = var.getInitialValue();
723 |             assignedToUnknownValue = value != null &&
724 |                 !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(value, true);
725 |           } else {
726 |             // This was initialized to a function arg or a catch param
727 |             // or a for...in variable.
728 |             assignedToUnknownValue = true;
729 |           }
730 | 
731 |           for (Assign assign : assignsByVar.get(var)) {
732 |             if (assign.isPropertyAssign) {
733 |               hasPropertyAssign = true;
734 |             } else if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(
735 |                 assign.assignNode.getLastChild(), true)) {
736 |               assignedToUnknownValue = true;
737 |             }
738 |           }
739 | 
740 |           if (assignedToUnknownValue && hasPropertyAssign) {
741 |             changes = markReferencedVar(var) || changes;
742 |             maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
743 |             current--;
744 |           }
745 |         }
746 |       }
747 |     } while (changes);
748 |   }

   * Try to collapse the given assign into subsequent expressions.
   */
Method code:
46 |   private void collapseAssign(Node assign, Node expr,
47 |       Node exprParent) {
48 |     Node leftValue = assign.getFirstChild();
49 |     Node rightValue = leftValue.getNext();
50 |     if (isCollapsibleValue(leftValue, true) &&
51 |         collapseAssignEqualTo(expr, exprParent, leftValue)) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.ArrowType.hasEqualParameters(ArrowType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/ArrowType.java
Original range: 146-169
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if our parameter spec is equal to {@code that}'s parameter
   *     spec.
   */
Method code:
146 |   boolean hasEqualParameters(ArrowType that) {
147 |     Node thisParam = parameters.getFirstChild();
148 |     Node otherParam = that.parameters.getFirstChild();
149 |     while (thisParam != null && otherParam != null) {
150 |       JSType thisParamType = thisParam.getJSType();
151 |       JSType otherParamType = otherParam.getJSType();
152 |       if (thisParamType != null) {
153 |         // Both parameter lists give a type for this param, it should be equal
154 |         if (otherParamType != null &&
155 |             !thisParamType.isEquivalentTo(otherParamType)) {
156 |           return false;
157 |         }
158 |       } else {
159 |         if (otherParamType != null) {
160 |           return false;
161 |         }
162 |       }
163 |       thisParam = thisParam.getNext();
164 |       otherParam = otherParam.getNext();
165 |     }
166 |     // One of the parameters is null, so the types are only equal if both
167 |     // parameter lists are null (they are equal).
168 |     return thisParam == otherParam;
169 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypedScopeCreator.createScope(Node,Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypedScopeCreator.java
Original range: 178-222

/**
   * Creates a scope with all types declared. Declares newly discovered types
   * and type properties in the type registry.
   */
Method code:
178 |   @Override
179 |   public Scope createScope(Node root, Scope parent) {
180 |     // Constructing the global scope is very different than constructing
181 |     // inner scopes, because only global scopes can contain named classes that
182 |     // show up in the type registry.
183 |     Scope newScope = null;
184 |     AbstractScopeBuilder scopeBuilder = null;
185 |     if (parent == null) {
186 |       // Find all the classes in the global scope.
187 |       newScope = createInitialScope(root);
188 | 
189 |       GlobalScopeBuilder globalScopeBuilder = new GlobalScopeBuilder(newScope);
190 |       scopeBuilder = globalScopeBuilder;
191 |       NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, scopeBuilder);
192 |     } else {
193 |       newScope = new Scope(parent, root);
194 |       LocalScopeBuilder localScopeBuilder = new LocalScopeBuilder(newScope);
195 |       scopeBuilder = localScopeBuilder;
196 |       localScopeBuilder.build();
197 |     }
198 | 
199 |     scopeBuilder.resolveStubDeclarations();
200 |     scopeBuilder.resolveTypes();
201 | 
202 |     // Gather the properties in each function that we found in the
203 |     // global scope, if that function has a @this type that we can
204 |     // build properties on.
205 |     for (Node functionNode : scopeBuilder.nonExternFunctions) {
206 |       JSType type = functionNode.getJSType();
207 |       if (type != null && type instanceof FunctionType) {
208 |         FunctionType fnType = (FunctionType) type;
209 |         ObjectType fnThisType = fnType.getTypeOfThis();
210 |         if (!fnThisType.isUnknownType()) {
211 |           NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, functionNode.getLastChild(),
212 |               scopeBuilder.new CollectProperties(fnThisType));
213 |         }
214 |       }
215 |     }
216 | 
217 |     if (parent == null) {
218 |       codingConvention.defineDelegateProxyPrototypeProperties(
219 |           typeRegistry, newScope, delegateProxyPrototypes);
220 |     }
221 |     return newScope;
222 |   }
